songPlan.title: Uh Huh Window
songPlan.arrangement: Slow 72 BPM lo-fi hip-hop ballad in F minor with dusty drum breaks, warm electric piano, muted bass, vinyl crackle, soft tape-warp textures, and occasional restrained guitar harmonics. Tony enters immediately with smoky, connected, lightly slurred melodic phrases, intimate muttered “uh huh” and “yeah” responses, and a catchable sung refrain. Keep spacious rests between phrases without long empty instrumental passages; build subtly through added bass movement and drum texture, then sustain the final “me” 8–12 seconds before a single resolved Rhodes chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh huh, the room is low
Yeah, the streetlight paints the ceiling slow
Uh huh, I hear the radiator sigh
Yeah, one little train goes crawling by

[Verse 1]
I keep my hands around a cooling cup
Watching the blue light on the corner shop
The city talks in puddles and tires
A quiet wire, a small red fire
I do not need a grand parade
Just that soft old record somebody played
A bass line leaning through the wall
Like it knows my name, like it knows it all

[Refrain]
Uh huh, yeah
Let the minute take its time
Uh huh, yeah
Leave the hard day outside
Uh huh, yeah
No big answer tonight
Just a window, just a beat
Just the dark breathing light

[Verse 2]
There is a note I never sent
Folded up with the rent
It says I was tired of running fast
Trying to turn every shadow into a past
But the kettle clicks and the floorboard bends
And a far-off siren rounds the end
I let the little noises stay
They make a home out of the gray

[Refrain]
Uh huh, yeah
Let the minute take its time
Uh huh, yeah
Leave the hard day outside
Uh huh, yeah
No big answer tonight
Just a window, just a beat
Just the dark breathing light

[Bridge]
If morning comes with a heavy coat
I will meet it with a softer note
Not a promise carved in stone
Just a breath that says I am not alone
Uh huh, I can hear it clear
Yeah, the quiet has a rhythm here

[Verse 3]
The last bus hums below my floor
Its yellow square moves past the door
I think of faces, names, and rain
Of losing things and finding them again
The clock gives up its little fight
The room turns silver near the light
I close my eyes and let it be
A slow beat holding me

[Refrain]
Uh huh, yeah
Let the minute take its time
Uh huh, yeah
Leave the hard day outside
Uh huh, yeah
I can finally see
The window, the beat, the night
Making room for me

[Outro]
Uh huh, yeah, the night makes room for me
[End]

songPlan.title: Influence Criteria
songPlan.arrangement: Mid-tempo alternative rock with a muscular melodic bass line, overdriven guitars, live drums, restrained synth texture, and piano accents. Tony V8 delivers rough, smoky, connected phrasing with muttered bite in the verses and sustained, catchable melody in the choruses. Start tense and contained, build through the stack-ranking verse, drop to bass and drums for the bridge, then surge into a resolute final chorus. Keep vocals active through the closing four lines; sustain the final word around 8–12 seconds before the 335-second end, followed by one resolved E-minor-to-major final chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Badge flashes green at six-oh-five
Rain on the glass and the lobby alive
I built the thing, I shipped it clean
But nobody clapped in the weekly machine
My manager says, "You did the work"
Then pauses hard with a practiced smirk
"The numbers shine, but the story's thin
You have to show how you pull people in"

[Pre-Chorus]
I ask for a map, they hand me smoke
A leadership principle dressed as a joke

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Verse 2]
A document lands with a careful tone
Thirty days to prove I don't work alone
A PIP with boxes, amber and red
Every vague little signal inside my head
"Raise the bar," "earn trust," "think big"
I circle each phrase till the margins twitch
I ask what changed, they clear their throats
And speak in weather reports and notes

[Verse 3]
There is stack ranking under the floor
A polished bell above a trapdoor
We trade our wins in a narrow light
Trying to look indispensable, pleasant, bright
I helped her launch, he fixed my break
Now every favor has a shape to take
The spreadsheet hums with a private heat
And somebody's future loses a seat

[Chorus]
Tell me what Influence means
Is it a meeting, is it a scene?
Is it my name on somebody's slide?
Is it a room where the truth stays outside?
I made the river run on time
Still I'm below some invisible line
Tell me what Influence means
Before they measure me out of the team

[Bridge]
Forced social gatherings, Thursday night
Tiny name tags under brewery light
I hold a paper cup, rehearse a laugh
Make a network from the better half
Political schmoozing by the catered wall
Nodding at titles I cannot recall
They call it connection, they call it care
I call it breathing the conference air

[Verse 4]
I bring a plan to the skip-level call
Three sharp proposals, risks and all
He says, "Be louder in the room"
Like volume alone can make a garden bloom
I say, "Whose room? Which door? What proof?"
The silence gathers around the truth
Then somebody says, "Let's take this offline"
And the clock keeps chewing my borrowed time

[Breakdown]
I will not sell a borrowed face
Or turn my friends into a ladder's place
I can speak clear, I can build and bend
But I won't call a contest a friend

[Chorus]
Now I know what Influence means
A shadow moving behind the scenes
A handshake held a second too long
A careful smile where a doubt belongs
But I made the river run on time
And I won't disappear to fit their line
You can score me, sort me, close the screen
I am more than your Influence criteria

[Outro]
Keep your amber boxes, keep your chart
I kept the craft and I kept my heart
When the badge goes dark, when the hallway clears
I leave with my name intact this year
[End]

songPlan.title: Season of Geglash
songPlan.arrangement: A 126 BPM D-minor gothic rock satire with organ, synthesizer, violin, piano, harp, electric bass, distorted guitars, and live drums. The selected pinned Tony V8 voice delivers smoky, connected, mischievous melodic lines with muttered character asides, then opens into a catchable sung refrain. Start with sparse piano, harp, and organ; add a lively bass pocket and full band for the choruses; strip back under the bridge before a decisive final chorus. The final sustained word “all” lands about 10 seconds before the 150-second endpoint, followed by one resolved D-minor-to-major closing chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The old campfire flickers beneath a premium sky
A merchant sells a ladder rung for every time you die
He says, “Welcome, hero, claim your daily shard”
Then locks the town portal behind a battle pass card

[Verse 1]
There’s a wheel in Harrogath with a demon on the rim
One free little spin, then the odds go dark and dim
Gold-framed loot boxes rattle by the forge
A tiny chance at angel wings, a mountain-sized surcharge

[Pre-Chorus]
The clock in town keeps counting down
A red exclamation owns the crown

[Chorus]
Season of Geglash, swipe the rune and feed the flame
Buy a brighter graveyard, buy a louder name
Season of Geglash, every blessing has a price
The devil takes installments, the shop takes dice

[Verse 2]
Rent a mercenary banner, lease a charm for seven days
Skip the cave, boost the level, light the fireworks in haze
Guild halls sell priority, raids sell extra turns
The portal waits for patience while the glowing currency burns

[Bridge]
A pop-up priest says, “Come back, friend, your streak is almost gold”
I hear the old dark wilderness beneath the script they sold
No coin can buy the thunder, no token owns the night
I close the gilded window and walk toward the firelight

[Chorus]
Season of Geglash, keep your wheel and painted crown
I want the cold road upward, I want to earn my way down
Season of Geglash, let the false enchantments fall
The last true rune is freedom—no purchase after all

[Outro]
No purchase after all
[End]

songPlan.title: Season of Geglash Debt at the Altar
songPlan.arrangement: A 155-second dark baroque rock reinterpretation in D minor: a driving bass-and-drum pocket supports ominous organ, wiry violin figures, sparse harp glints, and electric guitar. Tony V7 delivers smoky, connected melodic lines with sly mutters and a catchable hook; pronounce the G in “Geglash” hard. Build from a taunting intro through tighter verses to a bitter final chorus, with the final sung syllable landing about 10 seconds before a single resolved final chord decays.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The old road burns by the golden gate
Geglash is waiting: “Why should heroes wait?”
Tap the red button, watch the altar flame
Pay for the shortcut, come back changed again

[Verse 1]
Buy a bundle of blessing dust, a ladder made of keys
Lease a halo for your mercenary’s knees
Stamina runs out at the crypt-side door
Free chest tomorrow, if you still want more
A loot-box lantern swings above the town
Each purple almost-win pulls the dead man down

[Pre-Chorus]
There’s a wheel in Tristram under candle smoke
Every losing spin is dressed up like a joke

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Season of Geglash
Spin for the treasure, make the jackpot flash
One more pull for a perfect class
The demons fall, but the store moves fast
Season of Geglash, don’t close that screen
A legendary promise in a glowing machine

[Verse 2]
The battle pass sells resurrection breath
Premium insurance after hardcore death
Rent a private vault, finance a rune
Pay the moon tax before the next blood moon
Daily contracts ring before the sun
Miss a little login and the season’s done
Geglash says, “The odds are honest, friend”
Then offers store credit you can never spend

[Bridge]
Founder’s access to a patch not born
Trade your tokens for a cosmetic storm
I came to kill a demon, walk the rain
Now every menu bell knows my name

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Season of Geglash
The fire is pretty and the numbers crash
I sold my sword for a perfect class
Then borrowed gold for another pass
Season of Geglash, the candles lean
My purse is empty, my debt grows green

[Outro]
Geglash keeps smiling at the altar’s flame
The lender owns my armor and my name
No coin, no home, no way to flee
The hungry machine still charges me
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The old road glows with a golden gate
Geglash is waiting, says, "Why should heroes wait?"
A little red button, a little bright flame
Put your coin in the altar, come back stronger again

[Verse 1]
Buy a bundle of blessing dust, buy a tower of keys
Buy a seven-day halo for your mercenary’s knees
The dungeon has a stamina meter, the gate has a fee
A chest can open free tomorrow, if tomorrow agrees

[Pre-Chorus]
There’s a wheel in Tristram turning under candle smoke
Every near miss flashes purple, every loss becomes a joke

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Season of Geglash
Spin for the treasure, make the jackpot flash
One more pull for a perfect class
The demons fall, but the store moves fast
Season of Geglash, don’t close that screen
A legendary promise in a glowing machine

[Verse 2]
The battle pass has sixty tiers and wings at level ten
A premium path gives double sparks, a wolf, and twice the friends
Daily contracts call at sunrise, weekly raids at midnight blue
Miss three days and the calendar says the season passed through you

[Verse 3]
Guild halls sell their banner slots, the leaderboards reset
Rent a forge, insure your loot, protect the things you get
A cosmetic portal, a cosmetic horse, a cosmetic storm
The plain old armor looks ashamed beside the paid-for form

[Pre-Chorus]
Geglash says, "The odds are honest," with a shimmer in his eye
"Just one more shard and you can touch the stars before they fly"

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Season of Geglash
Spin for the treasure, make the jackpot flash
One more pull for a perfect class
The demons fall, but the store moves fast
Season of Geglash, don’t close that screen
A legendary promise in a glowing machine

[Bridge]
There’s a timer on the terror, there’s a sale below the moon
A founder’s pack for early access to a patch arriving soon
Trade your tokens, fuse your echoes, chase the number climbing high
Sanctuary keeps its doors unlocked for anybody who can buy

[Breakdown]
No rest at the waypoint, no quiet after dawn
The next reward is almost here, the old reward is gone
I came to kill a demon, I came to walk the rain
Now every bell from every menu knows my name

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Season of Geglash
The fire is pretty, and the numbers crash
I kept on spinning for a perfect class
Till the last small coin became the ash
Season of Geglash, the candles lean
I leave the glowing altar and the hungry machine
I leave the glowing altar… and the hungry machine
[End]

songPlan.arrangement: A 330-second post-punk rock song with a supple, prominent electric bass line, clipped electric guitars, live drums, restrained synth texture, and small piano accents. Open with a dry, intimate vocal over bass and guitar; grow through elastic verses into broad, melodic choruses, then pull back for the compassionate bridge before a full-band final chorus. Tony’s V8 delivery is smoky, connected, lightly slurred and mischievously human, with clear enough phrasing for the hook and sustained notes on the closing lines. Keep the groove lively rather than rap-like. The last sung syllable lands around 320 seconds, followed by one resolved E-minor chord decaying naturally to the end.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I traded the loading dock for a little blue square
A headset, a calendar, a meeting in the air
They said, “Keep the work moving, keep the people clear”
So I learned a dozen names for a thing called fear
The old shop clock had a fist and a face
This one sends a gentle ping when I’m losing my place
I ask what is blocking us, the room looks down
Somebody’s camera freezes in a far-off town

[Pre-Chorus]
I used to know the weight of a wrench in my hand
Now I move colored tickets across digital land

[Chorus]
Stand up, stand up, tell me where we are
We got a little whiteboard and a dying star
I’m not the boss, I’m just holding the thread
Trying to make a tomorrow out of what was said
Stand up, stand up, the world ran ahead
But I’m still here making room for the next small step

[Verse 2]
There’s a kid on the call with a faster tongue
He says the whole old system is already done
He can build a new future before lunch breaks through
And I say, “That’s beautiful—show me how you do”
My résumé reads like a closed-down street
Places where the forklifts sang and the night shift ate
I don’t hide those years in a polished phrase
They taught me how to listen when a plan decays

[Section]
We slice the mountain into pieces we can hold
One week at a time, one story getting told
A woman says she’s drowning; I cancel the race
We leave one chair empty and give her some space
Nobody applauds that, nobody sends a prize
But her shoulders come back when she opens her eyes

[Chorus]
Stand up, stand up, tell me where we are
We got a little whiteboard and a dying star
I’m not the boss, I’m just holding the thread
Trying to make a tomorrow out of what was said
Stand up, stand up, the world ran ahead
But I’m still here making room for the next small step

[Bridge]
Maybe I arrived when the language changed
With my paper maps and my weathered name
Maybe every door wants a newer key
Maybe that is not the end of me
I can ask the question nobody wants to raise
I can keep a lantern through the foggy days
I can hear the joke behind the corporate speech
And pull the quiet person back within our reach

[Verse 3]
Friday comes humming through the office glass
We look at the chart, let the numbers pass
Not every promise made it over the line
But nobody got left behind this time
I close the laptop, hear the evening train
For one second all the old noise calls my name
Then a message lands: “Thanks for making it safe”
And the tired little room has a different shape

[Chorus]
Stand up, stand up, tell me where we are
Not beneath the future, not beyond the scar
I’m not the boss, I’m just holding the thread
Making room for the living words unsaid
Stand up, stand up, let the new world run
I’ll meet it with the work that gets begun
If the road keeps changing under my feet
I’ll gather the people, and we’ll make the next step sweet

[Outro]
No grand conversion, no victory parade
Just a chair in the circle and a promise remade
When the screen goes dark and the last bell rings
I’ll carry us forward—one small human thing
[End]

songPlan.title: I Fuck Around
songPlan.arrangement: Up-tempo 1960s California surf-rock with bright reverb electric guitars, rolling electric bass, live kit, handclaps, organ touches, and stacked sunny backing harmonies. Tony leads in rough, connected, mischievous melodic phrasing, while the chorus opens into buoyant group responses. Start with a short instrumental surf-guitar pickup, build from breezy verses to a full final chorus, then carry the final sustained word through about 153–157 seconds before one resolved E-major chord decays naturally.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Salt on the dashboard, sun in my eyes
Board in the back and a gull cutting by
The radio crackles, the tide pulls out
I laugh at the blue and I turn it loud

[Verse 1]
I missed the turn at the corner store
Found a little beach I ain't seen before
Waves throw silver on the parking lot
Everybody worries, but I forgot
I fuck around when the daylight bends
Trade my tight plans for the tide and friends
Got a pocket of sand and a half-made scheme
Chasing the foam through a California dream

[Chorus]
I fuck around, I fuck around
With the sun going down on a seaside town
I fuck around, hear the whole world sing
When the surf kicks up and the gulls take wing
No map in my hand, no clock to obey
Just a bright white wake and a runaway day
I fuck around, then I come back home
With the ocean still humming inside my bones

[Verse 2]
Cherry-red coupe at the end of the pier
Somebody's laughing and shifting a gear
We steal a dance by the carnival light
Spinning our shadows into the night
A vinyl moon hangs over the bay
You say tomorrow can wait one day
I draw your name where the water won't stay
Then watch the wave take the letters away

[Bridge]
If the grown-up world starts calling my name
I'll let it ring while the breakers complain
There ain't a prize for a perfectly straight line
The best little detours are usually mine

[Chorus]
I fuck around, I fuck around
With the stars coming out on a seaside town
I fuck around, but I know what's true
Every wild blue mile keeps leading to you
No map in my hand, no clock to obey
Just your warm voice and the end of the day
I fuck around, then I come back home
With your name and the ocean inside my bones

[Outro]
When the last wave folds into the shore
I'll hold that bright blue feeling once more
[End]

songPlan.title: Blackout at Last Call
songPlan.arrangement: Dark theatrical cabaret-rock at 116 BPM in D minor. Driving bass and restrained rock drums anchor organ, piano, violin, harp and accordion; the arrangement grows from a smoky, close-miked opening into full-band choruses, then drops to piano and voice for the bridge before a resolved final chorus. Tony’s pinned v7 delivery is rough, smoky, connected and melodic, with muttered edges but a clear catchable hook. Pace the final sustained word “tonight” to land 8–12 seconds before 4:00, followed by one final resolved chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Neon leaking through the blind
Coins in my pocket, static in my mind
I keep buying one more hour
Like a promise from a broken tower

[Verse 1]
I meet a stranger under violet light
Both of us tired of pretending tonight
I say, “I’m fine,” with a laugh too loud
Trying to disappear inside the crowd
Every time the room gets close to still
Every time I think I’ve bent my will
The ceiling shakes, the streetlights flare
And I’m left alone with the smoke in the air

[Pre-Chorus]
I curse the clock, I curse the heat
I curse the pulse beneath my feet
What am I chasing down this lane?
A little thrill, a lot of shame

[Chorus]
Blackout at last call, blackout again
I keep making a stranger carry my pain
Blackout at last call, the whole room sways
I can’t buy back all my wasted days

[Verse 2]
The bartender knows my borrowed name
Slides the water, never feeds the game
An old piano finds a minor tune
Like a tired heart arguing with the moon
I see my face in the polished glass
A man who thinks the night will pass
But every promise comes apart
When you rent a room around your heart

[Pre-Chorus]
The sirens rise, the red lights spin
I hear the damage settling in
No lover, no drink, no louder song
Can make a wrong road right for long

[Chorus]
Blackout at last call, blackout again
I keep making a stranger carry my pain
Blackout at last call, the whole room sways
I can’t buy back all my wasted days

[Bridge]
I wanted the spark, I wanted the rush
Wanted the world to hush, hush, hush
But the ache had my number, the ache knew my name
And it never once asked what I became
So I leave the cash, I leave the key
Leave the little wreck that used to be me
Out on the pavement, dawn comes slow
And for the first time, I let somebody know

[Chorus]
No blackout at last call, not one more time
I’m done mistaking a fall for a climb
No blackout at last call, I breathe through the flame
I walk toward morning and answer my name

[Outro]
The piano holds one honest chord
The street gets quiet, the sky unwarms
I’m still here, and I choose the light
I’m still here tonight
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Door shut behind me, iron in my hand
Rain on the roof like a one-man band
Henri, you better quit hiding in the dark
I got a lantern and a nervous little spark
Every corridor keeps changing its face
Rats in the pantry, water in the place
I heard a chain go singing underground
Now I am walking where I should not be found

[Pre-Chorus]
Wind up the light, count to three
Something down there is counting me

[Chorus]
The bunker has teeth, the bunker has breath
It chews on the daylight and whistles for death
I pull that lever, I run for the door
But the thing in the walls wants a little bit more
The bunker has teeth
And I cannot sleep

[Verse 2]
Found an old soldier curled by the well
His empty eyes had a story to tell
A note said "save him," a note said "flee"
A gun in the drawer and a key for the sea
I drag my boots through a flooded hall
Hear that beast scrape across the wall
One wrong noise and the whole place wakes
I am feeding it fear with every step I take

[Bridge]
No, no, no—keep the generator alive
No, no, no—just give me one more try
Smoke in my lungs, blood on the floor
I am not dying in this damned old war

[Chorus]
The bunker has teeth, the bunker has breath
It knows all my footsteps, it laughs at my death
I found the way out, I found the last key
But the dark came running like it wanted me
The bunker has teeth, but I still move on
I carry the flame till the black is gone
Henri, if you hear me, hold on tonight
I am coming through the ruin with a shaking light

[Outro]
I am coming with a shaking li-i-ight
[End]

songPlan.title: S Rank on the Floor
songPlan.arrangement: Fast, tense tactical punk-rock with overdriven guitars, muscular moving bass, punchy live drums, clipped police-radio textures and brief siren-like synth swells. Tony’s pinned V8 delivery is smoky, slurred and increasingly exasperated, but the hook stays strongly melodic. Build from controlled verse tension into explosive choruses, then a frustrated half-time breakdown and final full-band release. The final sustained word “alive” lands about 9 seconds before the 310-second finish, followed by one resolved minor-to-major closing chord decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Blue light leaking through the motel glass
Radio says slow, but the first door cracks
I see a shadow raise a shaking hand
My finger answers before my head can plan
One bad guy down, one report to write
One more gold star turning charcoal tonight
The team says, “Clear,” I can hear the score
A little red stain by the bedroom door

[Pre-Chorus]
Zip ties, evidence, corners checked twice
Why does doing right come at such a price?

[Chorus]
Ready or not, I’m trying not to fire
Ready or not, the hallway climbs higher
I want that clean S shining at the end
But every armed fool makes the plan bend
Ready or not, I call for hands in sight
Then somebody reaches and ruins my night
I’m doing the job, I’m paying the cost
And watching that perfect rank get lost

[Verse 2]
Apartment three has a television glow
Cartoon laughter where the shell casings go
A man in a vest comes out of the smoke
I shout the command, he gives me a joke
He swings toward me, so the room goes loud
My report gets longer, my patience gets proud
Civilian crying by the laundry machine
Says, “Was that necessary?” You know what I mean

[Pre-Chorus]
I bag every weapon, I check every name
Still the debrief screen is spelling my shame

[Chorus]
Ready or not, I’m trying not to fire
Ready or not, the hallway climbs higher
I want that clean S shining at the end
But every armed fool makes the plan bend
Ready or not, I call for hands in sight
Then somebody reaches and ruins my night
I’m doing the job, I’m paying the cost
And watching that perfect rank get lost

[Bridge]
I brought beanbags, shields and all the restraint
I gave them a warning, I practically faint
I waited a second, then another half
The suspect fired first—don’t make me laugh
The clock keeps ticking, the bodycam rolls
I’m counting my penalties, losing control
No unauthorized force, no wounded friend
Just let one mission have a peaceful end

[Breakdown]
Stack on the door, breathe through the mask
“Talk to me, pal, just make this easy,” I ask
He drops the rifle, I almost believe
Then a pistol appears from under his sleeve

[Chorus]
Ready or not, I’m done being polite
Ready or not, I survive the night
I wanted an S, but the screen can wait
I got my whole team through the iron gate
Ready or not, let the record show
I gave every warning I had to throw
If keeping them breathing means losing the crown
Then stamp that rank while I put danger down

[Outro]
The van doors close and the city goes still
No perfect score, but we made it home alive
[End]

songPlan.title: Forty Below Midnight Signal
songPlan.arrangement: Dark synthwave reinterpretation at 100 BPM with pulsing analog bass, gated arpeggiators, icy pads, Linn-style drums, low electric-guitar swells, and a restrained lead synth. Tony V8 sings in a smoky, connected, slightly slurred melodic delivery; the recurring hook includes a brief muttered laugh. Build from sparse winter atmosphere into broad, catchable choruses, then carry the final sustained “home” to roughly 240 seconds before one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Snow against the window, bourbon in the glass
Fairbanks in December, headlights crawling past
The bartender knows better than to ask me why
I am drinking to the woman I was lucky to survive

[Verse 1]
We rented half a duplex by the old Steese road
A heater full of thunder and a roof bowed low with snow
She could kiss me like a promise, then accuse me with her eyes
By midnight every tender word was twisted into knives
I learned to read the weather in the muscles of her face
One minute I was everything, the next I was replaced
I tried to hold the center while the center would not stay
Love became a checkpoint at the ending of each day

[Pre-Chorus]
So fill it to the frost line
Let the old jukebox complain
I do not want that life back
I just miss it now and then

[Chorus]
Forty below and one more round
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down
She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free
That woman was crazy, and she was crazy for me
No more slammed doors, no more Avenue Two
I will not call her number, no matter what I do
But sometimes—heh heh—sometimes I remember when

[Verse 2]
Creamer’s Field in summer, mosquitoes in our hair
She danced beside the pickup like the whole world was not there
Then jealousy would find us before we made it home
My coat out in the yard and my telephone gone
I tried patience, tried forgiveness, tried the careful things to say
But every breath became a test I had to pass that day
You can give somebody everything and still not give them rest
And wake up in the cold convinced you failed their test

[Bridge]
Blue light rising over Chena in the spring
Her cheek against my shoulder, not demanding anything
For one clean little minute, we were quiet, we were kind
That is the piece the whiskey keeps polishing in my mind
But a photograph is not a shelter, a spark is not a stove
I miss the heat between us; I do not miss losing hope

[Chorus]
Forty below, this is my last round
Her memory can visit, but it cannot move back to town
She was wild as the river, I was drowning willingly
That woman was trouble, tangled up with me
I turn my phone face down beneath the Fairbanks moon
Let the old ache fade out with the vapor tune
Here is to what was beautiful, here is what I know:
I miss the fire sometimes, but I will not call it home

[Outro]
Snow against the window, morning coming slow
Here is to what was beautiful—and what I had to let go
I miss the fire sometimes, but I will not mistake it for home
No, I will not mistake it for home
[End]

[Intro]
The train quit breathing at the edge of town
Rain on the windows, moon hanging down
Per'kele laughing from the station wall
Said, “Three days, Tony—try not to fall”

[Verse 1]
I woke in a bed with the curtains tied
Knife in my pocket and a bad left side
Karin had a camera, Levi had a stare
Marina drew symbols in the rotten air

The town was empty but the bells still rang
A centipede priest had a rusted fang

songPlan.title: Yeah After Midnight (Velvet Pocket)
songPlan.arrangement: A brisk, smooth soul-jazz reinterpretation built around a lively electric-bass pocket, crisp drums, Rhodes electric piano, Hammond organ, clean electric guitar, muted trumpet and tenor saxophone. The opening uses close, audible breaths and one exposed “Yeah” before the groove enters. Tony V8 delivers the verses as a rough, smoky self-conversation, alternating questions, muttered replies, crooked timing and short laughs while keeping the melodic “Yeah after midnight” refrain clear and catchable. Horn punches and organ swells answer the vocal without creating long instrumental gaps. Energy rises from an intimate opening through increasingly animated exchanges, relaxes briefly in the bridge, then reaches a full-band final refrain. The last sustained syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved Eb-major chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Yeah
The room still breathing, the street gone quiet

[Verse 1]
Yeah
Yeah
Yeah
You still awake?
Uh huh, I might be
Talking to the shadow sitting right beside me
Heh, what'd he say?
Said the night ain't done
Said the clock lost count when it struck one
Rain on the glass and a red exit light
I ask myself a question, get myself right
You going home?
No, not yet
Got a little conversation I ain't finished with

[Refrain]
Yeah after midnight
Yeah, that's when it starts
Bass in the floorboards, smoke in the heart
Uh huh, after midnight
When the straight lines bend
I talk to myself like an old lost friend

[Verse 2]
Yeah
Yeah
Yeah
Yeah
Who moved the moon?
Wasn't me, no sir
Who told the whole room everything was a blur?
Maybe that horn did, leaning on blue
Maybe the mirror knows more than you
Woah, slow down
I am sitting still
Then why does the ceiling keep climbing the hill?
Heh, good question
Don't answer too soon
Leave a little silence for the bass and the moon
I say yes to the rhythm, it says yes to me
Two sides talking in the same body

[Interlude]
Yeah
Uh huh, I heard that
A little behind me, a little ahead
One voice laughing while the other one said
Yeah after midnight

[Bridge]
Yeah
Yeah
Tell me, are you lonely?
Only when I leave
Tell me, do you mean all the stories you believe?
Some of them sparkle, some of them lie
Some turn to vapor when the taxis roll by
Then keep one true thing
All right, I will
The pulse in the pocket when the whole town's still
The breath before the answer
The grin in the sound
That low little yes when the lights go down

[Verse 3]
Yeah
Yeah
Yeah
Now the window's paling, morning at the seam
You were talking mighty loud for a half-awake dream
Was I talking to myself?
You usually do
Did I say anything wise?
Not a word that was new
Uh huh, fair enough
But the groove stayed clean
And the night told the truth in the spaces between
The glass stopped shaking, the rain moved on
Still the bass kept walking toward the edge of dawn
If I ask one more question, will you answer me right?
Only if the answer is the rest of the night

[Refrain]
Yeah after midnight
Yeah, that's when it starts
Keys in the lamplight, time coming apart
Uh huh, after midnight
Every answer swings
One voice asks and the other voice sings
Yeah after midnight
I know what I heard
A whole conversation in a one-syllable word

[Outro]
Yeah
Yeah
Yeeaah
The morning can wait outside
I'm still here, talking to the night
Yeah after midni-i-ight
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Load the dungeon, light a torch
Tony's got a gaming coach
Says, “This time I know the route”
First dark hallway—lights go out

[Verse 1]
Found a bonesaw, lost a shoe
Something hungry chewed straight through
Missed the coin flip, lost his arm
Stepped on every fucking harm
Guard came dragging down the hall
Tony ducked behind the wall
Floor gave way beneath him then
Goddamn—nine-eleven'd again

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
Tony growls, “Aw, son of a bitch”
Loads that miserable save from six
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Verse 2]
Back downstairs with half a map
Dodged the dogs and found a trap
Fed the girl and saved his meat
Crow Mauler dropped him through the street
Tony leaned into the screen
“That's the cheapest shit I've seen”
Lit a smoke and counted ten
Got up—nine-eleven'd again

[Pre-Chorus]
Now his grin is getting crooked
Every guide says he mistook it
Every doorway smells like doom
Still he kicks into the room

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
Tony snarls, “You rigged this shit”
Throws the mouse but will not quit
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Bridge]
Coin in the air—call it clean
Heads means mercy, tails gets mean
It hits the stone, it rolls from sight
Dungeon laughs and kills the light
Tony mutters, low and slow
“You ain't tellin' me to go”
Blood at one and mind at ten
He crawls toward the throne again

[Breakdown]
No food left
No good limb
No clean save
Still goes in
Bell starts shaking
Ceiling bends
Tony sees it—“Not this again!”

[Verse]
Past the prison, past the mines
Past the rotten gods and signs
Every loss has taught his hands
Where the blade falls, where it lands
Last door opens, pale and wide
All that spite walks in beside him
Dungeon offers one last spin
Tony laughs, “Then let me win.”

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again—
But he rises through the din
Let it crash, he'll crawl back in
No more begging at the end
Tony roars, “You hungry pit,
I can die all night, you prick!”
Fear in the dark, but fire within
You can nine-eleven him again—
He'll load that bastard save and win

[Outro]
Screen goes black, the final chord bends
Tony grins: “Now who's annoyed, my friend?”
[End]

songPlan.title: Forty Below - Vapor Midnight
songPlan.arrangement: A dark vaporwave and synth-noir reinterpretation built around the recognizable title hook and wintry Fairbanks narrative. Begin with detuned electric piano, distant analog pads and cassette haze, then introduce a deep moving synth bass and restrained electronic drums. Choruses widen with pulsing arpeggiators, gated snare ambience and cold lead-synth countermelodies; the bridge strips back to bass, electric piano and suspended pads before the final chorus reaches the fullest weight. Tony V8 delivers rough, smoky, connected melodic phrases with crooked timing, a quiet laugh in the recurring hook and clearer emphasis on the title line. Keep the vocal present throughout, allow no extended instrumental gaps, and pace the outro so the final sustained “home” lands 8–12 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved F# minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Snow against the window, bourbon in the glass
Fairbanks in December, headlights crawling past
Bartender knows better than to ask me why
I’m drinking to the woman I was lucky to survive

[Verse 1]
We rented half a duplex by the old Steese road
With a heater full of thunder and a roof that bowed with snow
She could kiss me like a promise, then accuse me with her eyes
By midnight every tender word was twisted into knives
I learned to read the weather in the muscles of her face
One minute I was everything, the next I was replaced
Those borderline nights kept moving every wall
I loved her, but I couldn’t be the answer to it all

[Pre-Chorus]
So fill it to the frost line
Let the old jukebox complain
I don’t want that life back
I just miss it now and then

[Chorus]
Forty below and one more round
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down
She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free
That woman was crazy, and she was crazy for me
I’m glad it’s over, swear I know that’s true
No more slammed doors, no more driving Avenue Two
I won’t call her number, I won’t go back again
But sometimes—heh heh—sometimes I remember when

[Verse 2]
There were summer nights at Creamer’s Field, mosquitoes in our hair
She danced beside the pickup like the whole world wasn’t there
Then jealousy would find us before we made it home
She’d throw my coat into the yard and hide my telephone
I tried to hold the center while the center wouldn’t stay
Tried patience, tried forgiveness, tried the careful things to say
But love became a checkpoint, every breath became a test
You can give somebody everything and still not give them rest

[Pre-Chorus]
Now the bottle makes a halo
Round the places we went wrong
And every bad decision
Gets a pretty little song

[Chorus]
Forty below and one more round
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down
She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free
That woman was crazy, and she was crazy for me
I’m glad it’s over, swear I know that’s true
No more slammed doors, no more driving Avenue Two
I won’t call her number, I won’t go back again
But sometimes—heh heh—sometimes I remember when

[Bridge]
I remember blue light rising over Chena in the spring
Her cheek against my shoulder, not demanding anything
For one clean little minute, we were quiet, we were kind
That’s the piece the whiskey keeps polishing in my mind
But a photograph ain’t shelter, and a spark is not a stove
I miss the heat between us; I don’t miss losing hope

[Chorus]
Forty below, this is my last round
Her memory can visit, but it can’t move back to town
She was wild as the river, I was drowning willingly
That woman was trouble, and she was tangled up with me
I’m glad it’s over, and tonight I know it’s true
No more frozen apologies beneath that Fairbanks moon
I turn my phone face down before the old ache starts
She can keep the northern fire; I’m taking back my heart

[Outro]
Snow against the window, morning coming slow
Here’s to what was beautiful—and what I had to let go
I miss the fire sometimes, but I won’t mistake it for home
No, I won’t mistake it for home
[End]

songPlan.title: Forty Below and One More Round
songPlan.arrangement: A 270-second arctic honky-tonk soul-rock song in E minor at 92 BPM, carried by a swaying 6/8 pocket, prominent melodic electric bass, dry drums, baritone electric guitar, Wurlitzer electric piano, and restrained lap steel. Open immediately with Tony over the full groove, then broaden through two verse–pre-chorus–chorus cycles. Pull the band back for the reflective bridge before a stronger final chorus and concise resolved outro. The pinned V8 Tony vocal is rough, smoky, connected, and naturally slurred, with a brief mischievous “heh heh” in the chorus but a clearly sung hook and emotionally sober finish. Let the final sustained word “home” land around 260 seconds, followed by one resolved E-minor chord decaying to exactly 270 seconds; no extended instrumental tail.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Snow against the window, bourbon in the glass
Fairbanks in December, headlights crawling past
Bartender knows better than to ask me why
I’m drinking to the woman I was lucky to survive

[Verse 1]
We rented half a duplex by the old Steese road
With a heater full of thunder and a roof that bowed with snow
She could kiss me like a promise, then accuse me with her eyes
By midnight every tender word was twisted into knives
I learned to read the weather in the muscles of her face
One minute I was everything, the next I was replaced
Those borderline nights kept moving every wall
I loved her, but I couldn’t be the answer to it all

[Pre-Chorus]
So fill it to the frost line
Let the old jukebox complain
I don’t want that life back
I just miss it now and then

[Chorus]
Forty below and one more round
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down
She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free
That woman was crazy, and she was crazy for me
I’m glad it’s over, swear I know that’s true
No more slammed doors, no more driving Avenue Two
I won’t call her number, I won’t go back again
But sometimes—heh heh—sometimes I remember when

[Verse 2]
There were summer nights at Creamer’s Field, mosquitoes in our hair
She danced beside the pickup like the whole world wasn’t there
Then jealousy would find us before we made it home
She’d throw my coat into the yard and hide my telephone
I tried to hold the center while the center wouldn’t stay
Tried patience, tried forgiveness, tried the careful things to say
But love became a checkpoint, every breath became a test
You can give somebody everything and still not give them rest

[Pre-Chorus]
Now the bottle makes a halo
Round the places we went wrong
And every bad decision
Gets a pretty little song

[Chorus]
Forty below and one more round
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down
She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free
That woman was crazy, and she was crazy for me
I’m glad it’s over, swear I know that’s true
No more slammed doors, no more driving Avenue Two
I won’t call her number, I won’t go back again
But sometimes—heh heh—sometimes I remember when

[Bridge]
I remember blue light rising over Chena in the spring
Her cheek against my shoulder, not demanding anything
For one clean little minute, we were quiet, we were kind
That’s the piece the whiskey keeps polishing in my mind
But a photograph ain’t shelter, and a spark is not a stove
I miss the heat between us; I don’t miss losing hope

[Chorus]
Forty below, this is my last round
Her memory can visit, but it can’t move back to town
She was wild as the river, I was drowning willingly
That woman was trouble, and she was tangled up with me
I’m glad it’s over, and tonight I know it’s true
No more frozen apologies beneath that Fairbanks moon
I turn my phone face down before the old ache starts
She can keep the northern fire; I’m taking back my heart

[Outro]
Snow against the window, morning coming slow
Here’s to what was beautiful—and what I had to let go
I miss the fire sometimes, but I won’t mistake it for home
No, I won’t mistake it for home
[End]

songPlan.arrangement: A 195-second bass-forward soul-rock song with a lively 4/4 pocket, bright electric guitars, warm organ, punchy drums and restrained brass punctuation. Open immediately with the lead vocal over bass, rim-click and guitar, then widen through pre-choruses into full, melodic choruses. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
South Station breathed out a river of coats
I stepped through the steam with my past in my throat
The rain wrote silver on Atlantic Avenue
Every window held a man I almost knew
I followed the harbor where the cold wind came
Then somebody laughed and it sounded like my name
Not the name on the ticket, not the one I became
The old one underneath it, still carrying a flame

[Pre-Chorus]
I had crossed every line on the map
Just to circle the truth and come back

[Chorus]
Boston, you found me before I found you
Under that hard gray, breaking into blue
I was gone so long I thought gone was what I am
Then the city said my name and I remembered who I am
Yeah, the city said my name

[Verse 2]
Past the Common trees and the red-brick rows
A busker bent a melody the whole town knows
I bought bad coffee, let the morning sting
Watched a sparrow steal a piece of everything
There were years in my pocket I could never spend
Doors I had slammed that were open again
On the Charles, every ripple split the light
Like a hundred little chances getting something right

[Pre-Chorus]
No angel came, no thunder cracked
Just my own two feet that carried me back

[Chorus]
Boston, you found me before I found you
Under that hard gray, breaking into blue
I was gone so long I thought gone was what I am
Then the city said my name and I remembered who I am
Yeah, the city said my name

[Bridge]
Maybe home is not a house you keep
Maybe it is what wakes up when the hurt runs deep
A voice from a doorway, a hand on the rail
The nerve to begin when the old plans fail
I faced my reflection in a black shop pane
Said, there you are, you fool—and I laughed in the rain

[Chorus]
Boston, you found me, now I am standing true
With the harbor behind me and the whole sky new
I was gone so long, but gone is not where I end
The city said my name, and I answered it again
Boston, hold the morning while I make my way
I came here as a stranger—I am leaving here as me today
The city said my name
And I answered: here I am

[End]

songPlan.title: The Golden Plague
songPlan.arrangement: A fast, vicious horror-punk and surf-rock original in D minor, driven by tremolo electric guitar, overdriven bass, pounding drums, and stabbing organ. The Tony V8 pinned voice delivers smoky, connected phrasing with slurred consonants, muttered menace, and increasingly frantic melodic outbursts while keeping the refrain immediately catchable. Vocals enter at once; verses escalate from mass hysteria to grotesque national collapse, the bridge strips back around bass and floor toms, and the final verse expands into a grim resolution. The last lyric lands about 10 seconds before the 145-second mark, followed only by one resolved minor chord and its natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The Golden Answer hit the air at eight
By noon the bottles lined the interstate
They raised them warm beneath the courthouse clock
While smiling anchors called it common sense

A father toasted victory at lunch
His kidneys clenched before the evening news
A bride went gray beside the wedding cake
And left a yellow shadow in the lace

[Refrain]
Drink it down, the nation cried
Salt on the tongue and fire inside
The Golden Answer sold the lie
Then every bathroom learned to testify

[Verse 2]
In Phoenix, bodies blistered in the heat
Their mouths like paper, hearts off every beat
In Boston, office workers locked their jaws
And tore their lips on cups of brittle glass

A marching band collapsed along the route
Their uniforms went dark from inside out
One tuba held a final crooked tone
While something red and foaming filled the horn

[Refrain]
Drink it down, the nation cried
Salt on the tongue and fire inside
The Golden Answer sold the lie
Then every bathroom learned to testify

[Bridge]
No miracle was hiding in the waste
Just thirst returning with a poisoned face
The living watched the death count scrape the sky
And still the jingle told them one more try

[Verse]
The hospitals ran black with failing lights
The gutters steamed through three unending nights
A million cups lay shining in the dawn
Beside the swollen dead on every lawn

At last one child reached up and killed the song
The speakers clicked; the awful spell was gone
She poured the final bottle in the drain
And rain came clean against the windowpane

[Refrain]
Drink it down—the nation lied
Gold in the glass, but death inside
The answer failed, the fever died
Remember every mouth it left bone-dry

[Outro]
No cure was ever waiting in that cup
The drain swallowed the last gold drop
[End]

songPlan.title: Everybody Came as the End of the World
songPlan.arrangement: A fast, darkly comic horror-punk and garage-rock song in 4/4, performed with distorted electric guitars, a melodic overdriven bass, punchy live drums, and brief detuned organ accents. Begin with the vocal immediately over a tight bass-and-drum entrance. Verses use wiry palm-muted guitar and a lively pocket; pre-choruses climb with toms and organ; choruses open into broad power chords and a catchable melody. The bridge becomes increasingly surreal, then drops to bass, floor tom, and sparse guitar for the breakdown before the full band returns for the final chorus. Tony’s selected v8 voice stays rough, smoky, connected, and mischievously slurred at first, becoming alarmed and unexpectedly sincere by the ending, with natural crooked timing and fully sung melodic lines. Pace the final outro across the closing passage so the last sung syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 270 seconds; finish with one decisive D-minor chord and a natural decay, without an extended instrumental tail.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Halloween evening, Tony checked the glass
Cardboard skyline and a cloud of gray
A paper little airplane pinned across his chest
He said, “This is awful”—then he wore it anyway
He strutted down the sidewalk with a plastic pumpkin pail
Past the porch-light ghosts and the pharmacy fog
But every door was empty, every candy bowl was still
And the moon looked sick behind a telephone pole

[Pre-Chorus]
He heard a siren laughing two blocks down
Saw smoke above the old familiar town

[Chorus]
Everybody came as the end of the world
Every boy, every man, every terrible girl
Some were 9/11-ing right there in the street
Some had been 9'11'd from their heads to their feet
Tony said, “I had this first—this nightmare was mine”
But the whole block flashed like a warning sign
Everybody came as the end of the world
And nobody knew who had started it

[Verse 2]
Mikey wore a tie and kept reading the news
Jenny was a tower with a window-screen crown
Danny yelled “incoming” whenever leaves fell
Then collapsed on the lawn when the wind knocked him down
At the corner stood Frankie, staring straight through Tony
With ash on his jacket and punch in his hand
He muttered, “I was normal when the party began
Then somebody made history happen again”

[Pre-Chorus]
The porch band stopped on a sour little chord
Nobody laughed at the costumes anymore

[Chorus]
Everybody came as the end of the world
Every boy, every man, every terrible girl
Some were 9/11-ing right there in the street
Some had been 9'11'd from their heads to their feet
Tony said, “This joke has gotten too real”
As the Ferris-wheel moon started losing a wheel
Everybody came as the end of the world
And nobody knew how to stop it

[Bridge]
Tony tore the airplane loose from his shirt
Pulled down the skyline and stamped out the dirt
“Take off the smoke, take off the date
We can still be monsters without tempting fate”
But the masks had learned faces, the props had learned flame
And the night kept calling everybody by name
So Tony grabbed the fire bell, swung till it rang
One hard note through the panic and clang

[Breakdown]
No punch line
No prize
No clever disguise
Just friends in the street with the fear in their eyes
Tony shouted, “Party’s over—everybody come home”
And one by one they remembered their bones

[Chorus]
Everybody came as the end of the world
Then they peeled off the ruin, every boy, every girl
The 9/11-ing stopped when the church clock struck
And the 9'11'd rose up, dazed but unstuck
Tony stood in his undershirt, cold in the dawn
While the paper towers softened on somebody’s lawn
Everybody came as the end of the world
But nobody had to stay that way

[Outro]
He carried the costumes out to the curb
No speech, no laugh, not another bad word
When morning asked what he had been that night
Tony said, “Something stupid—and I finally got it right”
Then the last porch light went dark with the stars
And his friends walked home exactly as they are
[End]

songPlan.title: Don't Drink the Sales Pitch
songPlan.arrangement: A bass-forward acid-funk rock track in E minor, driven by syncopated electric bass, tight drums, wah guitar, clavinet, Hammond organ and brief baritone saxophone punches. The spoken opening introduces an unreliable pitch before Tony V8 enters with rough, smoky melodic phrasing, connected vowels, crooked timing and restrained muttered reactions. Verses build from sly skepticism into firm concern; choruses widen into memorable harmonies, and the bridge drops to bass, organ and rim clicks before a full-band final rise. Pace the closing verse and final chorus so the last sung syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 365 seconds, followed only by one resolved E-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Spoken Intro]
“You absolutely need to drink your own piss.”

[Verse 1]
That was the pitch from the folding-chair prophet,
Holding up a jar like the cure was inside it,
Promised clearer eyes and a stronger constitution,
But confidence is not the same as a solution.
He dressed up a rumor in a laboratory coat,
Put a mountain of assurance in a single little quote,
Said the body made a medicine too precious to dismiss—
The room leaned forward, but the evidence said this:

[Refrain]
Don't drink the sales pitch,
Don't swallow a claim
Just because somebody confident
Gives nature all the blame.
Your kidneys did their working,
Let the finished work depart;
There isn't proven healing
In returning to the start.

[Verse 2]
Urine carries water, salts, and filtered waste,
And traces of the medicines your system has displaced.
If you're dry and getting desperate, it can worsen what you face;
It is not clean drinking water and it cannot take its place.
No solid clinical evidence says drinking it will cure
Cancer, chronic illness, infection, or make immunity secure.
Anecdotes can sparkle when the data stays dim,
But a stranger's transformation doesn't make the odds less grim.

[Pre-Chorus]
Ask who ran the study,
Ask who checked the claim,
Ask if hope got dressed in facts
And borrowed science's name.

[Chorus]
Don't drink the sales pitch,
Put the miracle away.
Call a qualified clinician
When your health begins to sway.
Drink safe water when you're thirsty,
Take prescribed care to heart;
Your kidneys made an exit—
Don't send it back to start.

[Verse 3]
Maybe somebody mentions Colorado with authority,
A therapy group, a testimonial, a passionate minority.
A map pin isn't evidence, a club is not a trial,
And ten believers nodding cannot validate the vial.
They may list imagined benefits from skin to aching bone,
But repeating hopeful language doesn't make the outcome known.
If a claim could change your treatment or delay the help you need,
Bring it to a licensed expert before you act on creed.

[Instrumental Break]

[Verse 4]
Now the salesman taps the glass and says, “The old ways understood.”
But old does not mean harmless, and natural doesn't mean good.
Poison ivy's natural; dehydration is as well;
A simple-sounding ritual can hide a harder spell.
For someone taking medicine, unwanted traces may return;
For someone sick or vulnerable, there's more cause for concern.
And putting it on broken skin or drinking from another
Can introduce contamination—not a cure disguised as cover.

[Bridge]
This is not a joke on anybody searching for relief,
Pain can make a doorway for an easy kind of belief.
You deserve an honest answer, even when the answer's plain:
There may be no instant remedy for complicated pain.
Good care can feel less dazzling than a secret in a cup,
But tested help is kinder than a promise made up.

[Breakdown]
No proven fountain.
No hidden pharmacy.
No magic loop that makes the body's waste a therapy.
If symptoms keep returning,
If fever rises high,
Get medical attention—
Don't let a slogan decide.

[Chorus]
Don't drink the sales pitch,
Let the miracle depart.
Choose safe water, sound advice,
And give recovery a start.
Question every grand assurance,
Especially dressed as fact;
Real evidence invites inspection,
It doesn't fear being checked.

[Outro]
So when a voice insists you need it,
And certainty fills the room,
Remember hope needs honesty
If hope is going to bloom.
Leave the jar upon the table,
Let the shining story miss;
You absolutely need good evidence—
You do not need to drink your piss.
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Tony found a paperback beside the laundromat machine
Said the age of air was coming, said the planets must be clean
He drew a crooked little moon chart on a paper grocery sack
Then he canceled soap and reason—said he wouldn't need them back

[Verse 1]
Now he's charging jars of water in the blue light of the moon
Breathing through alternate nostrils every afternoon
He bought a crystal pendulum and hung it from the fan
It pointed at the kitchen, so he called it destiny's plan

He said, “Every drop is sacred, every urge must be retained
I can feel my hidden thunder getting polished in my brain”
Seven days of concentration, fourteen lectures in a row
Now he whispers to his trousers, “We got energy to grow”

[Chorus]
Tony's got an aura with a radius
You can sense it coming down the hall
He says nature never made a bar of soap
And enlightenment don't wash at all
Tony's got an aura with a radius
Cosmic truth and something else besides
He opens every window for the universe
The universe takes one sniff and hides

[Verse 2]
Then he read about recycling what the body throws away
Raised a warm and cloudy tumbler like a toast to break of day
Said, “The fountain is internal, and the proof is in the taste”
His houseplants leaned away from him with dignity and haste

At the market he wore linen and a necklace made of seeds
Told the cashier, “Modern bathing only manufactures needs”
She held her breath and scanned the sage, the incense, and the lime
While Tony praised his natural smell for seven solid minutes' time

[Break]
Bass line creeping, floorboards speaking
Tony's third eye starts to twitch
Saturn rising, friends advising
“Maybe rinse a little, Rich?”
He laughs, “You fear vibration!”
Then the whole room changes chairs
Even peace-loving strangers
Suddenly discover urgent errands downstairs

[Chorus]
Tony's got an aura with a radius
You can sense it coming down the hall
He says nature never made a bar of soap
And enlightenment don't wash at all
Tony's got an aura with a radius
Cosmic truth and something else besides
He opens every window for the universe
The universe takes one sniff and hides

[Bridge]
One night beneath the moonlight
His crystal gave no sign
He shook it over every jar
And blamed the grand design
Then a quiet thought came drifting
Clearer than his mystic brew:
“If the cosmos lives in everything,
Maybe soap is cosmic too”

[Verse]
Tony stood beneath the shower like a prophet in the rain
Watched a fortnight of ascension spiral laughing down the drain
Kept the breathing and the moonlight, kept the linen, kept the seeds
But retired the private tumbler and revised his daily needs

[Chorus]
Tony's got an aura with a radius
Now it smells like cedar, rain, and lime
He says wisdom isn't losing every strange idea
It's knowing when to change your mind
Tony's got an aura with a radius
But his friends can share the room again
He leaves one crystal shining on the windowsill
And lets the clean night air roll in

[Outro]
Let the clean night air roll in
Tony smiles and lets it in

[End]

songPlan.title: Who I Are
songPlan.arrangement: Bass-forward alternative funk-rock in 4/4, built from muscular electric bass, clipped electric guitars, live drums and restrained organ. Tony V8 delivers smoky, connected melodic lines with crooked timing, muttered emphasis and excited sustained outbursts while keeping the chorus catchable. songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jordan, you draw your maps with a trembling hand,
Sell a ladder to a boy who only needs a friend.
Tell him every room's a war, every heart's a test,
But a throne made out of anger never lets a body rest.
I have swallowed all the rules that said a man can't bend,
Found the strongest thing I did was let somebody in.

[Pre-Chorus]
Because I fought the demon, and I wear the scar, and who I am, is who I are
No borrowed crown, no ranking chart,
Can tell me what to do with my own heart.

[Chorus]
IT'S WHO I ARE, YEAH!
Not a wolf at the gate, not a king at the bar,
Not a number on a screen saying who the winners are.
I can carry my brother, I can ask him to stay,
I can lose, I can love, I can change my way.
IT'S WHO I ARE, YEAH!

[Verse 2]
To the boys in the basement with the blue light eyes,
You were lonely before somebody monetized the why.
They gave your hurt a uniform, put contempt in your mouth,
Pointed north toward domination while your hope headed south.
But women aren't a riddle and kindness isn't weak,
You don't need a grand permission slip to say what you need.
Wash the doctrine from your hands, come stand out in the rain,
There is life beyond the feed, there is language for the pain.

[Band Stop]
Drop it.

[Verse 3]
I'm a-one step ahead of the mortician, can't live day to day, business as usual, looking forward to front and center at a funeral
Not because I worship endings or want the final word,
I just know the clock keeps moving underneath the noise we've heard.
I'm burning that candle at both ends, alone or with friends living life before it ends
So I won't spend my little flame policing someone else's skin,
I would rather build a table and invite the whole world in.

[Bridge]
No alpha, beta, sigma badge can make the frightened whole,
No twelve clean rules can substitute for tending to the soul.
Clean your room, sure—but open up the door.
A tidy little kingdom can still leave you wanting more.
Say you're scared without disguising it as rage,
Turn the key, leave the cage,
Write a kinder page.

[Chorus]
IT'S WHO I ARE, YEAH!
I am rough around the truth, but I know where we are:
Every man is more than muscle, every wound is more than war.
You can carry your brother, you can ask him to stay,
You can lose, you can love, you can change your way.
No borrowed crown, no ranking chart,
No cold machine gets ownership of your heart.
Because I fought the demon, and I wear the scar, and who I am, is who I are

[Outro]
You don't want your time lyin' round, ya only... gonna get... laid down... UGHHHHH
So call the friend you miss tonight,
Trade the sermon for a porch-light.
I'm here till the last bright wick has waved,
Til I get laaaaaaaaaaid, down-in-my-grave!
IT'S WHO I ARE, YEAH!
[End]

songPlan.title: Occupied Until the End
songPlan.arrangement: A fast, macabre surf-punk rock song led by Tony C's pinned V8 voice, with spring-reverb electric guitars, prowling electric bass, pounding live drums, and brief organ stabs. Tight verses accelerate into explosive, catchable choruses; the bridge briefly thins to bass, toms, and tremolo guitar before the full band returns. Tony sings with rough, smoky slurs, nervous laughs, connected vowels, and increasingly frantic melodic outbursts while retaining clear hooks. The final chorus gives way to a grim, slower outro; the last syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved E-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony woke with a thunderclap
Low in the belly, mean and fast
Coffee cup shaking in his hand
He saw the restroom across the land
He ran through traffic, pale with need
Past every light at desperate speed
The porcelain sign shone clean and white
Then smoke climbed up and swallowed the light

[Pre-Chorus]
One step away, one handle to turn
The walls came down and the doorway burned

[Chorus]
Every bathroom got nine-elevened on approach
Every blessed stall went up in smoke
Tony cried, “Just give me thirty seconds alone!”
But the pipes burst loose and the whole roof blown
No vacancy, no mercy, no porcelain throne

[Verse 2]
He tried the diner by the tracks
The waitress pointed toward the back
He crossed the tiles with a hopeful shout
The mirrors shook and the lights went out
He tried the mall, the park, the bar
A roadside stop beneath a star
Each little figure upon the door
Vanished beneath another falling floor

[Pre-Chorus]
One step away, with salvation near
A siren screamed in his ringing ear

[Chorus]
Every bathroom got nine-elevened on approach
Every blessed stall went up in smoke
Tony begged, “I ain’t asking for a marble home!”
But the sinks took flight and the plumbing blown
No vacancy, no mercy, no porcelain throne

[Bridge]
He found a lonely service station
Beyond the edge of civilization
No crowd, no tower, no reason for doom
Just one dim hall and one small room
Tony slowed down, afraid to believe
The vacant sign offered sweet relief
His fingers closed on the silver latch—
The building folded like a struck match

[Breakdown]
He crawled from rubble, buttoned tight
Still denied on his final night
He cursed the sky, he cursed the street
He cursed each ruin beneath his feet
“Was one clean toilet too much to spare?”
Only ash answered through the air

[Chorus]
Every bathroom got nine-elevened on approach
Every final chance disappeared in smoke
Tony laughed once: “What a way to go—
The whole world’s got a restroom, but it tells me no.”
No vacancy, no mercy, no porcelain throne

[Outro]
At dawn they found him by the county line
With the restroom key and the vacant sign
He never crossed that last tiled floor
Never reached the handle, never closed the door
Tony C died with his need unmet
The cruelest appointment the world could set
One final breath, one unfinished plea:
“Couldn’t one damn bathroom wait for me?”

[End]

songPlan.title: Whoopsie Apartheid - The Rebuttal Room
songPlan.arrangement: A bass-forward Levantine art-rock reinterpretation in D minor at 104 BPM, built on muscular electric bass, dry drums, angular electric guitar, oud flourishes and restrained analog organ. The recurring “Whoopsie, apartheid” motif remains recognizable, but the verses use a tense new harmonic setting and the chorus opens into a broader melodic rebuttal. Tony V8 delivers the verses with smoky, connected phrasing, muttered skepticism and crooked timing while keeping the hook clear and sung. The bridge strips back to bass, oud and toms before a full-band final rise. Pace the final outro across the closing bars so the last syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 235 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
I walked back in the war room late
Coffee cold, maps on the wall
They said, “We solved the whole thing, Tony”
I said, “You missed half of it all”

[Verse 1]
One man said, “It’s uncomplicated”
One said, “History starts today”
I said, “Tell that to the hostage
Whose family waits and wastes away”
The room went still, the pens went down
Somebody guarded the door
I said, “A child is not a target—
Not in a kibbutz, not in war”

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid?
That’s a verdict, not a plan
You cannot make a safer home
By hiding half of where we stand
Whoopsie, apartheid?
Easy answers travel light
But peace must hold two peoples’ grief
And keep two peoples’ futures bright

[Verse 2]
Bring every living hostage home
Give each prisoner lawful trial
Let the food trucks through the crossings
Let the wounded leave in file
Stop the rockets, stop the bombing
Let the doctors do their work
When a leader orders slaughter
Put that leader before the court

You ask why the fences hardened
Why the shelters line the street
I remember buses burning
You remember armored feet
Neither memory grants permission
Neither terror makes things right
Fear may tell us why we’re fighting
It cannot tell us how to unite

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid?
Words can wound and words can warn
But no slogan wakes the missing
Or rebuilds what war has torn
Whoopsie, apartheid?
Peace is more than choosing sides
It means safety without conquest
Law without a place to hide

[Bridge]
Name the dead from every village
Hear the living, face to face
No ancestral wound gives license
To destroy another place
No October justifies famine
No occupation answers fear
If the truth has two cracked windows
Open both and make it clear

[Verse 3]
So we opened every ledger
Brought the witnesses inside
Made the powerful answer plainly
For the blood their speeches hide
Pulled the gunmen from the schoolyards
Pulled the checkpoints from the road
Built the homes before the slogans
Shared the water, shared the load

Every faith could keep its sacred
Every family lock its door
Children learned their neighbor’s language
Not the mathematics of war
Then the experts cleared their throats and asked,
“What miracle did you apply?”
I said, “Rights and recognition”
They said, “Surely that’s too simplified”

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid—
Maybe labels start the call
But a name alone won’t free a hostage
Or bring justice through the wall
Whoopsie, apartheid—
Now the gates can still come down
Equal dignity and shelter
Equal law in every town

[Outro]
It was simple, never easy
That distinction matters most
Peace began when neither future
Was a footnote to a boast
I still don’t know why nobody
Tried the obvious before:
Keep each other safe and free—
Then peace can walk through every door
[End]

A brief ominous intro leads through two rising verse–pre-chorus/chorus cycles, a stripped and suspenseful bridge, then a broadened final chorus. songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Engines wake beneath a violet sun
Black glass trembling, countdown begun
I leave my name where the radio glows
Then follow the signal nobody knows

[Verse 1]
Past the dead satellites and their blinking scars
I steer by static and unfinished stars
Earth folds down to a pale blue coin
While the hull keeps time with the asteroid noise
There is something breathing beyond the charts
Sending little cold knocks through the ship's steel heart
I turn every dial till the red lights sting
I bring my mic up to Uranus and I sing, I'll be Solo you be Lea cuz a playa gotta swing

[Pre-Chorus]
No map in my pocket, no moon in the glass
Just a voice from the void saying come on past
If the night wants a name, I will give it mine
Then outrun my shadow at the edge of time

[Chorus]
Ride that midnight current where the lost worlds shine
Bass pulse under me, danger close behind
I came for the distance, I stayed for the sound
Where the stars fall silent and the dark comes around
Send my song through the cold unknown
Four small words on the carrier tone:
Keep that blue world turning till I get back home

[Verse 2]
Had a room and a coolaw, in my big chevy
Now my bed is a harness and the air feels heavy
There are storms on Saturn like a crown of knives
And a red dust moon where nothing survives
I find an old beacon with a fractured face
Still whispering coordinates into empty space
I'll maybe even tour outer space, buy some Mars and Jupiters tickets from my guitar case
But the farther I travel, the clearer it gets:
Every bright new frontier leaves a trail of debts

[Chorus]
Ride that midnight current where the lost worlds shine
Bass pulse under me, danger close behind
I came for the distance, I stayed for the sound
Where the stars fall silent and the dark comes around
Send my song through the cold unknown
Four small words on the carrier tone:
Keep that blue world turning till I get back home

[Bridge]
Then the signal opens like an eye in the deep
Shows me every promise that the darkness keeps
Cities made of crystal, oceans without shores
Every missing traveler standing at their doors
I cut the main receiver, let temptation fade
Turn the ship toward morning through the mess I made
The unknown keeps calling, but I know its cost
You can chase every wonder and become what it lost

[Chorus]
Ride that midnight current, let the engines climb
Earth is still a heartbeat on the edge of time
I carry back the silence and the things I found
A scar across the starmap and a low machine sound
Send my song through the cold unknown
Tell them I was frightened, tell them I flew on
When the blue world rises in the forward glass
I will spend one quiet breath on all that passed
No throne in the heavens, no world I can own
I charted the dark, and the dark sang me home
[End]

Shows me every promise that the darkness keeps
Cities made of crystal, oceans without shores
Every missing traveler standing at their doors
I cut the main receiver, let temptation fade
Turn the ship toward morning through the mess I made
The unknown keeps calling, but I know its cost
You can chase every wonder and become what it lost

[Chorus]
Ride that midnight current, let the engines climb
Earth is still a heartbeat on the edge of time
I carry back the silence and the things I found
A scar across the starmap and a low machine sound
Send my song through the cold unknown
Tell them I was frightened, tell them I flew on
When the blue world rises in the forward glass
I will spend one quiet breath on all that passed
No throne in the heavens, no world I can own
I charted the dark, and the dark sang me home

songPlan.title: Whoopsie Apartheid
songPlan.arrangement: Bass-forward art-punk and funk-rock in 4/4, driven by syncopated electric bass, dry drums, clipped electric guitar, organ and restrained brass punches. Verses use a sly, conversational Tony V8 delivery with smoky slurs and muttered disbelief; choruses open into rough, sustained melodic lines and a catchable title hook. The bridge darkens to half-time before the final verse rebuilds into the largest chorus. Keep the singer continuously present, land the final sung syllable about 10 seconds before 4:40, then resolve one firm D-minor chord and let it decay naturally.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
I walked into the war room late
Coffee cold, maps on the wall
Everybody spoke in riddles
Like peace required no peace at all

[Verse 1]
One man said, “It’s complicated”
One said, “History ties our hands”
I said, “Quit bombing families
And stealing homes and land”
The room went still, the pens went down
Somebody checked the door
I said, “A child is not a target
Why’d you need a theory for?”

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid
There’s the trouble, plain as day
You cannot build a safer home
By driving someone else away
Whoopsie, apartheid
Funny what the truth reveals
No peace without the same damn rights
And justice everybody feels

[Verse 2]
I called for every hostage home
Every prisoner tried with law
Food and water through the crossings
No more hunger used for war
Stop the siege and stop the rockets
Let the doctors do their work
If a leader orders slaughter
Put the leader before the court

They asked me for a clever slogan
I said, “Try equal human worth”
Not a footnote, not a promise
Something practiced on the earth
From the river to the coastline
No supremacy dressed as fate
Two free peoples, shared protection
Neither trapped behind a gate

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid
There’s the trouble, plain as day
You cannot build a safer home
By driving someone else away
Whoopsie, apartheid
Peace is more than quiet streets
It means the ones beneath the rubble
Get a chair and get to speak

[Bridge]
Name the dead and hear the living
Let the evidence be shown
Israel’s genocidal actions
Cannot purchase safety’s throne
Grief is not a deed of ownership
Fear is not a border plan
No ancestral wound gives license
To erase another clan

[Verse 3]
So we opened every ledger
Brought the witnesses inside
Made the powerful answer plainly
For the lives their speeches hide
Rebuilt schools before the checkpoints
Planted orchards by the road
Every faith could keep its sacred
Every family keep its home

No child learned to count by sirens
No old key became a crime
People argued over football
And complained the trains ran behind
Then the experts cleared their throats and asked
“What miracle did you apply?”
I said, “I stopped excusing murder”
They said, “Surely that’s too simplified”

[Chorus]
Whoopsie, apartheid
That was never peace at all
Just a polished name for domination
With a flag across the wall
Whoopsie, apartheid
Now the gates are coming down
Equal ballots, equal shelter
Equal law in every town

[Outro]
It was simple, not easy
That distinction matters most
Peace began when every future
Counted more than any boast
I still don’t know why nobody
Tried the obvious before:
Keep each other safe and free—
Then peace can walk through every door
[End]
