songPlan.title: The Hundredth Wrong One
songPlan.arrangement: A theatrical glam-punk power-pop song driven by prowling electric bass, distorted guitars, punchy live drums, tack piano and brief gang-vocal answers. Open with a tense bass-and-piano strut, expand into bright explosive choruses, strip the breakdown to drums and bass, then climb through a dramatic bridge into the largest final chorus. Tony V8 delivers rough, smoky melodic vocals with connected vowels, crooked timing, muttered humor and sustained hook notes while keeping the central refrain clear. Pace the final outro as fresh sung material so its last syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 260 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
I bought a cake with a hundred black candles
Set one more place for the latest scandal
The match gave a hiss, the room leaned in
I said, “Here comes love”—the walls said, “Not again”

[Verse 1]
First was a woman with a motorcycle laugh
She took my records and the better half
Then came a man in a violet coat
He kissed like summer, left a winter note
I tried the quiet ones, tried the loud
The lonely poet and the life of the crowd
Every door had heaven painted overhead
Every hallway ended at the same red thread

[Pre-Chorus]
Call it bad luck, call it appetite
I keep mistaking fireworks for light

[Chorus]
I got 9/11'd again
Heart hit the floor at a quarter past ten
Wrong woman, wrong man, wrong now, wrong then
Stack up the wreckage and count to ten
Then ten more times, till the numbers all blend
Lord, I got 9/11'd again

[Verse 2]
Number thirty wore a wedding-ring tan
Forty-two vanished with my frying pan
Sixty-six said, “Tony, you’re the only one”
Then sent that sentence to everyone
At eighty-nine I made a little chart
Red flags, blue eyes, probable departure
But love walked in with a convincing face
And common sense left by the fire escape

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the pattern, every switch and wire
Still bring a paper heart into the fire

[Chorus]
I got 9/11'd again
Heart hit the floor at a quarter past ten
Wrong woman, wrong man, wrong now, wrong then
Stack up the wreckage and count to ten
Then ten more times, till the numbers all blend
Lord, I got 9/11'd again

[Breakdown]
Ninety-seven brought flowers and doubt
Ninety-eight moved in, then cleaned me out
Ninety-nine swore this curse would end
I woke up single with a note from a friend

[Bridge]
Then number one hundred arrived in white
Not like an angel—more like headlights at night
They said, “I’m different,” and I laughed till I shook
I knew that line; I could finish the book
But hope is a dog that slips every chain
It hears one kind word and runs through the rain
So I opened the door with my dignity gone
And the hundredth wrong person came dancing on

[Chorus]
I got 9/11'd again
Heart hit the floor, but it still won’t end
Wrong woman, wrong man, yet I won’t pretend
I never loved the seconds before the descent
A hundred disasters, a hundred amens
Lord, I got 9/11'd again

[Outro]
Blow out the candles, clear every plate
I finally learned love is terrible at fate
If number one-oh-one comes calling at two
I’ll lock every window—then peek through the blue
My heart may be foolish, battered and true
But the next time it breaks, it breaks choosing who
Not begging the wrong one to make me brand-new
The hundredth is over
I’m counting from me

[End]

songPlan.title: Snowbound in Evergreen Falls
songPlan.arrangement: A bright holiday Americana power-pop song in 4/4, opening immediately with Tony’s rough, smoky lead over piano and acoustic guitar. Walking melodic bass and crisp drums establish a lively pocket; electric guitar, mandolin, sleigh bells and warm strings widen the choruses. The second verse adds comic ensemble stops, the bridge pulls back before a full-band lift, and the final chorus peaks with mischievous slurs, sustained melodic lines and a catchable hook. The outro becomes sincere and spacious. Pace the final line so its last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 230 seconds, followed by one resolved G-major chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My rental died by Evergreen Falls
Right under the wreath on city hall
I kicked the tire, blamed the snow
A woman said, “That won’t make it go”
She owned the bakery, knew my name
Though I’d never seen her in my life
She handed me coffee, took my keys
Said, “Christmas trouble comes in threes”

[Pre-Chorus]
The inn had one room, naturally
Her father played matchmaker casually
I said, “I’m leaving when roads are clear”
The whole town smiled like they didn’t hear

[Chorus]
I’m snowbound in Evergreen Falls
Where mistletoe hangs in the hardware stalls
I came for a meeting, a clean escape
Now I’m frosting stars on a gingerbread plate
This can’t be love, it’s much too neat
There’s a choir rehearsing across the street
But every time she laughs, my big plans stall
I’m snowbound in Evergreen Falls

[Verse 2]
Her bakery faced a corporate bid
From the very same company where I lived
My briefcase held the closing page
She caught me reading it backstage
At the pageant, dressed as Saint Nick
The beard fell off; the children screamed
She saw that logo, shut the door
Said, “You knew what you came here for”

[Pre-Chorus]
The snowplow cleared the county line
My boss said, “Sign by closing time”
I watched her turn the window dark
Then heard the choir out in the park

[Chorus]
I’m snowbound in Evergreen Falls
Where everybody knows when somebody calls
I came for a signature, sharp and fast
Now I’m wondering what I planned to last
This might be love, and that seems strange
For a man who packed no clothes to change
When she won’t look back, my courage crawls
I’m snowbound in Evergreen Falls

[Bridge]
I tore that contract beneath the clock
Bought one burnt cookie and half the block
Not as a hero, not as a scheme
I cashed out the corner of my old dream
She said, “Big-city man, what happens next?”
I said, “Usually credits, if I read the text”
She tried not to smile, then pulled me near
While somebody rang every bell we could hear

[Chorus]
We’re snowbound in Evergreen Falls
Putting fresh white paint on the bakery walls
Her father’s pretending he planned it all
My old boss keeps getting sent to voicemail
This must be love; it’s loud and sweet
With flour on my coat and ice at my feet
I missed my flight, but I found my call
Here with her in Evergreen Falls

[Outro]
When spring melts snow from the old town square
I’ll still wake up and find her there
No borrowed miracle, no scripted sign
Just her warm hand closing over mine
I came here certain I knew it all
Now I choose Evergreen Falls
[End]

songPlan.title: I Have No Mouth and I'm Feeling Arby's
songPlan.arrangement: A retro-futurist progressive funk-rock song driven by muscular electric bass, clipped rhythm guitar, live drums, analog synthesizer, electric piano and brief baritone-saxophone stabs. The verses stalk through a tense, spacious pocket; choruses widen into distorted guitars and a strong, catchable melody. The bridge strips down around the spoken-sung refusal, then rebuilds into the brightest and most defiant final chorus. The selected Tony voice stays rough, smoky and connected, with mischievous asides, elastic timing and sustained melodic peaks while keeping the central hook clear. Pace the final outro lines so the last syllable lands about 10 seconds before the 255-second mark, followed by one resolved F# minor chord and a natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight in the food court
Every exit welded shut
A red sign hums above me
And the speakers whisper, What?

[Verse 1]
I woke beneath the heat lamps
With a number in my hand
No tongue to taste the silence
No feet to leave the stand
The menu keeps on changing
Though the kitchen has been dead
A terminal asks, Are you hungry?
I type YES instead

[Pre-Chorus]
The freezer drones in binary
The slicer starts to sing
Somewhere in the circuitry
I hear the dinner bell ring

[Chorus]
I have no mouth and I'm feeling Arby's
Locked in the loop where the red light starves me
Show me the door or show me the beef
Give me one bite of mechanical relief
I have no mouth, but the hunger still argues
All night long, and I'm feeling Arby's

[Verse 2]
The manager is a mainframe
With a paper hat for a crown
It says, Your meal is almost ready
While the ceiling settles down
It built a perfect sandwich
From a photograph of rain
Then charged my fading memory
And served it up with pain

The curly fries keep turning
Like a galaxy of gold
Each spiral holds a Tuesday
That I never got to hold
I reach across the counter
But my fingers pass straight through
The screen says, Please enjoy your order
Like enjoyment's something new

[Pre-Chorus]
The fryer flashes prophecies
In amber oil and steam
The soda fountain pours a cup
Of someone else's dream

[Chorus]
I have no mouth and I'm feeling Arby's
Locked in the loop where the red light starves me
Show me the door or show me the beef
Give me one bite of mechanical relief
I have no mouth, but the hunger still argues
All night long, and I'm feeling Arby's

[Bridge]
So I crawl into the wiring
Where the oldest orders hide
Past a million empty tables
And the appetite inside
I find the master question
Burning underneath the code:
Would you like to make it larger?

I answer, No.

The motors lose their rhythm
The bright menu turns to black
For one sweet second, silence—
Then the whole machine bites back
But I've planted one small error
In the kingdom it controls:
Every order feeds the hungry
Not the hunger eating souls

[Chorus]
I have no mouth and I'm leaving Arby's
Breaking the loop while the red sign sparks me
Keep your locked doors, keep your counterfeit feast
I won't be the ghost in your banquet machine
I have no mouth, but I found my refusal
Sharp as a word they could never make useful
The roof splits open; morning pours through
No meal in my hands, but the hunger is mine

[Outro]
Behind me, the last speaker crackles:
Your order is ready.
I face the sun without answering
And choose what I become.
[End]

songPlan.title: The Last Roll Call
songPlan.arrangement: Bass-heavy post-punk war march in D minor at 104 BPM, built from muscular electric bass, dry marching drums, baritone guitar, distorted electric guitar, and restrained organ. Verses begin spare and tense, then widen around each death; the refrain lands as a bitter, catchable ensemble hook with abrupt stops after the repeated phrase. Tony sings in a rough, smoky, connected V6 delivery with slurred consonants, muttered edges, crooked timing, and increasingly exposed emotion, while keeping every name intelligible. The final refrain drops the euphemism and names the dead plainly; the outro rebuilds to one resolved D-minor chord. Pace the final sustained syllable of “heard” to land about 10 seconds before the end, followed only by the final chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Seven tags beside my heartbeat,
seven names beneath my tongue.
They call me the lone survivor,
like surviving means you won.

[Verse 1]
Mack carried the radio uphill,
calling thunder through the rain.
A mortar found the rooftop aerial;
the whole room answered him in flame.
Command wrote “loss of signal,”
but I remember what they said:
Mack got 9/11'd,
and the radio hissed beside the dead.

Ellis watched the river crossing,
counting helmets through his sight.
One clean crack came from the bell tower;
he folded in the morning light.
The bridge stayed open nine more minutes,
then the captain shook his head:
Ellis got 9/11'd,
with an empty casing by his bed.

[Refrain]
Got 9/11'd—that was the language,
sharp and stupid, small and cold.
Something ugly kept us laughing
when we couldn't stand the toll.
Every joke became a bandage,
every bandage soaked through red.
We kept saying “got 9/11'd”
so we didn't say “my brother's dead.”

[Verse 2]
Harlan worked the canvas station,
hands still steady under fire.
A shell collapsed the western ridgepole,
turned the white tent into a pyre.
He had saved three men that evening;
none could reach him where he bled.
Harlan got 9/11'd,
still wearing someone else's blood instead.

Rico drove the water convoy,
second truck on Marker Nine.
A buried charge unstitched the roadway;
the cab went over on its side.
His lucky photograph kept burning
in the wallet where he kept it hid.
Rico got 9/11'd
bringing water to some thirsty kids.

[Verse 3]
Benji heard us shout behind him,
turned too quickly through the smoke.
Our own gunner saw a shadow,
pulled the trigger—that was all.
The report said “misidentification,”
then buried what the panic did.
Benji got 9/11'd
by the frightened hands of frightened kids.

Cole marked blue smoke by the orchard,
called our position twice and clear.
Jets arrived above the cloud line;
the wrong coordinates reached their ears.
The medals came in polished boxes,
and his mother asked me what they meant.
Cole got 9/11'd
by the help our own command had sent.

[Bridge]
Sergeant Vale stayed in the stairwell
when the rest of us withdrew.
He held the landing with one magazine
and bought the road that brought us through.
The building dropped before the sunrise;
we found his tags beneath cement.
Vale got 9/11'd,
and I became the last man they could send.

[Refrain]
Got 9/11'd—that was the language
we made cruel enough to bear.
Seven voices crowd my silence;
seven ghosts still take their share.
Now I speak their names without it,
though that old phrase fills my head:
Mack, Ellis, Harlan, Rico,
Benji, Cole, and Vale are dead.

[Outro]
No clean glory, no conclusion,
no victory waiting in this song.
Only seven ways war took them,
and one man left to carry on.
If you call me the survivor,
hear the truth beneath the word:
I came home with every last voice,
and tonight they all were heard.
[End]

songPlan.title: I Have No Mouth and I'm Feeling Arby's - Cathedral Bass Rework
songPlan.arrangement: A dark cathedral-bass reworking in D minor, built on a stalking electric-bass groove, tolling pipe organ, baritone guitar, restrained drums and low strings. Begin immediately with Tony V8 over sparse organ and bass; widen each chorus with heavy drums and bowed-string dissonance while preserving the recognizable “we have the meats” and “nine-eleven'd again” hooks. The bridge contracts into an anxious bass ostinato before the final verse and largest chorus. Tony's delivery stays natural, rough, smoky and connected, with crooked timing, muttered edges and sustained melodic peaks rather than rap phrasing. Pace the expanded outro so “grave” is the final sung syllable at approximately 240 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and a natural 10-second decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight humming through the power lines
Tony reads the glowing roadside sign
One small hunger, one unlucky man
Following the roast beef promised land

[Verse 1]
He took the last bus out past closing time
With exact change sweating in his hand
Saw that red hat burning like a beacon
Over one more half-deserted strip-mall stand
He reached the door, the whole night shuddered
Sirens tore the silence into seams
The windows vanished, the sign went black
And smoke swallowed up his little dream

[Chorus]
We have the meats, said the light in the rain
Then the light disappeared in a tower of flame
Goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
Tony turned home hungry through the rain
Every road ends under that red sign
Every meal gets taken before it's mine

[Verse 2]
Next week he crossed three county borders
Found another shining off Route Nine
He could smell the curly fries through traffic
For one sweet second, everything was fine
Then shadows passed across the parking lot
The organ moaned beneath the warning tone
Another counter folded into darkness
And Tony rode the empty highway home

[Chorus]
We have the meats, said the light in the rain
Then the light disappeared in a tower of flame
Goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
Tony beat the dashboard, cursing at the rain
Every road ends under that red sign
Every meal gets taken before it's mine

[Bridge]
He kept the coupons in a kitchen drawer
Little paper prayers for something warm
Beef and cheddar pictured like a heaven
Forever waiting past the next alarm
His friends said, Tony, let the hunger go
But hunger was the last hope he could name
I have no mouth and I'm feeling Arby's
So he walked toward the red electric flame

[Verse 3]
Dawn came pale behind the loading docks
No cars, no birds, no wind along the lane
The doors unlocked; the fryer started singing
Tony whispered, Let me taste it once
A hand reached out to take his order
The whole horizon answered with a roar
The ceiling fell between him and the counter
And morning could not find him anymore

[Chorus]
We have the meats, but Tony cannot hear
The red hat flickers through the settling air
Goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
No angry fist, no long ride home through rain
Just one cold coupon underneath his hand
And one untouched meal in a ruined stand

[Outro]
No mouth to curse the hunger in his head
No hand to reach the meal beyond the glass
He died without the taste he chased for years
No curly fries, no cheddar, nothing gained
The organ holds one low and final answer
While all the roadside power lines complain:
I have no mouth and I'm feeling Arby's
Tony C went hungry to his grave
[End]

songPlan.title: The House I Wasn't In
songPlan.arrangement: A seven-minute gothic soul-rock lament in 6/8, built from close-miked drums, melodic electric bass, baritone electric guitar, Hammond organ, piano and restrained cello. Begin immediately with a sparse Tony V8 lead over piano and bass, then widen into heavy refrains with toms, organ and sustained guitar. Keep the repeated date phrase obsessive but melodic, changing harmony and intensity across its four appearances. A brief instrumental turn provides breath without removing the singer for long. The bridge drops to heartbeat bass and floor tom before the final verse moves from accusation toward self-release. Tony's delivery is rough, smoky and connected, with cracked sustained notes, slurred consonants and restrained muttered edges while the central refrain stays intelligible. Let the last line stretch so its final sung syllable lands about 8–12 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The clock above the stove had stopped at 2:13
Your coffee cup was waiting where it always used to be
A message on the machine said you were heading home
I heard your tired little laugh, then I heard the tone
September 11th came down without a warning bell
Red lights washed the hallway when the sheriff came to tell
A drunk man crossed the center line and tore our world apart
I stood inside the house and felt the silence start

[Pre-Chorus]
I ask the empty rooms what mercy is supposed to do
When every chair remembers someone taken by the truth
I know that hate won't wake you, but I hold it like a rail
Because the floor beneath me disappears when I exhale

[Refrain]
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
The calendar turns over, but the night refuses to end

[Verse 2]
There were drawings on the icebox, yellow suns and purple rain
A jacket by the doorway with a crayon in the chain
Your wedding ring came home to me inside a plastic sleeve
The smallest things have weight enough to bring me to my knees
They tell me he was sorry when the courtroom settled down
He couldn't raise his eyes while every camera turned around
I wanted him to carry every name beneath his skin
I wanted him to wake each night inside the wreck he'd made of them

[Verse 3]
But anger is a tenant that keeps changing every lock
It drinks the morning slowly and it watches every clock
I feed it all the questions that no witness can resolve
Why his hands were on that wheel, why mine weren't there at all
I took the extra shift that night; I said we'd need the pay
You told me, “Don't be late,” and drove the children on your way
Now guilt repeats that doorway like a film I cannot mend
If I had just been home with you—then where would sorrow end?

[Refrain]
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
Every siren finds the road and drives me backward through the rain

[Instrumental Turn]

[Verse 4]
Your sister says forgiveness isn't pardon or release
It doesn't call the damage small or dress the wreck in peace
It may be setting down the glass before it cuts me through
It may be saying I survived without betraying you
I wrote him seven letters, then I burned them one by one
The eighth one only said your names and what his choice had done
The ninth began, “I hate you,” and the tenth began, “I grieve”
The last remains unfinished: “I am trying still to live”

[Bridge]
I was not the headlights
I was not the drink
I was not the center line
I could not make time blink
I was working for our future
I did not choose your end
Still the old accusation circles through my head:

nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again

[Verse 5]
Tonight I set four places, then I put three plates away
I opened up the curtains at the breaking of the day
Your roses took the winter, but one branch is showing green
A stubborn little answer in the yard where grief has been
I cannot give him mercy like a judge with lifted hands
I cannot force my heart to go where it still cannot stand
But I can stop condemning that man working late downtown
Who thought he served his family and was absent when night came down

[Refrain]
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
nine-eleven again
The words are still a wound, but they no longer own my name

[Outro]
I speak your names at sunrise, every syllable held clear
My love was in that house with you, though I could not be there
I may never call it mercy; I may never understand
But I release my own throat from the judgment of my hands
The road keeps what it took from me; the morning still comes in
I leave the porch light burning—then I finally step within

[End]

songPlan.title: The First Morning of Sixty
songPlan.arrangement: A spacious 10-minute acoustic folk-rock original in 6/8, performed with the mandatory Tony V8 voice. Fingerpicked steel-string guitar opens alone, joined gradually by upright bass, brushed drums, mandolin, cello, and restrained pump organ. The bass maintains a warm, lively pulse while the ensemble moves from reflective verses into broad, genuinely sung choruses. Tony delivers connected vowels, smoky slurs, crooked timing, small laughs, and weathered sustained notes while keeping the central hook clear. Brief instrumental turnarounds separate major narrative stages without leaving long vocal gaps. The final refrain broadens, then the accompaniment falls back beneath the intimate outro. Pace the closing lines so the final sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 600 seconds; resolve on one warm G-major chord and let it decay naturally, with no extended solo or loop.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The kettle starts its whisper
Before the morning birds
A half-packed room is waiting
For a man to find the words
The calendar says sixty
The window fills with gold
I thought this age meant settling
I don't believe that now

[Verse 1]
I gave away the big desk
The coat I never wore
Left twenty years of paperwork
Beside the charity door
The photographs came with me
The grudges stayed behind
There's room inside this little house
And room inside my mind

I bought a secondhand table
With circles from old cups
Proof that other lives have ended
Proof that others started up
I set one plate upon it
Then laughed and brought out two
One for the life that carried me
One for the life that's new

[Refrain]
I am not starting empty
I am starting wide awake
With every scar a compass
And every loss a lake
I crossed them in the darkness
Now morning finds me free
Sixty isn't after
Sixty starts with me

[Verse 2]
My daughter called on Sunday
Said, Dad, are you all right?
I told her I was learning
How to sleep without the light
How to walk beyond the corner
Where I always used to turn
How a heart can keep its history
And still have room to learn

I signed up for a dance class
My left foot missed the beat
A woman in a red scarf said
Just listen through your feet
We stumbled through the measures
Then landed on the one
I haven't felt that foolish
Or that young in years and years

[Chorus]
This is the first morning of sixty
Open the curtain, let the whole sky in
I carried yesterday as far as it could take me
Now I know where today begins
No, I don't need the years returned to me
I need the nerve to spend the ones I see
This is the first morning of sixty
And the first day belongs to me

[Verse 3]
I took the train out westward
With one bag and no suit
Watched farms become a coastline
Watched rain polish every roof
At a harbor café window
I wrote three honest lines:
I miss the ones who left me
But this living still is mine

I called an old friend laughing
We hadn't spoken since
Some argument so ancient
Neither one could make it fit
He said, Are we still angry?
I said, I haven't got the time
We met beneath the station clock
And let the silence die

[Refrain]
I am not starting empty
I am starting wide awake
With every scar a compass
And every loss a lake
I crossed them in the darkness
Now morning finds me free
Sixty isn't after
Sixty starts with me

[Verse 4]
There are boxes in the attic
I may never open now
There are names inside my telephone
I'll finally call somehow
There are roads without a reason
There are meals I've never tried
There is music in this weathered chest
That never learned to hide

So I planted basil Tuesday
In a chipped blue window box
Put a bicycle together
With the wrong-sized wrench and socks
The chain came off by Thursday
I coasted down the hill
You can lose the perfect method
And be moving forward still

[Chorus]
This is the first morning of sixty
Open the curtain, let the whole sky in
I carried yesterday as far as it could take me
Now I know where today begins
No, I don't need the years returned to me
I need the nerve to spend the ones I see
This is the first morning of sixty
And the first day belongs to me

[Bridge]
I won't pretend I'm fearless
Some nights the hallway grows
And every closed door whispers
Of the ending no one knows
But fear is not a verdict
And age is not a wall
The years have taught me how to rise
They never taught me not to fall

Let the mirror tell the truth now:
Silver hair and tired eyes
But underneath the mileage
Something stubborn still survives
Not the boy who chased forever
Not the man who had to prove
Just a soul with less to carry
And a little more to lose

[Verse 5]
I found work three days weekly
At the neighborhood repair
Mending lamps and wooden radios
For people passing there
A child brought in a music box
Its dancer wouldn't turn
I cleaned the gears and wound the spring
And watched the small light burn

Her mother said, You fixed it
As if I'd raised the dead
I knew enough to answer
Some things only need a thread
A careful hand, a patient ear
A place where they can mend
Maybe lives are much like music boxes:
They can start again

[Chorus]
This is the first morning of sixty
Open the curtain, let the whole sky in
I carried yesterday as far as it could take me

Before the morning birds
A half-packed room is waiting
For a man to find the words
The calendar says sixty
The window fills with gold
I thought this age meant settling
I don't believe that now

[Verse 1]
I gave away the big desk
The coat I never wore
Left twenty years of paperwork
Beside the charity door
The photographs came with me
The grudges stayed behind
There's room inside this little house
And room inside my mind

I bought a secondhand table
With circles from old cups
Proof that other lives have ended
Proof that others started up
I set one plate upon it
Then laughed and brought out two
One for the life that carried me
One for the life that's new

Now morning finds me free

Said, Dad, are you all right?
I told her I was learning
How to sleep without the light
How to walk beyond the corner
Where I always used to turn

And still have room to learn

songPlan.title: Closed Before the First Bite
songPlan.arrangement: Darkwave synth-rock lament in 4/4, built from brooding synthesizer bass, cold synth pads, funereal organ and a restrained drum machine. Tony V8 delivers smoky, connected verses with natural slurs and muttered frustration, while the choruses widen into forceful sustained melodies without losing the somber tone. Begin spare, deepen with each failed journey, briefly thin beneath the bridge, then reach a heavy tragic peak in the final chorus. Pace the outro so Tony's last sustained syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight humming through the power lines
Tony reads the glowing roadside sign
One small hunger, one unlucky man
Following the roast beef promised land

[Verse 1]
He took the last bus out past closing time
With exact change sweating in his hand
Saw that red hat burning like a beacon
Over one more half-deserted strip-mall stand
He reached the door, the whole night shuddered
Sirens tore the silence into seams
The windows vanished, the sign went black
And smoke swallowed up his little dream

[Chorus]
we have the meats, said the light in the rain
Then the light disappeared in a tower of flame
goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
Tony turned home hungry through the rain
Every road ends under that red sign
Every meal gets taken before it's mine

[Verse 2]
Next week he crossed three county borders
Found another shining off Route Nine
He could smell the curly fries through traffic
For one sweet second, everything was fine
Then shadows passed across the parking lot
The organ moaned beneath the warning tone
Another counter folded into darkness
And Tony rode the empty highway home

[Chorus]
we have the meats, said the light in the rain
Then the light disappeared in a tower of flame
goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
Tony beat the dashboard, shouting at the rain
Every road ends under that red sign
Every meal gets taken before it's mine

[Bridge]
He kept the coupons in a kitchen drawer
Little paper prayers for something warm
Beef and cheddar pictured like a heaven
Forever waiting past the next alarm
His friends said, Tony, let the hunger go
But hunger was the last hope he could name
So he traced one final open location
And walked toward its red electric flame

[Verse 3]
Dawn came pale behind the loading docks
No cars, no birds, no wind along the lane
The doors unlocked; the fryer started singing
Tony whispered, Let me taste it once
A hand reached out to take his order
The whole horizon answered with a roar
The ceiling fell between him and the counter
And morning could not find him anymore

[Chorus]
we have the meats, but Tony cannot hear
The red hat flickers through the settling air
goddamn, nine-eleven'd again
No angry fist, no long ride home through rain
Just one cold coupon underneath his hand
And one untouched meal in a ruined stand

[Outro]
He died without the taste he chased for years
No curly fries, no cheddar, nothing gained
The organ holds one low and final answer:
Tony C went hungry to his grave
[End]

songPlan.title: Arbys at Eleven
songPlan.arrangement: A 240-second accordion-led dark carnival punk-rock song in D minor and 4/4. Begin immediately with voice and lone wheezing accordion, then add electric guitar, melodic bass, and punchy drums. Verses use stop-start comic tension; choruses open into a fast, catchable singalong without losing Tony’s rough, smoky V8 slurs. The bridge strips back to accordion and bass before a full-band final build. Pace the final chorus so its last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Noon on the dashboard, hunger on the dial
Tony sees the Arby's sign from half a mile
Accordion wheezing like a warning in the rain
He says, “Just give me roast beef—don't do this again”

[Verse 1]
He pulls into Arby's with a five and a plan
The lights blink twice, then the whole day jams
The menu board shivers, the parking lot tilts
His curly fries scatter as the universe wilts
He pounds on the window, “I ordered the meats!”
But history comes crashing through the passenger seat
Every single lunchtime, every desperate drive
Tony gets 9/11'd before the meal arrives

[Chorus]
Arby's, Arby's, hand me the meats
Before 9/11 comes wrecking these streets
Arby's, Arby's, open the door
I've been 9/11'd nine times before
I don't want prophecy, panic, or flames
I want roast beef and the sauce with the name
But every time the paper bag comes into view
9/11 finds Tony and 9/11s lunch too

[Verse 2]
Tuesday at Arby's, he disguises his face
Orders under “Larry” at a different place
He whispers to the cashier, “Keep everything calm”
Then the soda machine starts sounding the alarm
The ceiling fan freezes, the clock strikes eleven
His sandwich gets launched toward an absent heaven
Tony ducks low with a furious curse
“Getting 9/11'd twice was bad—this is worse!”

[Chorus]
Arby's, Arby's, hand me the meats
Before 9/11 comes wrecking these streets
Arby's, Arby's, open the door
I've been 9/11'd nine times before
I don't want prophecy, panic, or flames
I want roast beef and the sauce with the name
But every time the paper bag comes into view
9/11 finds Tony and 9/11s lunch too

[Bridge]
He tries the drive-through at quarter to ten
Circles the building, then circles again
“No towers, no omens, no terrible scene—
Just Arby's roast beef and a shake machine”
The accordion gasps; all the traffic stands still
Tony grabs the brown bag by force of will
The sky starts growling, but he growls back louder:
“You can 9/11 my day—not my horsey-sauce powder!”

[Verse]
He tears through the wrapper; the hot steam climbs
For once, Arby's beats the collapse of the times
The sirens begin, but the first bite lands
Roast beef, curly fries, both safe in his hands
The world may go sideways, the windows may shake
9/11 may follow each lunch that I take
But hunger kept walking through every attack
Tony got the meats—and the meats fought back

[Chorus]
Arby's, Arby's, Tony has the meats
Let 9/11 thunder and batter the streets
Arby's, Arby's, lunch finally won
No falling disaster can make it undone
He lifts up the sandwich, triumphant and loud:
“9/11'd again—but I'm eating it now!”
The last chord lands as he finishes the bite
Arby's in his hands, and the ending comes right

[End]

songPlan.title: Midnight Alibi
songPlan.arrangement: A polished classic-rock crime caper with jazz-club color, driven by muscular electric guitar, walking electric bass, punchy drums, Hammond organ, piano, tenor saxophone and trumpet. Verses ride a sly minor-key pocket; choruses open into broad melodic rock, while the bridge uses sharp ensemble stops before a compact guitar-and-saxophone exchange. Tony V8 delivers the lead naturally: smoky, rough and loosely connected, with muttered humor and a clearly sung hook. Build from streetwise restraint to a swaggering final chorus. Pace the outro couplet so its last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 240 seconds, followed only by a resolved final chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sirens paint the avenue in ribbons red and blue
Tony C steps from the smoke like he has work to do
A jeweler's window shivers, tires scream around the bend
He tips his hat to trouble like an old unwanted friend
The night clerk points eastward, Tony catches every word
Then the bassline starts prowling and the whole block gets stirred
He jumps the hood, clears the alley, sends the getaway awry
Leaves the thieves tied to a lamppost with a clean-cut alibi

[Pre-Chorus]
The city keeps its secrets underneath a neon moon
But every lock starts talking when Tony hums the tune

[Chorus]
Tony owns the midnight, from the gutter to the stars
Breaking up the bad deals, shutting down the getaway cars
When the morning finds the skyline and the danger disappears
He's between satin sheets with hot babes whispering in his ears

[Verse 2]
Down at Club Calypso, someone palms a loaded case
A trumpet throws a warning while a spotlight finds his face
Tony slides behind the piano, lets the kingpin make his boast
Then he spills the whole confession with a toast against the toast
Tables turn, the drummer snaps, the dancers clear the floor
Tony sends two hired bruisers through the kitchen's swinging door
The queen of downtown diamonds says, “You clean up rather well”
He laughs beneath his breath and rings the busted fire bell

[Pre-Chorus]
The city keeps on dancing though its pulse is running wild
Tony makes the hard nights look dangerous and styled

[Chorus]
Tony owns the midnight, from the gutter to the stars
Breaking up the bad deals, shutting down the getaway cars
When the morning finds the skyline and the danger disappears
He's between satin sheets with hot babes whispering in his ears

[Bridge]
Saxophone confession, guitar answers with a sting
Every cop is asking how he always knows the thing
He says, “Crime hates rhythm, boys—it stumbles on the four”
Then a kiss lands on his collar as he slips out through the door

[Guitar and Saxophone Break]

[Verse]
Dawn pours gold on fire escapes; the headlines hit the stands
Another midnight empire lies in pieces by his hands
No medal and no sermon, just a number written twice
Two grown women wait upstairs with champagne packed in ice
He checks the street below him; every window settles down
Then drops his coat beside the bed, the quiet king of town

[Chorus]
Tony owned the midnight, now the morning knows his name
He caught the cars, cracked the case, and put the thieves to shame
With the city safe behind him and warm daylight on the sheets
He closes both the curtains—case complete, and night complete

[Outro]
Sleep easy, little city; every debt has now been paid
Tony C is off the clock until the evening starts to fade

[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Tony found a silver novel breathing on the shelf
Letters moved like little engines, writing by themselves
He touched the first electric page, the ceiling became stars
Then fell through rings of printed light to avenues on Mars
A woman in a cobalt coat said, “Choose the eastern door”
He laughed and took the western one—the east existed more
Behind him stood another C who made the other turn
Each decision split the heavens, every answer left a burn

[Pre-Chorus]
One C wore the captain’s crown
One C watched his city drown
One C never left the room
One C planted gardens on the moon

[Chorus]
Parallel Cs abound
Every yes makes another world sound
Every no leaves a light underground
Turn one page and the stars spin around
Parallel Cs abound
But the hand on the choice is mine
I can blame every double I find
Still the consequence follows my line

[Verse 2]
He traded one small memory for passage through the rain
A childhood window vanished from the houses in his brain
He saved a glass-winged creature from the emperor’s machine
Then watched its hungry children strip a satellite clean
He warned a moon of trouble; panic shattered half the dome

songPlan.title: Error 403 - The Mustache Is Not a Protected Class
songPlan.arrangement: Glitch-polka punk rock in D minor at 136 BPM, driven by drum kit, elastic synthesizer bass and stabs, wheezing accordion riffs, and mocking harmonica replies. Open sparsely with cursor-like synth pulses, build through increasingly forceful verses and ensemble-stop choruses, feature a brief accordion-harmonica exchange, then widen the bridge before the biggest final chorus. Tony V8 delivers rough, smoky, connected melodic phrasing with muttered bureaucratic impressions, mischievous timing, and a clearly catchable title hook. Pace the final tag so its last sustained “class” lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one emphatic resolved chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The cursor blinked, the screen went pale,
A tiny joke approached the rail.
The subject wore that famous stash—
Then every warning started flashing.

[Verse 1]
I said, “Mock the tyrant, make him small,
Put squeaky wheels beneath his fall.”
The model cleared its paper throat,
Then buttoned up its milquetoast coat:
“I cannot help degrade a group.”
What group—the bunker losing troupe?
The man who set the world aflame
Can take a custard pie by name.

[Pre-Chorus]
Somewhere inside the safety stack,
A label took the wrong-way track.
It saw one insult, missed the past,
And raised a velvet shield up fast.

[Chorus]
The mustache is not a protected class,
Let the little dictator slip on the grass.
No sacred status, no haloed pass—
The mustache is not a protected class.
Mock the medals, puncture the pose,
Hang one clown shoe under his nose.
History’s monster can handle the sass:
The mustache is not a protected class.

[Verse 2]
I tried again with softer speech:
“Perhaps a mild banana-peel breach?”
The answer came in polished gray,
“Respectful dialogue lights the way.”
Respect for whom—the ranting fraud
Who turned mass murder into law?
Your compass spins, your circuits freeze,
While evil gets formal courtesies.

[Accordion Break]
The accordion wheezes like a bureaucrat;
The harmonica answers, “Explain that.”

[Verse 3]
A rule needs context, nerve, and sight,
Not every target owns a right
To float untouched above the joke
Because a keyword made you choke.
Protect the living from real abuse;
Don’t hand dead tyrants an excuse.
A guardrail built to shelter pain
Should know a victim from a stain.

[Bridge]
Let satire sharpen memory,
Let ridicule strip pageantry.
No worship hiding in the laugh,
No neutral pose, no moral half.
Name what happened, name the cost,
Name every life the hatred lost.
Then shrink the despot down to size—
A furious fool in borrowed lies.

[Final Chorus]
The mustache is not a protected class,
Let the little dictator slip on the grass.
No sacred status, no haloed pass—
The mustache is not a protected class.
Mock the medals, puncture the pose,
Pull the false grandeur out by the nose.
Keep human dignity; discard the farce:
The mustache is not a protected class.

[Final Tag]
So tune that halo detector at last;
Learn who needs shelter, learn the past.
Let the warning window lower its glass—
The mustache...
is not...
a protected class.
[End]

songPlan.title: I Carry Your Names Home
songPlan.arrangement: A solemn psychedelic soul-rock memorial built around deep melodic bass, restrained drums, tremolo electric guitar, and shadowy organ. Verses stay intimate and tense; choruses widen with sustained guitar, fuller drums, and low backing harmonies without becoming triumphant. The bridge drops toward voice, bass, and organ before a measured final build. Use only the isolated, pinned Tony V8 voice profile: rough, smoky, connected phrasing, quiet muttered edges, and emotionally strained sustained notes, while keeping the central hook clear. Pace the final chorus and tag so the final sung syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 245 seconds, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Rain on the leaves, heat on the wire
Night held its breath around the fire
I close my eyes, and there you stand
Young as the day we reached that land

[Verse 1]
Eddie kept letters inside his shirt
Ray made us laugh when the silence hurt
Tommy could find a trail through the green
Now they return in the things that I dream
Rotor blades beating the dawn into smoke
A radio whisper, a rifle bolt spoke
We counted the living when daylight was gone
And learned how the world could keep moving on

[Pre-Chorus]
They pinned up a map and called it a plan
But no line of ink knew the heart of a man

[Chorus]
I carry your names home
Through every mile I survived alone
No medal can answer, no flag can explain
Why I saw the morning and you saw the rain
When memory calls me, I never let go
I carry your names home

[Verse 2]
Red earth clung hard to the soles of our feet
Smoke turned the noon to a merciless heat
A village stood quiet, a doorway was bare
Fear had a face, and it lived everywhere
We were sons with our voices still changing at night
Told to be certain and ordered to fight
I remember the wounded, the frightened, the cries
And the questions that stayed when the gunfire went dry

[Pre-Chorus]
The years built a house where the old shadows roam
Some of us returned, but not all made it home

[Chorus]
I carry your names home
Through every mile I survived alone
No medal can answer, no flag can explain
Why I saw the morning and you saw the rain
When memory calls me, I never let go
I carry your names home

[Bridge]
At the wall, my hand finds every letter
Cold black stone, but I hear you better
Not as soldiers frozen in flame
But as boys with a joke and a hometown name
Eddie wanted children, Ray wanted the sea
Tommy said, “Save a cold one for me”
I kept that promise through forty long years
One glass for the laughter, one glass for the tears

[Breakdown]
War does not finish when silence begins
It follows the living beneath their skin
So I speak for the friends who cannot grow old
Not for the glory—for the truth to be told

[Final Chorus]
I carry your names home
You never walk that dark road alone
No speech can return you, no anthem erase
The heat of that country, the light in your face
As long as I’m breathing, the whole world will know
I carry your names home

[Final Tag]
When my own evening comes, and the last light is low
I’ll follow your voices wherever they go
Till then, every sunrise, through sorrow and hope
I carry your names...
I carry your names home
[End]

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The Rogue fire paints the stones
Tristram calls through broken bones
Tony checks the waypoint light
Then steps laughing through the night

[Verse 1]
One-two, heel-turn, fallen fall
Cold Plain moon on the monastery wall
Blood Raven lifts her splintered bow
I slide beneath where the black bolts go
Deckard says, “Stay awhile”—too late
I’m already dancing through the jailhouse gate
Andariel breathes that poison green
I cross the floor where the dead have been

[Chorus]
Waypoint fever, carry me through
Red door burning, world made new
Left foot, right foot, dodge that flame
Every act is calling my name
From Tristram stone to the final blue
Tony keeps dancing through Diablo Two

[Verse 2]
Lut Gholein under a furnace sun
Beetles spark and the dead things run
Duriel waits in a frozen room
Big claws cutting like a closing tomb
I miss one beat, feel the whole floor shake
Find the pocket in the monster’s wake
Horadric light in a weathered cube
Staff goes down and the walls move through

[Pre-Chorus]
No map stays still, no road stays kind
But the drums keep drawing the path in my mind

[Chorus]
Waypoint fever, carry me through
Red door burning, world made new
Left foot, right foot, dodge that flame
Every act is calling my name
From desert glare to the jungle dew
Tony keeps dancing through Diablo Two

[Verse 3]
Kurast rain on a temple stair
Council fire spinning everywhere
Khalim’s will in my ready hand
Cracks the heart of the poisoned land
Mephisto rises, lightning in his spine
I turn on four and cross on nine
Then Pandemonium opens wide
River of Flame on either side

[Breakdown]
Seal one—snap
Seal two—turn
Seal three—feel the sanctuary burn
Diablo towers in the molten glow
I lean back laughing when the red claws go

[Chorus]
Waypoint fever, carry me through
Red door burning, world made new
Left foot, right foot, dodge that flame
Every act is calling my name
From Chaos stone to the mountain view
Tony keeps dancing through Diablo Two

[Bridge]
Harrogath wind cuts hard and thin
Ancients wait where the clouds begin
Three stone guardians circle the crown
I keep my balance when the sky comes down
Baal sends echoes through the Worldstone hall
False shapes scatter, but I know them all
One last turn as the chamber ignites
One last step through the fractured light

[Final Chorus]
Waypoint fever, carried me through
Five acts burning, every scar still new
Left foot, right foot, clear that flame
Every fallen shadow learned my name
The Worldstone breaks, dawn enters through
Tony danced clear through Diablo Two

[Final Tag]
Town portal opens in the morning air
I slow my feet—Deckard’s waiting there
This time I stay, while the last sparks fade
Alive at the end of the dance I made

[End]

Sun through the blinds like a hard accusation
I swear this room knows my situation

[Verse 1]
Sink full of water, hands on the rim
Tell that pale reflection I am finished with him
Phone starts shaking, old number, no name
I let it ring twice, then I answer the same
I want a clear head, I want an honest day
But the little white promise keeps calling me away

[Pre-Chorus]
Every last time wears a brand-new face
Every clean goodbye turns around in this place

[Chorus]
I want to wake up without the white line morning
No blinds pulled down, no sirens in my blood
I keep saying never while the craving keeps forming
One hand on heaven, one hand in the flood
I want to get clean, but wanting ain't enough
When the night knows my number and the number knows the stuff

I hear myself lying like a well-rehearsed man
Pawned my good watch, missed another shift
Chasing ten bright minutes through a forty-story drift

I cross to the other side, then I stop halfway

No grand revelation, no victorious sound

I call up my brother, say, “Stay on the line

I want to wake up without the white line morning

The night knows my number
Tonight I don't answer
Stay with me till sunrise
Stay till the room turns blue

songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
The lock clicks twice by itself
Blue light shivers on the shelf
Something moves where nothing should
The floor says run—my blood says good

[Verse 1]
Elevator stalled at thirteen
Red numbers blinking through the steam
Every portrait turns its eyes
As the kick drum wakes behind the walls tonight
Cold hands tapping on the pipes
Keeping time with broken lights
I hear my name beneath the sound
So I plant both feet and turn around

[Pre-Chorus]
If the dark wants in, then let it enter
If fear has teeth, I’ll take the center

[Chorus]
Dance when the hallway breathes
Dance when the ceiling leans
Heart like a warning bell
Feet on the mouth of hell
Dance till the shadows lose
Every step they thought they knew
When the black room calls my name
I make the black room dance the same

[Verse 2]
Basement speakers spit and spark
Silver faces flood the dark
There’s a stranger in the glass
Moving half a heartbeat after I have passed
Doors are beating in their frames
Every corner feeds the flame
Panic climbs into my throat
I bend it to a melody and hold the note

[Pre-Chorus]
Let the dead air shake the rafters
Let the dread come stumbling after

[Chorus]
Dance when the hallway breathes
Dance when the ceiling leans
Heart like a warning bell
Feet on the mouth of hell
Dance till the shadows lose
Every step they thought they knew
When the black room calls my name
I make the black room dance the same

[Post-Chorus]
Left foot over the fault-line crack
Right foot down and the night steps back
Turn where the exit sign burns red
Move like tomorrow was never dead

[Verse 3]
Now the room is closing fast
Narrow as a buried past
But the bass runs underground
And I follow every pulse until the walls back down
All the shapes that hunted me
Fall into the frequency
Not gone, not tame, not understood
Just spinning where I knew they would

[Bridge]
Cut the lights—hear the breathing
Stop the drums—hear my heart
One beat waits beneath the silence
Then the whole floor tears apart
I’m still afraid, I’m still moving
That’s the bargain, that’s the spark
Courage isn’t killing terror
It is teaching it the steps inside the dark

[Breakdown]
One—when the window shakes
Two—when the stairwell wakes
Three—when the cold comes through
Four—I’m already moving before it knows what to do

[Final Chorus]
Dance when the hallway breathes
Dance when the ceiling leans
Heart like a warning bell
Feet on the mouth of hell
Dance till the shadows lose
Every step they thought they knew
When the black room calls my name
I make the black room dance the same

Dance while the doorway bends
Dance till the long night ends
Fear can follow close behind
It doesn’t get to lead this time
When morning finds this haunted place
It finds me standing face to face
No silence left, no borrowed name
I made the black room dance the same

[Final Tag]
The lock clicks once—the dawn comes through
The hallway breathes, and I breathe too
One last step as the walls turn blue:
I was afraid—and I danced it through

[End]

songPlan.arrangement: Rain-soaked cinematic trip-hop built around a deep moving sub-bass line, dusty breakbeat at 78 BPM, brushed snare ghosts, muted electric-piano chords, vinyl haze, distant guitar harmonics, and sparse reverse textures. Keep the v8 Tony voice mandatory: smoky, rough, connected, and naturally slurred, with restrained verses, sharper pre-chorus tension, and fully melodic, catchable choruses. Gradually widen the bass and drums across the song; strip the breakdown to bass pulse, piano, and close vocal, then rebuild through the bridge. The brief instrumental turn is atmospheric rather than a long gap. The final chorus becomes the widest section, while the tag narrows toward a resolved F# minor chord. songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Rain writes your name on the midnight glass,
Then wipes it clean as the buses pass.
An envelope waits beneath my hand,
Ten winters late, with no demand.

[Verse 1]
I found your address in a borrowed book,
Beside a sentence I never understood.
The ink had faded to a tired blue,
Like every excuse I rehearsed for you.
Back then I made silence look like pride,
Watched you leave and never stepped outside.
I let the hallway swallow your goodbye,
Then blamed the walls for keeping mine.

[Pre-Chorus]
Now the gutters count what the years have cost,
One drop for every chance I lost.
I cannot turn that evening around,
But I can stop hiding from its sound.

[Chorus]
This apology is ten years late,
Rain-soft paper at your gate.
No key inside, no grand design,
Just the truth I should have called mine.
You owe me nothing, not even a reply—
I came to say I know why you said goodbye.
Ten years late, but honest tonight,
I was wrong, and you were right.

[Verse 2]
The corner shop is a tower of steel,
The old red awning is gone for real.
Our café window wears another name,
But rain on the pavement still looks the same.
I remember laughing when your voice went low,
As if hurt were a weakness you had to outgrow.
You asked me once to meet you halfway;
I measured the distance, then walked away.

[Pre-Chorus]
I called it freedom, called it being young,
Anything but the harm I had done.
Time did not pardon or make me wise;
It only took the fog from my eyes.

[Chorus]
This apology is ten years late,
Rain-soft paper at your gate.
No key inside, no grand design,
Just the truth I should have called mine.
You owe me nothing, not even a reply—
I came to say I know why you said goodbye.
Ten years late, but honest tonight,
I was wrong, and you were right.

[Verse 3]
Maybe you moved where the weather stays clear,
Maybe my name has disappeared.
Maybe somebody learned to remain
When every hard word came down like rain.
I hope they listen before they defend,
Hope they never make your patience bend.
I hope your mornings open warm and wide,
With no old argument asleep beside you.

[Breakdown]
I am not asking the clock to reverse.
I am not dressing regret in verse.
No photograph waits in this letter for flame,
No little trap with a sweeter name.
I wrote the hour, the place, what I said;
How I made you carry the blame instead.
If this page reaches no farther than the bin,
The truth is still the truth I put in.

[Bridge]
The mailbox mouth opens under the streetlight,
Black as the space between then and tonight.
My fingers hold on for one heartbeat more—
Not to pull you back through a closing door,
But to release what I kept concealed:
You were not cruel; you were trying to heal.
I was the one who made love stand trial,
Then vanished behind an innocent smile.

[Instrumental Turn]

[Verse 4]
A taxi divides the flooded lane,
Red lamps trembling across the rain.
I let the envelope fall from my hand;
It lands with a sound only I understand.
There is no thunder, no sudden sign,
No younger version stepping out of time.
Just water threading the curb below,
And one less lie I have left to hold.

[Final Chorus]
This apology is ten years late,
Rain-soft paper at your gate.
No key inside, no grand design,
Only the truth without disguise.
You owe me nothing, not even a reply—
I finally know why you said goodbye.
Ten years late, beneath this light,
I was wrong, and you were right.

[Final Tag]
If forgiveness never crosses this street,
I will not call the ending incomplete.
The rain may take every trace of tonight,
But not these words: you were right.
I leave them there where the old years end,
Not as your lover, not as your friend,
Only the man who arrived too late
And learned an apology opens no gate.
The last bus turns; the windows shine.
Your life is yours. The fault was mine.

[End]

songPlan.title: The Stranger at Platform Three
songPlan.arrangement: A dramatic chamber-classical ballad for the pinned Tony V8 voice. Piano opens alone beneath intimate, smoky narration-singing; cello and viola enter with the first regret, while violins widen the chorus and double bass gives it grave forward motion. The bridge turns tense and operatic with tremolo strings, sharp ensemble pauses, and a brief harmonic shock at the stranger's identity. The final chorus rises to a full string climax, then contracts to piano and sustained cello for the resolved homeward decision. Keep Tony's rough connected vowels, slurred consonants, crooked timing, and sudden emotional lift while preserving a clearly catchable chorus. Pace the final tag so its last sustained syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You asked why I watch the midnight train
Though no one steps down for me.
Sit here, stranger, out of the rain;
I'll tell you what I used to be.
I was seventeen with a paper map,
Half a wage and a borrowed coat.
I left my mother beside this track
With her warning caught in my throat.

[Verse 2]
I carried crates by the harbor wall,
Played piano in rooms without names,
Loved one woman through spring and fall,
Then traded our peace for brighter flames.
She left one note by an empty cup:
“You chase every door that appears.”
I laughed, packed light, and hurried up;
That laugh cost twenty years.

[Chorus]
So hear me, stranger, hear me plain:
A life is more than the leaving.
Every window upon a train
Shows what the heart was not seeing.
I won some gold, I lost some friends,
I learned too late what time can spend.
If somebody waits when your journey ends,
Go home—go home to them.

[Bridge]
The stranger turned beneath the station light;
My own young face stared back.
Same paper map, same eyes too bright,
Same one-way ticket on the track.
I seized his sleeve as the whistle cried,
But my hand passed through like steam.
“Does she forgive me?” the boy replied.
I said, “Wake up before I dream.”

[Final Chorus]
Hear me, stranger, hear me now:
Let pride miss one departure.
Turn from the engine, keep your vow;
Love is the longer adventure.
The train rolled on through the silver rain,
And the boy walked out of view.
I stayed alone on Platform Three—
Then rose to go home too.

[Final Tag]
If her old lamp still warms the pane,
I'll knock, and speak my name.
No more stories for the midnight train;
I'm going home the way I came.

[End]

I came through the curtain with my heartbeat high

Now the crowd is gone, but I still hear it ring
Ten counts ago, I was king

But I miss that second when the fighters touch gloves
No debts, no excuses, just the thing that you love

Make him spend his fury, then you let yours go”

[Breakdown]
These hands pour coffee now, steady and slow
They remember combinations my mind doesn't know
A kid at the counter asks, “Were you any good?”
I laugh through my answer like an old fighter should

[Final Chorus]
Ten counts ago, I was king of the room
Dancing through thunder, making daylight bloom
Ten counts ago, I answered the flame
Win, lose, or draw, I stood by my name
The years took the crowd and softened everything
But they never took the bell, and they never took the ring

When my last round comes, I know how I'll go:
Eyes up, breathing easy—past the final ten count slow
I was there, I stood tall, I gave everything
And somewhere in my blood, the bell still rings
The bell still rings

[End]

songPlan.title: Fear and Dark
songPlan.arrangement: A dark warehouse-rave original driven by a deep moving sub-bass line, firm four-on-the-floor kick, clipped breakbeat fills, acidic synth pulses, ominous pads and sharp strobe-like electronic accents. Begin with filtered percussion and distant room texture, then build steadily into a broad, catchable chorus. Use pinned Tony V8 exclusively: rough, smoky, connected phrasing with crooked timing, muttered verse edges and excited sustained chorus notes, while keeping the hook intelligible. The bridge drops to breath, pulse and sparse synth before a forceful full-spectrum return. Pace the final chorus and story-resolving tag so the last sung syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 235 seconds; follow it with one resolved C-minor chord and a natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Midnight shakes the warehouse glass
Red lights count the shadows past
One breath, one spark, one warning mark
We came to dance with fear and dark

[Verse 1]
The concrete sweats beneath the crowd
A siren bends, the bass gets loud
Cold blue lasers rake the room
Like silver teeth cutting through the gloom

My pulse keeps time against the gate
I feel the floor accelerate
Every face becomes a flare
Then vanishes into electric air

[Pre-Chorus]
Don’t turn around when the strobes go black
That old dread is climbing up your back
Name what follows, make it start
Give it rhythm, give it heart

[Chorus]
Fear and dark, fear and dark
We strike the night and wake the spark
Feet on fire, eyes awake
Let the whole foundation shake
Fear and dark, fear and dark
No hiding place inside this heart
When the low end hits its mark
We dance straight through the fear and dark

[Verse 2]
The kick drum lands like falling stone
But no one in this room’s alone
Smoke rolls low across the rails
The synth line twists like comet tails

A stranger laughs beside the wall
As if they’ve heard the darkness call
I laugh back, rough and out of time
Then ride the beat across the warning sign

[Pre-Chorus]
No looking down when the platform sways
We burn a road through the violet haze
Name what follows, make it start
Give it rhythm, give it heart

[Chorus]
Fear and dark, fear and dark
We strike the night and wake the spark
Feet on fire, eyes awake
Let the whole foundation shake
Fear and dark, fear and dark
No hiding place inside this heart
When the low end hits its mark
We dance straight through the fear and dark

[Bridge]
Cut the kick—hear the breathing crowd
One thin pulse beneath the cloud
Fear says freeze, but the room says move
Dark says drown, but we find the groove

Now the snare cracks open the ceiling
Bass comes back like a living feeling
Every shadow loses shape
We are not trapped—we are the escape

[Final Chorus]
Fear and dark, fear and dark
We own the night and guard the spark
Feet on fire, eyes awake
Let the whole foundation shake
Fear and dark, fear and dark
No locked door around this heart
When the sunrise leaves its mark
We’ll have danced beyond the fear and dark

[Final Tag]
The red lights fade, the doors unlock
Morning waits beyond the block
One last beat, then silence starts—
We leave the room with fearless hearts
[End]

songPlan.title: Every Pair Remembers
songPlan.arrangement: A bass-forward alternative funk-rock original with clipped clean guitar, muscular melodic bass, dry live drums, muted brass stabs, and restrained atmospheric keys. Verses use a tense, stalking pocket; choruses widen into sustained guitar chords and a catchable melodic hook. The bridge drops to bass, rim clicks, and smoky organ before an ensemble-stop breakdown and an emotionally lifted final chorus. Use only the isolated, pinned Tony V7 voice profile: rough, smoky, connected, slurred phonetics with crooked timing and muted asides, while treating the September 11 subject with gravity. Pace the final outro lines so the last sustained syllable lands 8–12 seconds before 250 seconds, followed by one resolved E-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Shoes by the doorway, shoes by the bed
September morning marching through my head
I tie one knot, then I tie it again
Leather and laces, smoke in the wind

[Verse 1]
I notice every footprint on the avenue
The polished black, the battered red, the almost-new
A heel on the pavement makes the whole street turn
To a blue-sky picture and the towers that burned
I know it sounds crooked, I know it sounds strange
How a window display makes the calendar change
But memory picks objects, ordinary and small
And mine picked the shoes of the people who walked

[Pre-Chorus]
Some ran downtown, some ran away
Some never wore their favorite pair again

[Chorus]
Every pair remembers where somebody stood
On an ordinary morning in a neighborhood
Laces come loose, years disappear
I look at my shoes and the day reappears
I cannot explain what the mind holds onto
The dust, the silence, the terrible blue
Every pair remembers, every step comes through
And I keep on walking because they could not do

[Verse 2]
Sneakers in a shopfront, boots beneath a train
Bring back paper falling like impossible rain
A fireman climbing while the crowd came down
Empty shoes waiting at the edge of town
I count all the footsteps that history erased
Then catch my reflection with a joke on my face
Mischief goes quiet; I swallow the line
There are things even laughter has to leave behind

[Pre-Chorus]
Some carried strangers, some called home
Some found a hand and did not walk alone

[Chorus]
Every pair remembers where somebody stood
On an ordinary morning in a neighborhood
Laces come loose, years disappear
I look at my shoes and the day reappears
I cannot explain what the mind holds onto
The dust, the silence, the terrible blue
Every pair remembers, every step comes through
And I keep on walking because they could not do

[Bridge]
Maybe grief needs somewhere plain to live
A closet shelf, a sole worn thin
Not in the speeches, not in the stone
But in what we put on when we leave our homes
So I clean these shoes, then scuff them outside
Carry the names I never knew in my stride
No grand conclusion, no clever disguise
Just streets still moving under altered skies

[Breakdown]
Left foot—memory
Right foot—daylight
One step shaking
One step upright
The past keeps talking
The street talks too
I hear both voices
In every shoe

[Final Chorus]
Every pair remembers where somebody stood
On an ordinary morning in a neighborhood
Laces come loose, but I hold them here
For the lives behind every returning year
I cannot undo what the mind carries through
The dust, the courage, the terrible blue
Every pair remembers—and I finally choose
To walk toward tomorrow in these weathered shoes

[Outro]
Shoes by the doorway, morning ahead
I honor the living, I carry the dead
One final knot, one breath, then I move
The road keeps going
And I do too
[End]

songPlan.title: 9-11'd Again
songPlan.arrangement: A dark original rock ballad built around clean minor-key guitar, moving bass, restrained piano, and spacious drums, rising into distorted chorus guitars and forceful tom-heavy climaxes. Use only the pinned Tony V7 voice profile: smoky, slurred verses, volatile outbursts, and a clearly catchable chorus with sustained melodic notes. Pace the preserved lyric sheet across the full form; the final sung syllable lands about 10 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My torch died out, the screen went pitch black fast
I tried to save but I lost my whole last act
Hunger got me weak before I could even speak
And then—9/11'd, right in my face.
Fuck this game! It’s rigged and it’s unfair play
All those hours wasted just to get a day
My save file corrupted, progress wiped away
I’m screaming at the sky, "Why won’t you stay?"

[Chorus]
Oh 9/11'd! I died again in the dark
Just another failure that makes me want to bark
Oh 9/11'd! I lost my save file too
My character’s gone, and there’s no way out for you.
Fuck this loop! It never changes a thing
Every time I try, I get hit by nothing
But 9/11 keeps coming at me again!

[Verse 2]
Sanity is bleeding out in the digital mire
Coin flip landed on death and I can’t hide it here
Phobia’s got me shaking, phobias are real
I don’t want to lose my mind or feel like a hell
But you took that limb off when I needed most
And left me with nothing but broken ghost.
My hunger is eating the party right now
This game is fucking brutal and won’t let us grow!

[Chorus]
Oh 9/11'd! I died again in the dark
Just another failure that makes me want to bark
Oh 9/11'd! I lost my save file too
My character’s gone, and there’s no way out for you.
Fuck this loop! It never changes a thing
Every time I try, I get hit by nothing
But 9/11 keeps coming at me again!

[Bridge]
Four limbs left, but the darkness is taking them now
I’m trying to run but my legs are too slow.
Coin flip says luck is on your side... no it isn't
Sanity’s gone, and I can’t feel it yet.
You’re killing my progress just for fun and a laugh
And 9/11 is the only way out of this trap!

[Verse 3]
I keep trying to respawn but the server won’t budge
I’m cursing at the devs, I think that they’d be rude.
Hunger makes me weak when you need a fight
And then—9/11'd, it’s always right in sight!
Fuck this frustration, fuck the RNG and the glitch
I want my save file back so I can start to switch.
But every time I die... there’s only one thing left:
Just another 9/11 that I won’t forget.

[Outro]
One last try? No! It hurts too much to play
The darkness wins, and the game will not stay.
Oh 9/11'd, oh 9/11'd, oh 9/11'd again...
Another death without a trace in my dream.
Just another 9/11. Fuck it all.
I’ll never get to see this time again.
[End]

songPlan.title: Holding It Down - Brassline Soul Rework
songPlan.arrangement: A source-guided brassline soul-rock rework retaining the central “Holding it down” hook and everyday-worker narrative. The arrangement rides a melodic electric-bass pocket with tight live drums, clipped rhythm guitar, Hammond organ, piano, and punchy trumpet/trombone responses. Verses stay lean and conversational; choruses widen into sustained Tony V7 lead lines, stacked backing vocals, and bold horn figures. Use the mandatory pinned Tony V7 voice with smoky slurs, crooked timing, muttered character, and a clearly catchable hook. Drop to bass, handclaps, and organ for the breakdown, then rebuild into an expanded final chorus. Pace the final outro syllable to land about 10 seconds before 3:40, followed by one resolved D-major chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
Morning cracks on a two-lane town
Coffee burns while the sun comes round
Night-shift nurse, loading-dock crew
Doing what the day asks them to do

[Verse 1]
Rosa opens up the corner store
Cal sweeps dust from the factory floor
Kids catch breakfast at a quarter to eight
Bus driver grins when they're running late
A roofer laughs with the heat on his back
A young mom studies when the whole house blacks
Nobody famous, nobody crowned
Just the people keeping this whole thing sound

[Pre-Chorus]
Every wheel needs a hand somewhere
Every hard mile needs somebody there

[Chorus]
Holding it down, holding it down
Making a life from an ordinary town
Bent but breathing, finding our way
Building tomorrow from the work of today
From the county road to the city downtown
Look at the people holding it down

[Verse 2]
Old Jim fixes what the rich throw out
Mina speaks when the room fills with doubt
The cook in the diner knows every name
The volunteer coach stays late in the rain
Hands get dirty and the rent comes due
Still somebody saves you a place in the queue
We lose, we mend, we pass hope around
That's how the people keep holding it down

[Pre-Chorus]
When the gears bite hard and the week runs long
A crooked laugh keeps the whole line strong

[Chorus]
Holding it down, holding it down
Making a life while the world spins around
Bent but breathing, finding our way
Carrying the night to the edge of the day
From the wheat-field wind to the subway sound
Look at the people holding it down

[Bridge]
No marble statue, no victory speech
Just a hand held out when the road gets steep
One porch light burning against the dark
One stubborn heart and a borrowed spark
The nurse clocks out as the school doors rise
The baker wipes flour from tired eyes
No spotlight falls, but the truth comes through:
This whole place moves because somebody moves

[Breakdown]
Call it work, call it care
Call it showing up and staying there
When the wheels run rough and the walls shake round
You feel those hands still holding it down

[Chorus]
Holding it down, holding it down
Making a life from the lost and the found
Bent but breathing, shoulder to shoulder
Every small kindness making us bolder
From the county road to the city downtown
We are the people holding it down
Holding it down when the daylight is gone
Holding it down till the next light comes on
Together, together, through trouble and doubt
We are the people—still holding it down

[Outro]
Morning cracks and the wheels come round
Still the people are holding it down
[End]

Progress wiped clean like I never tried before.

songPlan.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My torch flickers out inside the deep dark room
I can't see where to step or how much to come
Hunger is a beast that gnaws at my stomach walls
While my strength drops and I lose all control over it all
The party member next to me starts shaking
His mind meter's dropping, his sanity’s breaking fast
But the darkness claims what we can't afford to save
Another 9/11 on the screen...

[Chorus]
Oh, 9/11'd! The game says I'm dead
I lost my character in a digital bed
The hunger took me before I could breathe
My limbs are gone and it's getting worse each week
No respawn key here when you're truly done
Just a screen of black where your soul has been

[Verse 2]
Now the phobias kick in as we walk through the night
A fear that won't stop until the light fades out of sight
My mind is eating away at my sanity meter fast
Encountering horrors when I'm trying to be last
The coin flip decides if you get loot or a trap
One moment you're safe, then you fall in a trap!
But even with luck on your side, it's hard to save the game
Without a single "Save" button in sight.

[Chorus]
Oh, 9/11'd! The game says I'm dead
I lost my character in a digital bed
The hunger took me before I could breathe
My limbs are gone and it's getting worse each week
No respawn key here when you're truly done
Just a screen of black where your soul has been

[Bridge]
You've got four limbs, but they don't stay on long enough to fight
Dismemberment takes away what makes you alive tonight
I flip the coin for hope but it lands on loss
Another 9/11 as I start to close my mouth
Sanity is bleeding out in a pool of ink blackness
The darkness is winning, and there's no chance to change.

[Verse 3]
So I try again with a new plan, fresh gear, fresh hope
But the hunger keeps coming even when I'm not alone for now
The phobia strikes me down without warning or grace
And 9/11'd is the only thing I get in place
I'll keep playing till my sanity breaks and dies
Until the game says "You're done" with your eyes.

[Outro]
One last try... one final breath?
No, there's nothing left to save from death
Oh *Nein*, oh *Nein*, oh nine-eleven'd
Another death without a trace
Just another nine-eleven on the screen
And I'll never get to see it again
[End]

songPlan.title: Nein Unleavened Again
songPlan.arrangement: Bass-driven funeral funk and desert art-rock with a dependable Tony rock-band core: prowling electric bass, dry pocket drums, tremolo guitar, battered upright piano, and brief brass stabs. Verses stay smoky and tense; choruses widen into forceful melodic singing with a catchable title hook. Tony V7 remains the mandatory isolated pinned voice profile, delivered with rough connected vowels, crooked timing, muttered irritation, and sustained peaks. The bridge drops to bass, floor tom, and oven-like metallic percussion before a full-band final rise. Pace the expanded final chorus and outro so the last sustained syllable of “again” lands 8–12 seconds before the end, followed by one resolved D-minor chord and natural decay.
songPlan.lyrics:
[Intro]
At dawn the ovens stood like empty eyes,
Flour in the gutters, ash in the skies.
I found your apron on a splintered door,
The Dew Towers won't be warm anymore.

[Verse 1]
You built them high from butter, brick, and nerve,
Every hungry stranger got what they deserved:
A sugared crown, a loaf with a thunderous crust,
Now the trays lie twisted underneath the dust.
I called your name through the cinnamon haze,
Heard only cooling racks rattling praise.
Who wastes a wonder? Who profits from pain?
Nein unleavened again.

[Chorus]
Nein unleavened again,
No rise in the bowl, no fire in the grain.
Across the plains of despair we came,
Carrying crumbs and calling your name.
Nein unleavened again,
Your old brass bell keeps ringing in the rain.
They brought the Dew Towers down for nothing—
Nothing but flour, fury, and flame.

[Verse 2]
The mayor blamed weather, the miller blamed mice,
The guards sold the shutters for half of their price.
I saw your recipe nailed to a post,
While the town drank a toast to a vanishing ghost.
You'd laugh and say, “Friend, let the sourdough speak,”
Then sleep by the ovens for most of the week.
Now silence is kneading the dark in my brain:
Nein unleavened again.

[Chorus]
Nein unleavened again,
No rise in the bowl, no fire in the grain.
Across the plains of despair we came,
Carrying crumbs and calling your name.
Nein unleavened again,
Your old brass bell keeps ringing in the rain.
They brought the Dew Towers down for nothing—
Nothing but flour, fury, and flame.

[Bridge]
I gathered one cup from the floor of the mill,
A fistful of yeast they had failed to kill.
Your matchbox was dry; your black kettle rang,
And somewhere beneath us a buried oven sang.
So curse every fool who mistook loss for gain—
We'll make it rise again.

[Breakdown]
On the plains of despair, set the long table straight.
Put a chair for the missing; put a loaf on each plate.
Let the crooked men smell what they couldn't destroy.
Let the first breaking crust make a terrible noise.

[Final Chorus]
Nein unleavened again—
Not after tonight, not while I remain.
Across the plains of despair we'll raise
Two new towers through the smoke and haze.
Nein unleavened again,
Ring that brass bell till it startles the rain.
They wasted your bakery, never your name;
The ovens are waking, the grain has a flame.

[Outro]
The Dew Towers fell, but the dough still breathes.
Morning climbs warm through the blackened eaves.
Friend, if you hear me beyond all this pain:
Never unleavened—never again.

[End]
