lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Ba-da, mm-ba-dah, window hummin’ low
Autumn got its cold hands everywhere I go

[Verse 1]
Morning on the radiator, barely any heat
Brown leaves scratch a crooked rhythm down the empty street
Coffee tastes like yesterday, daylight’s wearing thin
Old coat on the chair asks where the hell I’ve been
My knees predict the weather, my mirror tells the years
I laugh and call it wisdom, then swallow down the fear
Cats are in the kitchen, plants lean toward the gray
Both of them keep watching like they know I’ll go away

[Pre-Chorus]
Do-ba, dee-ba, time moves slow
Every room gets bigger when there’s nowhere else to go

[Chorus]
Who’s gonna care for my cats and plants
If I lose this tired old dance?
Who’ll turn the pots toward the afternoon
And feed those little fools beneath the moon?
Cold Autumn days, don’t close on me
I still got sparks where no one sees
Sheeeet, ya feel me? I ain’t through
There’s a little green left pushing through

[Verse 2]
Hospital on Monday, plastic bracelet tight
Fluorescent constellations buzzing through the night
Doctor said the word cancer, soft and practiced-clean
One cold syllable cutting through the humming machine
I stared out at the parking lot, rain across the glass
Counted every red tail light and watched the hours pass
Nurse brought me a blanket, said, “Let tomorrow come”
I scatted at the ceiling—bap-ba-daa—and tapped my thumb

[Pre-Chorus]
Mm-da, broken tune, don’t quit
If the heart can miss a doorway, it can find another bit

[Chorus]
Who’s gonna care for my cats and plants
If I lose this tired old dance?
Who’ll know the tabby hates closed doors
Or catch the ivy crawling on the floors?
Cold Autumn days, don’t close on me
I still got sparks where no one sees
Sheeeet, ya feel me? I ain’t through
There’s a little green left pushing through

[Bridge]
Then I dreamed a magic vaccine
Gold as October, bright and strange
It didn’t promise forever
Just one good season’s change
One more supper by the window
One more paw against my hand
One more chance to water roots
And tell somebody where I stand

[Breakdown]
Ba-rum, ba-ray, hear that old heart knock
Crooked little drummer with a busted pocket watch
I called my neighbor Rosie, gave her keys and wrote things down
Not a will of surrender—just some love passed around

[Final Chorus]
We’re gonna care for these cats and plants
We’ll keep alive this stubborn dance
She’ll turn the pots toward afternoon
I’ll feed those little fools beneath the moon
Cold Autumn days can call my name
I’ll answer rough, but I’ll answer just the same
Sheeeet, ya feel me? Here’s what I know
Love is who you teach to help things grow

[Outro]
The first frost shines, the room turns gold
I’m lonely, yes—but not alone
Ba-da, mm-ba-dah, soft and low
I close the window, keep the warm light on

originalPrompt.idea: Tony C scats about the loneliness of old age and the cold Autumn days
originalPrompt.keep: Must include a hospital visit, cancer, and a magic vaccine. Who's gonna care for my cats and plants? Sheeeet, ya feel me?

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Streetlamp glow on the avenue
Five hearts humming, making room for you

[Verse 1]
She does the work, she carries the day

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
He learned to keep the weather locked behind his teeth
Carry every failure where nobody could see
No hand on his shoulder, no language for the ache
Just a glowing little kingdom saying, Brother, stay awake
They sold him iron answers in a midnight feed
A villain for his loneliness, a throne for every need
Said love was just a market and mercy made you weak
But anger sounds like purpose when you haven't been heard in weeks

[Pre-Chorus]
He wasn't born a weapon
He was looking for a name
For the hollow in the hallway
For the rules without a game

[Chorus]
They say, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
We'll give you back the crown they stole
A code, a cause, a role
But every promise gets smaller
When every wall gets taller
You can't build a life by shutting the whole world out
Try that in a small town

[Verse 2]
He wanted work that mattered, friends who'd call him first
A father who could tell him what to do with all the hurt
A chance to be desired without performing like a king
Some proof that being useful wasn't worth more than being seen
The screen supplied a brotherhood with targets painted red
Easy little certainties to tuck him into bed
Said tenderness was surrender, and doubt was a disease
Then charged another payment for the secret to be free

[Pre-Chorus]
There was truth beneath the sales pitch
Men are starving to belong
But a wound becomes a business
When the cure keeps it raw

[Chorus]
They say, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
We'll give you back the crown they stole
A code, a cause, a role
But every promise gets smaller
When every wall gets taller
You can't build a life by shutting the whole world out
Try that in a small town

[Bridge]
You can lift the weight, learn the trade
Keep your word and still be afraid
You can want respect without demanding control
You can lose, you can grieve, you can ask what you need
Without making an enemy feed your soul
No guru owns the doorway
No stranger holds the key
Brotherhood ain't worship
And strength ain't cruelty

[Breakdown]
Tell me what was missing
A table, a teacher, a place in the crowd?
Tell me what they promised
A kingdom where pain could never speak aloud?
I won't laugh at the hunger
I won't kneel to the lie
A man can need another man
And look him in the eye

[Final Chorus]
They said, try that in a small town
Stand tall, never back down
But nobody needs a stolen crown
To turn his whole life around
Let every promise grow larger
Let every open door start here
Build a life with people, not a bunker made of fear
If the town is worth defending
Let compassion make it strong
There is room beside the fire
You were needed all along

[Outro]
No throne, no target, no final score
Just hands rebuilding what the hurt tore
Say what you need, let the old walls fall
A stronger man can answer when his brothers call

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro]
Dis is Tony C, from da troof? And yaw washin sessunz, ahhh Ay-oh-el, thank you very mush

[Verse 1]
Miss June keeps coffee by the screen door
Eddie knows which engine needs a hand
Kids leave their bicycles by the corner
Like trust is something everybody understands
When thunder knocks the county power sideways
Flashlights bloom from every kitchen drawer
Nobody waits to hear a stranger calling
We're already walking out the door

[Pre-Chorus]
One porch wakes another
One name travels down the line
You don't face the dark alone here
Not tonight, not any time

[Chorus]
Every porch light on, every curtain drawn
Open eyes from dusk until the dawn
If trouble comes around pushing folks apart
It meets a row of neighbors and a stubborn town heart
No fists, no fear, just a thousand little ties
Meals on the table and the truth against the lies
Every porch light on, shining strong
Around here, looking out is how we all belong

[Verse 2]
Old Ray brings a toolbox to the widow
Nina drives the night-shift workers home
Sam knows every dog and every grandchild
And who has been too proud to ask for help alone
When a slick voice starts a crooked bargain
Passing poison underneath a smile
We bring it into daylight at the courthouse
And stand beside each other all the while

[Pre-Chorus]
One hand finds another
One truth travels down the line
You don't face the wolves alone here
Not tonight, not any time

[Chorus]
Every porch light on, every curtain drawn
Open eyes from dusk until the dawn
If trouble comes around pushing folks apart
It meets a row of neighbors and a stubborn town heart
No fists, no fear, just a thousand little ties
Meals on the table and the truth against the lies
Every porch light on, shining strong
Around here, looking out is how we all belong

[Industrial Break]
Hammer on the rail, sparks against the rain
Boots across the gravel, calling every name
Lock the shop together, walk the long way home
Trouble loses power when nobody stands alone

[Bridge]
We don't need a hero on a billboard
We need soup when someone's paycheck's gone
A spare-room bed, a ride, a witness
Someone staying when the sirens move along
And if hate comes selling easy answers
We'll answer with the lives we've woven tight
You can rattle every gate along the main road
But you cannot turn our mercy off tonight

[Final Chorus]
Every porch light on, let the whole street glow
Every lonely soul has somewhere safe to go
If trouble comes around pushing folks apart
It meets a living wall made of an open heart
No fists, no fear, we remember every name
Drive the trouble out by starving out its game
Every porch light on, and the morning coming strong
Around here, looking out is how we all belong

[Outro]
The mill bell rings, the shadows withdraw
June pours coffee as the sunrise warms the wall
Door by door, we kept the promise through the night
Town waking whole beneath the fading porch light

lyrics.text:
[Intro - Low Tony, spoken]
Funny how a fence looks tall
Till both sides have to mend it.

[Verse 1 - Country Tony]
I wake up with the grain trucks rolling
Coffee black and the radio low
Boots by the door, screen needs fixing
Same old road everywhere I go
You pulled in with the bass line shaking
City plates and a midnight coat
I made up a story before you spoke one
You read my silence like a warning note

[Pre-Chorus - Country Tony]
We were drawing hard lines in borrowed dust
Calling it truth before earning trust

[Chorus - Both]
Two lanes, one town, one bridge between us
Different kind of thunder, same rain above
You bring the rhythm, I bring the rust
Neither one means much without a little trust
Lay the old assumptions down
Two lanes, one road through the same small town

[Verse 2 - Deep Tony, rap]
Hold up—came for a job, not a judgment at the pump
You saw chrome in the dark, heard the kick and the thump
I saw hands in your pockets, thought the welcome was thin
Two strangers keeping score before the talk could begin
My uncle drove a rig, wore the soles off his shoes
Your daughter loops beats with the porch-light blues
Whole map full of labels, every label too small
A name ain't a window, and a wall ain't all
I talk quick, you draw slow, still the point comes around
Every life got a basement and a bright upstairs sound
So I lowered that bass, you unfolded that chair
Now the night ain't as heavy when the truth gets some air

[Chorus - Both]
Two lanes, one town, one bridge between us
Different kind of thunder, same rain above
You bring the rhythm, I bring the rust
Neither one means much without a little trust
Lay the old assumptions down
Two lanes, one road through the same small town

[Verse 3 - Country Tony]
You showed me how the backbeat leans in
I showed you where the river bends
Your deeper voice shook dust from the rafters
Mine found a high note at the end
We never traded names for costumes
Never claimed the past was gone
We just quit making each other carry
Every wrong somebody else had done

[Bridge - Call and Response]
[Country Tony]
I don't know every road you've taken

[Deep Tony]
I don't need you to pretend you do

[Country Tony]
But I can ask before deciding

[Deep Tony]
And I can leave some room for you

[Both]
No grand speech, no easy answer
Just a door that opens wide
A beat beneath an old guitar
And two stubborn men inside

[Final Chorus - Both]
Two lanes, one town, that bridge can hold us
Different kind of stories, one sky above
You bring the rhythm, I bring the rust
Turn it into something louder than distrust
Lay the old assumptions down
Two lanes, one road through the same small town

[Outro - Both, sung]
When morning paints the county line
Your road and mine run side by side
No borrowed verdict, no backing down
We meet as ourselves in this two-lane town

[Deep Tony, spoken]
Leave the chair out.

[Country Tony, softly]
I'll leave the light on.

songs.title: No Flag Can Wash the Dust

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Sirens stitch the midnight sky
A screen turns grief to battle cries
Somebody whispers, Pick a side
But every child deserves a life

[Verse 1]
Boots in the hallway, drones overhead
Names become numbers, the missing called dead
Men at the podium polish each phrase
While families vanish inside the haze
They call it defense, they call it fate
They seal every crossing and rattle the gate
But law does not bend for a uniformed lie
And no sacred banner makes innocence die

[Pre-Chorus]
I hear the machine say, Look away
I hear the frightened voices stay

[Chorus]
No flag can wash the dust away
No anthem makes the terror brave
If children pay the price you name
Then history will mark the shame
No flag can wash the dust away
Every life has weight today
You cannot bury what was done
Beneath the shadow of the sun

[Verse 2]
Food held back and water denied
Hospitals trembling through another night
Homes turned hollow, schools turned still
Punishment measured by somebody's will
Hostages taken, civilians struck
Vengeance keeps feeding the same black truck
Every war crime needs daylight and names
Evidence kept when the powerful blame

[Pre-Chorus]
The camera shakes, the signal breaks
Still truth survives the noise they make

[Chorus]
No flag can wash the dust away
No anthem makes the terror brave
If children pay the price you name
Then history will mark the shame
No flag can wash the dust away
Every life has weight today
You cannot bury what was done
Beneath the shadow of the sun

[Bridge]
Do not sell me blood as duty
Do not dress revenge in beauty
A people living, safe and free
Cannot be built on misery
Jewish child and Palestinian child
Neither born condemned or exiled
Justice is not a loaded word
It starts when every cry is heard

[Breakdown]
Count the missing
Name the dead
Guard the witness
Save the thread
Try the orders
Trace the chain
No rank absolves deliberate pain

[Final Chorus]
No flag can wash the dust away
No anthem makes the terror brave
Let every captive see the day
Let every family find a way
No flag can wash the dust away
No ancient grief excuses hate
The final word is not the gun
A human future must be won

[Outro]
When all the broadcast towers fade
The truth remains beneath the names
No child is tribute, prize, or blame
No flag can sanctify the flame
Put down the lie, let mercy come
Let justice speak when war is done

Boots in the hallway, drones overhead
Names become numbers, the missing called dead
Men at the podium polish each phrase
While families vanish inside the haze

Food held back and water denied
Hospitals trembling through another night
Homes turned hollow, schools turned still
Punishment measured by somebody's will
Hostages taken, civilians struck
Vengeance keeps feeding the same black truck
Every war crime needs daylight and names
Evidence kept when the powerful blame

[Pre-Chorus]

Still truth survives the noise they make

[Chorus]

No anthem makes the terror brave
If children pay the price you name

No flag can wash the dust away
Every life has weight today

Beneath the shadow of the sun

Do not sell me blood as duty

Cannot be built on misery
Jewish child and Palestinian child
Neither born condemned or exiled
Justice is not a loaded word
It starts when every cry is heard

[Breakdown]

Name the dead
Guard the witness
Save the thread
Try the orders
Trace the chain
No rank absolves deliberate pain

Let every captive see the day
Let every family find a way

No ancient grief excuses hate

When all the broadcast towers fade
The truth remains beneath the names
No child is tribute, prize, or blame

Put down the lie, let mercy come
Let justice speak when war is done
Every child deserves the sun
Every child deserves the sun

lyrics.text:
[Intro]

[Tony]
Sign said MERCY, population small,
I asked that sign, “You know me at all?”
My map was upside down, my name felt borrowed,
I told the deputy I’d remember tomorrow.

[Verse 1 — Tony]
I walked in Dot’s with dust on my shoes,
A crooked grin and a head full of blues.
Saw Miss Renee by the coffee machine,
Said, “Fill mine up, if you know what I mean.”
The whole room stopped; one fork hit a plate.
She said, “I don’t work here. You can wait.”
I laughed too quickly, tried playing it light,
But a joke ain’t a lantern when the joke ain’t right.

[Verse 2 — Renee]
You didn’t burn a cross or shout a cruel name,
But old assumptions still carry old flames.
You saw my skin, then assigned me a place;
That little mistake had a history’s face.
I’m chair of the council, I teach Sunday school,
But I shouldn’t need titles to prove you were cruel.
Don’t tell me your heart is harmless and free—
Ask what made that picture appear when you saw me.

[Pre-Chorus — Tony]
I checked every pocket for somebody to blame,
Found lint, one nickel, and my own damn name.

[Chorus — Duet]
[Tony]
I was wrong in Mercy, Alabama,
No excuse hiding under my stammer.
I’m sorry for the weight I made you carry;
I’ll face what’s in me, even when it gets scary.
[Renee]
An apology opens, but action walks through;
Don’t ask me to finish the fixing for you.
[Both]
Tell the truth plain, let the old lie fall—
Mercy ain’t mercy till it reaches us all.

[Verse 3 — Tony]
I said, “I’m not that kind,” then heard what I’d done:
Made my good intentions the place I could run.
I remembered my uncles and half-heard advice,
The laughs at the table I never checked twice.
Maybe I inherited a room full of smoke,
But I’m holding the match every time I repeat it.
So I went table to table, no grandstanding show,
Said, “What I assumed was wrong, and I need you to know.”

[Verse 4 — Renee]
I don’t need a promise polished for applause,
Or tears that make your comfort the cause.
Learn people’s names; let correction land;
Speak when your friends say what you understand.
You may feel lost, but you’re standing right here,
And confusion can’t cancel the harm made clear.
If you want to change, then change when unseen;
Make better habits where the old ones have been.

[Instrumental Turn — short Telecaster and fiddle answer]

[Verse 5 — Tony]
I volunteered Tuesday at the library sale,
Put history books where I once put a tale.
When Earl made a crack by the courthouse wall,
I didn’t grin sideways; I answered the call.
Said, “That ain’t harmless, and silence joins in.”
My knees started knocking underneath my grin.
Then I bought my own coffee and carried the tray,
Didn’t ask for a medal at the end of the day.

[Pre-Chorus — Renee and Tony]
[Renee]
You still look lost.
[Tony]
Ma’am, that much is true.
Is this Alabama—or Kalamazoo?
[Renee]
You’re Tony.
[Tony]
That sounds vaguely familiar.
[Renee]
Then be someone better.
[Tony]
I reckon that’s clearer.

[Chorus — Duet]
[Tony]
I was wrong in Mercy, Alabama,
No excuse hiding under my stammer.
I’m sorry for the weight I made you carry;
I’ll face what’s in me, even when it gets scary.
[Renee]
An apology opens, but action walks through;
I can name the wound, but the work belongs to you.
[Both]
Tell the truth plain, let the old lie fall—
Mercy ain’t mercy till it reaches us all.

[Bridge — Renee]
Hear my side without rehearsing your defense:
Being underestimated leaves a long expense.
One small moment joins a thousand from before;
That’s why your “little mix-up” felt like something more.
I can see your effort; I can guard my peace.
Forgiveness isn’t owed, and trust grows piece by piece.

[Bridge — Tony]
I won’t make you teach me every road I missed,
Or turn my shame into a clenched-up fist.
I’ll read, I’ll listen, I’ll interrupt the chain,
And when I fail, I’ll own it without making you explain.
I can’t change yesterday by hating who I’ve been,
But I can make amends with the man beneath my skin.

[Breakdown — Duet]
[Renee]
Who are you now?
[Tony]
The fool who finally heard.
[Renee]
Where are you now?
[Tony]
Trying to live my word.
[Renee]
What happens next?
[Tony]
The unglamorous part:
A thousand better choices from a reeducated heart.

[Final Chorus — Duet]
[Tony]
I was wrong in Mercy, Alabama,
Now truth rides shotgun through the static and clamor.
No halo on my hat, no hero in this story,
Just a man doing work without claiming the glory.
[Renee]
I have my own voice, my own road, my own view;
I’m more than the lesson that happened to you.
[Both]
Tell the truth plain, let the old lie fall—
Mercy ain’t mercy till it reaches us all.

[Final Tag — sustained duet]
[Tony]
If I lose my way, I’ll remember what is true:
Being lost never gives me leave to misjudge you.
[Renee]
Keep walking awake; let your better deeds answer.
[Both]
In Mercy, Alabama, there is room to change after—
Room to change after all.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Load the dungeon, strike a match
Tony's got a rusty latch
Says, “This time I know the route”
First dark hallway—lights go out

[Verse 1]
Found a bonesaw, lost a shoe
Something hungry chewed straight through
Missed the coin flip, broke his arm
Stepped on every fucking harm
Guard came dragging down the hall
Tony ducked behind the wall
Floor gave way beneath him then
Goddamn—nine-eleven'd again

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
Tony growls, “Aw, son of a bitch”
Loads that miserable save from six
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Verse 2]
Back downstairs with half a map
Dodged the dogs and found a trap
Fed the girl and saved his meat
Crow Mauler dropped him through the street
Tony leaned into the screen
“That's the cheapest shit I've seen”
Lit a smoke and counted ten
Got up—nine-eleven'd again

[Pre-Chorus]
Now his grin is getting crooked
Every guide says he mistook it
Every doorway smells like doom
Still he kicks into the room

[Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again
Right when the good run begins
One loud crash, the whole plan ends
Nine-eleven'd again
Tony snarls, “You rigged this shit”
Throws the mouse but will not quit
Fear in the dark and hunger within
Then he gets nine-eleven'd again

[Bridge]
Coin in the air—call it clean
Heads means mercy, tails gets mean
It hits the stone, it rolls from sight
Dungeon laughs and kills the light
Tony mutters, low and slow
“You ain't tellin' me to go”
Blood at one and mind at ten
He crawls toward the throne again

[Breakdown]
No food left
No good limb
No clean save
Still goes in
Bell starts shaking
Ceiling bends
Tony sees it—“Not this again!”

[Final Verse]
Past the prison, past the mines
Past the rotten gods and signs
Every loss has taught his hands
Where the blade falls, where it lands
Last door opens, pale and wide
All that spite walks in beside him
Dungeon offers one last spin
Tony laughs, “Then let me win.”

[Final Chorus]
Nine-eleven'd again—
But he rises through the din
Let it crash, he'll crawl back in
No more begging at the end
Tony roars, “You hungry pit,
I can die all night, you prick!”
Fear in the dark, but fire within
You can nine-eleven him again—
He'll load that bastard save and win

[Outro]
Screen goes black, the final chord bends
Tony grins: “Now who's annoyed, my friend?”

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Neon on the flight deck, midnight engine glow
Swann wiped his hands where the red alarms would show
Raynor crossed the gantry with a storm behind his eyes
While a row of black-winged Banshees waited silent as the skies

[Verse 1]
Swann said, “Pull that panel, Jimmy, look beneath the skin
Heat sinks humming cold enough to hide the fire within
Spectral coils are steady, phase grid’s running clean
They’ll never see our pilots till they’re tearing through the screen”

Raynor watched the readouts paint a ghost across the glass
“They disappear from sensors, but how long can that trick last?”
Swann laughed through the static, struck the console with his hand
“Long enough to cross their guns and leave ’em where they stand”

[Pre-Chorus]
Blue current in the cables
Black wings against the stars
No shadow on the radar
Just thunder wearing scars

[Chorus]
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Ghost wings ready to deploy
Kill the lights and cut the noise
Let the Dominion chase decoys
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
A Banshee they cannot destroy

[Verse 2]
Raynor leaned in closer as the cloak began to bend
Every edge went liquid, every shape refused to end
Then the ship was absent, though its turbines shook the floor
Like a loaded question breathing just behind the hangar door

“I’m not sure this is the best time to be experimentin’”
Swann sparked up a welder, never pausing to explain
“Hell Cowboy, best time there is”
Then he kicked the housing shut and grinned into the rain

[Pre-Chorus]
No beacon for the towers
No heat trail for the guns
Just pilots counting heartbeats
Before the firing run

[Chorus]
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Ghost wings ready to deploy
Slip unseen through burning lanes
Strike the locks and break the chains
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Then vanish in the reactor haze

[Verse 3]
The tactical display lit up with cruisers wall to wall
Swann traced out a crooked route that threaded through them all
“Cloak draws hard on power, so don’t waste a single breath
Drop it when you’ve crossed the line, then give their engines death”

Raynor keyed the squadron, “Keep it low and keep it tight
Swann has built a doorway through the teeth of hell tonight”
One by one the Banshees faded underneath the warning red
Leaving only engine whispers circling overhead

[Instrumental Break]
[Driving bass sequence, gated drums, distorted guitar harmonics]

[Bridge]
Swann said, “Every ghost needs copper
Every miracle needs grease
Every clean escape begins
With bolts that won’t release”

Raynor said, “If this goes sideways—”
Swann said, “Then turn the whole thing straight
You bring the revolution
I’ll bring something they can’t trace”

[Breakdown]
Cloak on—the stars go blind
Cloak off—the rockets shine
One breath—the targeting slips
Two hands—the whole sky rips
No flag, no flare, no warning cry
Just Banshee wings in an empty sky

[Final Chorus]
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Hear that hidden engine roar
Through the grid and past the guns
Till the raid and night are one
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Ghost wings settling the score

Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Bring every lost pilot home
Let the tyrants scan the night
All they’ll find is fractured light
Got somethin for ya Cowboy
And a clear road back to home

[Outro]
The squadron crossed the gantry as the cloak released its hold
Black wings rising into view beneath the morning gold
Raynor tipped his hat and said, “She flies exactly right”
Swann laughed, “Told ya, Cowboy”—and shut down the neon night

Ghost wings home…
Engines low…
Cowboy, now you know

Blue current in the cables
Black wings against the stars

Got somethin for ya Cowboy
Got somethin for ya Cowboy

Raynor leaned in closer as the cloak began to bend
Every edge went liquid, every shape refused to end
Then the ship was absent, though its turbines shook the floor
Like a loaded question breathing just behind the hangar door

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Halloween moon, cardboard skyline,
Tony hit the porch at half past nine.
Two silver towers strapped side by side—
He took one step and got stuck outside.

[Verse 1]
He turned to the left, knocked over a witch,
Turned to the right, caught a cape on a hitch.
The screen door snapped with a terrible clang,
Tony just grinned while the doorbell rang.

The neighbors yelled, “Tony, you’re much too wide!”
He muttered, “That’s architecture,” and shuffled inside.
A plastic bat landed high on his crown;
He wore it like a gargoyle all over town.

[Chorus]
Two towers too wide for the Halloween street,
Bumping every pumpkin with his cardboard feet.
Candy in the lobby, cobwebs in the sky,
Every narrow doorway made the whole thing fly.
Two towers too wide—clear a little room!
Tony brought a skyline to the costume gloom.

[Verse 2]
At the haunted garage, the bass kicked hard;
He clipped both towers on the skeleton yard.
One leaned west and the other leaned east,
Then both popped back to the beat of the beast.

A kid dressed as traffic waved him around,
But Tony spun once and the signs fell down.
He laughed through the smoke, “That’s city design,”
Then traded the gargoyle for a licorice vine.

[Bridge]
When the rain made the cardboard buckle and sway,
He folded both towers and danced them away.
No grand disaster, no reason to pout—
Just two soggy boxes with Tony sticking out.

[Final Chorus]
Two towers too wide for the Halloween street,
Now flat as a map underneath his feet.
Candy in his pockets, moon riding high,
He bowed to the doorway and finally slipped by.
Two towers too wide, but the joke landed right—
Tony wore the whole town home that night.

[Tag]
He rang his own bell with a crooked little grin:
“Next year, one tower—and I’m getting in.”

originalPrompt.idea: Tony C dresses up as the twin towers for Halloween and hijinks ensue

Tony V7 remains the mandatory pinned voice, delivered with smoky slurs, crooked timing, muttered punch lines, and a clearly sung hook. Build the final chorus with gang-free backing harmonies and a rising organ line; sustain the last word of the tag around 129–132 seconds, then land one resolved D-minor chord and allow an 8–12-second decay.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Red light, blue light, split down the lane
Two fools enlisted in a mathematical pain

[Verse 1]
I brought the army, you brought the nerve
Then the field put a sign on who we're allowed to serve
Your guns hit hard, mine bounce off clean
The cruelest little rule that the sector's ever seen
Shoes on the floor and my hands on the wheel
Watching your base take damage I can see but cannot heal
I cross the map with a desperate plan
But the target flashes wrong—I'm an unauthorized man

[Pre-Chorus]
Shoes full of gravel, teeth full of sparks
We're paired together but assigned to different marks

[Chorus]
Shoes, get moving, but the lock says no
Shoes, keep kicking while the red lights glow
Shoes at the doorway, rage in the hall
I'm strong enough to save you, not permitted to at all
Polarity! What a beautiful scam
You carry half the battle while I carry who I am

[Verse 2]
Your side gets flooded, my side takes a nap
I'm drawing angry circles on the tactical map
Shoes hit the metal as the hybrid comes through
Every useful shot I've got is the wrong color for you
Shoes in the fire, and the timer runs thin
I could clear the whole disaster if the game would let me in
You ping like thunder, I answer like rain
Then I fire one round and hear that useless clank again

[Pre-Chorus]
Shoes on a wire, balance and swear
Two allied armies, neither welcome everywhere

[Chorus]
Shoes, get moving, but the lock says no
Shoes, keep kicking while the red lights glow
Shoes at the doorway, rage in the hall
I'm strong enough to save you, not permitted to at all
Polarity! Divide and command
You hold the wrong objective while I wave from promised land

[Bridge]
Shoes to the north where your enemies breed
Shoes to the south where I've got what you need
Shoes through the smoke, but the rules disagree
Shoes do the marching while the lock laughs at me
No cowardice, no shortage, no tactical doubt
Just a plus and a minus keeping both of us out
So trade me your targets, I'll trade you my blame
We'll beat this crooked circuit at its own divided game

[Verse 3]
Shoes nearly broken, but we're reading the signs
You take the left mutation, I erase the right-hand lines
Shoes find the rhythm: swap, cover, attack
When your color meets the target, I keep death off your back
No hero can carry what no hero can touch
So we carry one another, and we curse twice as much
The final wave rises, every warning turns red
We split it down the middle and we leave the hybrids dead

[Final Chorus]
Shoes, keep moving—now we both know how
Wrong side a minute, right side now
Shoes at the doorway, kick through the wall
They said I couldn't carry you—we carried us all
Polarity! Your circuit is blown
Two mismatched allies made the battlefield our own

[Finale]
The lock goes dark, the last sparks fall
You carried me—I didn't carry you at all

originalPrompt.idea: The pain and frustration of carrying an ally in SC2 co-op where you can't - because of polarity

songPlan.arrangement: Raw late-1970s British punk energy without copying a specific band: snarling electric guitars, muscular moving bass, dry live drums, abrupt ensemble stops, and a short feedback-streaked finale. Tony V7 delivers smoky slurs, crooked timing, dismissive laughs, and a clearly shouted central hook. Final lyric lands near 230 seconds, followed by roughly 10 seconds of sustained guitar chord and decay.

songs.title: No Saints in the Bomb Crater

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro]
Bring out the black flags.
The minister has found another war.

[Verse 1]
Tony climbed the marble stair
With medals borrowed, teeth laid bare
“Triple the guns, triple the pay
We’ll flatten every doubt away”
The brass band coughed, the widows stared
At maps that rich old cowards shared
He called them infidels abroad
Then billed the bloodshed straight to God

[Pre-Chorus]
But every border drawn in smoke
Leaves someone’s child beneath the oak

[Chorus]
No saints in the bomb crater
No truth in the targeting light
You can dress that hatred in a uniform
It’s still fucking murder at night
Ring the bell for the dealmaker
Count every name that he forgot
No saints in the bomb crater
Just the living—and the ones who are not

[Verse 2]
He promised glory, clean and fast
A holy future, armored glass
The cameras loved his crooked grin
While folded flags came rolling in
A mother spat upon his shoe
Said, “My dead boy believed in you”
The choir bent beneath the sound
Of empty chairs and lowered ground

[Pre-Chorus]
The ledger swelled, the table shone
The ones who voted stayed at home

[Chorus]
No saints in the bomb crater
No truth in the targeting light
You can dress that hatred in a uniform
It’s still fucking murder at night
Ring the bell for the dealmaker
Count every name that he forgot
No saints in the bomb crater
Just the living—and the ones who are not

[Funeral Procession]
Slow boots through the rain now
Black mud on the wheel
Tell me what your heaven costs
Tell me who pays the bill
Not the bastard at the podium
Not the hands behind the screen
It’s the stranger under rubble
It’s the kid who turned nineteen

[Bridge]
Lay down the flag for a minute
Let the silence testify
Faith is not a firing order
And no anthem makes that lie
If your god demands a graveyard
Maybe hell is where you stand
With a pen above the budget
And no blood upon your hands

[Final Chorus]
No saints in the bomb crater
No crown for the loudest lie
We won’t turn our grief to ammunition
We won’t bless another strike
Ring the bell for the warmaker
Till the marble halls all shake
No saints in the bomb crater
Only choices human beings make

[Outro]
Tony faced the final headstone
All his thunder drained away
No crowd left to salute him
No frightened god left to obey
The last bell broke the morning
And the living walked away

originalPrompt.idea: Tony proposes tripling the military budget and laying infidels low around the world.

songPlan.title: No Saints in the Bomb Crater
songPlan.arrangement: A bleak funeral-dirge rock arrangement with tolling church bell, bowed upright bass, floor toms, harmonium, low brass, distorted baritone guitar, and restrained male choir. Tony delivers smoky, slurred verses, rising into a catchable accusatory chorus; the procession grows heavier before dropping to near-silence for the bridge. The final vocal ends at about 235 seconds, followed by one unresolved bell resolving into a low D-minor chord and 11 seconds of decay.

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
The telephone company sent me a bill
For a conversation I never could finish
I held that receiver against the windowsill
And watched the last light quietly diminish
A woman said sir we can trace every call
I said can you trace where the good ones go
She put me on hold with a hole in the wall
And a little brass tune from a lifetime ago

[Chorus]
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And he's got nothing left to explain
He can sing over everyone's business
He can shake himself dry in the rain
I've been paying to talk to the silence
I've been waiting for somebody's sign
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And tonight I'm taking back my line

[Verse 2]
My neighbor came over with half of a peach
And a story that wandered all over the county
He said what you want is a little more reach
I said what I want is somebody around me
We sat on the steps as the buses went by
And the peach got divided into smaller pieces
He told me a joke and forgot all the why
But we laughed till the trouble began to release us

[Chorus]
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And he's got nothing left to explain
He can sing over everyone's business
He can shake himself dry in the rain
I've been paying to talk to the silence
I've been waiting for somebody's sign
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And tonight I'm taking back my line

[Bridge]
Hello to the woman who answered
Hello to the room down the hall
Tell the machine I've gone outside
I don't need it to carry this call
There is a porch and a person beside me
There is a laugh I can hear without trying

[Final Chorus]
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And he's got nothing left to explain
He can sing over everyone's business
He can shake himself dry in the rain
I'm done sending my voice into nowhere
There is someone who knows it is mine
There's a bird on the telephone wire
And tonight I'm taking back my line

[Verse 1]
You left a key inside a coffee tin
Underneath the pot where nothing grows
You said the lock gets stubborn when the rain comes in
Lift the handle gently when it goes
I kept your note behind a grocery list
Bread and apples written over June
There were other little things I must have missed
A chair pulled out and waiting in the room

[Chorus]
It's spare key weather
The sky is coming down
We don't have to put ourselves together
Before we come around
Leave your coat beside the heater
Let the water mark the floor
It's spare key weather
You don't have to knock on this door

[Verse 2]
I used to think a visit needed reasons
A birthday or a ladder I could lend
I let a hundred ordinary evenings
Disappear before I called a friend
Tonight the road is shining like a river
I carry nothing useful in my hands
The little key is cold against my fingers
The handle lifts exactly like you planned

[Chorus]
It's spare key weather
The sky is coming down
We don't have to put ourselves together
Before we come around
Leave your coat beside the heater
Let the water mark the floor
It's spare key weather
You don't have to knock on this door

[Bridge]
You look up from the kitchen
Like I've only been a minute
There is tea enough for another cup
And a little room left in it
I start to say I'm sorry
You ask me how I've been
The rain can keep the whole wide world
Tonight you let me in

[Final Chorus]
It's spare key weather
The sky is coming down
We can sit here coming back together
With the whole storm all around
Leave the light beside the window
Leave the boots across the floor
It's spare key weather
I remembered what the key was for

songs.title: The Last Light in the Station (Tony V7 Study)

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
They took the numbers off the platform wall
They rolled the timetable into a tube
The station clock still heard the morning call
And moved its hands although the trains were through
I had a ring of keys and thirty years
A broom that knew the corners of the place
I swept the tickets out from underneath the chairs
And found a child's drawing of my face

[Chorus]
I'll leave the last light in the station
Till the morning finds its way
For the ones who missed their destination
For the ones who couldn't stay
If you see it through the weather
If you're coming down the line
There's a little room to wait together
And the last light will be mine

[Verse 2]
A man arrived with flowers in his coat
He hadn't heard the service had been ended
He showed me where his daughter's hand had wrote
The time and place their distance could be mended
I brought him to the office telephone
He stood so straight and struggled with her number
I stepped outside and left him there alone
And heard his voice grow younger through the timber

[Chorus]
I'll leave the last light in the station
Till the morning finds its way
For the ones who missed their destination
For the ones who couldn't stay
If you see it through the weather
If you're coming down the line
There's a little room to wait together
And the last light will be mine

[Bridge]
A car pulled up at half past seven
She ran across the empty square
I never saw a train arrive
That brought so much as seeing her there
They asked if I was heading home
I turned the key and joined them in the air

[Final Chorus]
There's a last light in the station
And the morning found its way
For the ones who changed their destination
For the ones who chose to stay
You can see it through the weather
Like a star above the line
There was room enough to wait together
Now the road ahead is mine

songs.title: Jihad at the Holy Big Top

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Roll up the canvas, tighten the wire
Tony's in the ring with a mouthful of fire
Brass in the alley, drum at the gate
The fat-cat parade has arrived too late

[Verse 1]
They came in silk with a contract grin
Selling us the locks, then charging to get in
They weighed every laugh, put a tax on the rain
Stamped their little logo on the side of my brain
But this crooked nation has a pulse below
Where the battered horns and the wild hearts go
I kissed the dust, heard the kettledrum call
Tonight we raise the tent or we bury it all

[Pre-Chorus]
Round goes the wheel, but the axle is ours
Light every lantern on the carnival towers

[Chorus]
Jihad! Jihad! Hear the battle cry:
“Break the golden cages—send the pigdogs flying high!”
For the holy nation of the hungry and ignored
We march with a bass drum, a bell, and a sword
Jihad! Jihad! Let the crooked brass roar
No king owns the midway, no banker owns the door

[Verse 2]
The minister juggles three counterfeit laws
While the chairman applauds with mechanical claws
They auction the moon by the sliver and slice
Then sell back the darkness at a holiday price
Tony laughs low, wipes the smoke from his chin
Says, “You bought the whole game, but you still cannot win”
The acrobats tumble, the painted carts sway
And the workers turn the spotlights the opposite way

[Pre-Chorus]
Round goes the wheel, hear the old engine cough
When the smallest hand pulls, the whole crown falls off

[Chorus]
Jihad! Jihad! Hear the battle cry:
“Break the golden cages—send the pigdogs flying high!”
For the holy nation of the hungry and ignored
We march with a bass drum, a bell, and a sword
Jihad! Jihad! Let the crooked brass roar
No king owns the midway, no banker owns the door

[Bridge]
Half-time now—the calliope wheezes
Tony bends the notes till the brass section sneezes
No blood for the ledger, no graves for the throne
We conquer their circus by making it our own
Rip up the price tags, unlock every stall
Bread on the tables and music for all

[Instrumental Break]

[Final Chorus]
Jihad! Jihad! Hear the battle cry:

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Rain on the fire escape, ten past two
Your name in the glow, and the whole night knew

[Verse 1]
You wrote, “I’m sorry,” like a door left wide
Ten winters late, with the truth tucked inside
Back then I waited by the corner-store light
Every cab made me think you might arrive
I learned how silence gets heavy with age
How a clean white screen can feel like a cage
Now your little blue bubble wants mercy from me
But the kid you abandoned ain’t the man that you see
I wore out the question, I buried the blame
Built a roof from the ruins, quit saying your name
And tonight every gutter keeps counting the cost
Of a message that found me when needing you stopped

[Chorus]
Ten years in the rain, now you’re calling my name
Your apology lands, but it don’t land the same
I can read every word, I can hear what you mean
But you can’t dry a decade with a sorry on a screen
Ten years in the rain, I survived every stain
I forgive what I can—I won’t live there again

[Verse 2]
You say you were scared; well, I was scared too
Difference is, I stayed with what you put me through
Had birthdays go quiet, had good news turn gray
Had whole conversations with what you wouldn’t say
Maybe you changed, maybe guilt found a voice
Maybe losing my number was never your choice
I ain’t here for revenge, I got no knife to twist
Just a life that grew around the shape that you missed
So keep this reply when the thunder gets loud:
I was worth showing up for—I know that now

[Bridge – Arabic/throat accent]
Ten years beneath this rain
Ten years beneath this rain

[Final Chorus]
Ten years in the rain, now you’re calling my name
Your apology lands, but it don’t land the same
I believe you regret every mile in between
But you can’t dry a decade with a sorry on a screen
Ten years in the rain, let it wash through the pain
I forgive you tonight—I won’t wait here again

[Outro]
Your words came too late, but my answer came clear:
I release what you broke; I am leaving it here
No hate in my hands, no old chain on my name
I walk into morning through the last of the rain

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Three years dry on a barroom stool
Drinking ginger ale and keeping cool
Geglash came in from the pouring rain
Just to hear the old jukebox complain

[Verse 1]
He'd been stout-hearted, standing tall
Never missed the morning after at all
Knew every bottle by its old first name
But quit returning when temptation came
Then the barman raised a midnight brew
Black as a boot with a collar of dew
Said, “This one's roasted, rich and slow”
Geglash whispered, “Ja... I gotta know”

[Pre-Chorus]
His eyes went wide at that coffee crown
Three sober years couldn't stare it down
The room held still, then his grin turned loud
That little word fell right through the crowd

[Chorus]
That was the night when the Ja dropped
Hit the floor and the whole room stopped
He found his stout, but his footing thinned
A dark little door let the old light in
He said, “Ja, that's smooth,” with a crooked laugh
Then read his whole past in the empty half
Three years built, one swallow shocked
That was the night when the Ja dropped

[Verse 2]
He called it research, called it grain review
Said, “I'm only checking what the barley knew”
But the head had vanished, the truth stayed plain
You can't pour sunshine through an old storm drain
He made some porter jokes, growing bold
Said the ale had body but his alibi was cold
Asked for one more round to settle the score
The barman said, “Your tab weighs more than before”

[Pre-Chorus]
His twang got thick and his timing slid
He found the man that sobriety hid
The joke wore out when the glass rang bare
And three hard years stood watching from the chair

[Chorus]
That was the night when the Ja dropped
Hit the floor and the whole room stopped
He found his stout, but his footing thinned
A dark little door let the old light in
He said, “Ja, that's smooth,” with a crooked laugh
Then read his whole past in the empty half
Three years built, one swallow shocked
That was the night when the Ja dropped

[Instrumental Turn]

[Verse 3]
At closing time beneath the buzzing sign
He couldn't walk a straight punch line
Said, “I went against the grain, that's true
Now every road is brewing into two”
His sponsor came in an old Ford truck
Said, “A slip ain't fate, and shame ain't luck
You lost one night, not the miles you crossed
Stand up now before the rest gets lost”

[Bridge]
Geglash stared at the dawn coming pale
Said, “I chased a stout and found myself frail
I thought one pint was a harmless guest
But it moved old furniture back in my chest”
Then softer, smoky, almost under breath:
“Ja... that foam wrote a heavy check”
He poured the last dark inch away
And let the gutter drink his yesterday

[Breakdown]
No grand oath and no courthouse scene
Just coffee black and a conscience clean
A battered joke and a lesson learned:
Even roasted bridges still get burned
He laughed once low, though his eyes stayed wet
“I'm not starting over—I'm starting from regret”
Then marked the date where the old one stopped
The morning after the Ja had dropped

[Final Chorus]
That was the night when the Ja dropped
Hit the floor and the whole room stopped
He found his stout, then he found his feet
With a bitter truth where the malt tasted sweet
He said, “Ja, I slipped,” no alibi
No frothy story and no reason why
Three years still count though the bottle talked
He carried every mile when he sober-walked

[Final Tag]
Now when somebody raises that coffee crown
He lets the word rise but the glass stay down
“Ja, I know stout—and I know my cost”
A night went missing, but the man stayed lost
Only till sunrise, when the old spell broke
He chose his road through the barley smoke
His jaw came back, and the barroom clock
Kept moving on from the night Ja dropped
Kept moving on... from the night Ja dropped

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro]
Laces tight, dignity loose.
I got one more rune to chase.

[Verse 1]
Woke up creased beneath the bed
Rubber tongue and leather head
Tony in the mirror, nowhere to be found
Just one crooked loafer crawling downtown
My eyelets blinked, my heel felt mean
I smelled like smoke and kerosene
Had an empty stash and a fevered goal
Diablo on the screen saying, Bring me Sol

[Pre-Chorus]
I sold the jacket, pawned the chair
Traded every decent thing I had to spare
Now the stash tab glows, and the craving calls
So I click-clack out through the motel halls

[Chorus]
I’m selling my sole for a pocketful of Sol
Working this curb with a hole in my soul
Red nose moon and the streetlights strobe
I’m a size-ten sinner in a secondhand robe
Pay what you want, but the rune comes first
Every little trade only sharpens the thirst
I’m selling my sole, and I know what it costs
One more night in Sanctuary, completely lost

[Drop]
Squeak—step, lace snap, bass goes crooked
Big red grin, but the eyes look cooked
Sol in the socket, gold in the slot
I said, “That all ya got?” then I took the lot

[Verse 2]
A limousine hissed by the liquor-store sign
Some bastard whispered, “Hey, that shoe looks fine”
I tipped my tongue with a dismissive laugh
“Cash up front, pal—don’t do halves”
The circus synths began to squeal
While dirty sub-bass shook my heel
Every deal bought another run
Countess at midnight, still no fun

[Pre-Chorus]
My laces frayed, my polish cracked
But the glowing little letters kept pulling me back
No sacred armor, no grand control
Just a cheap-room altar to another Sol

[Chorus]
I’m selling my sole for a pocketful of Sol
Working this curb with a hole in my soul
Red nose moon and the streetlights strobe
I’m a size-ten sinner in a secondhand robe
Pay what you want, but the rune comes first
Every little trade only sharpens the thirst
I’m selling my sole, and I know what it costs
One more night in Sanctuary, completely lost

[Bridge]
Then the server went black at a quarter to four
No loot, no light, no knock at the door
I saw my bent shape in a rainwater stain
A clown-painted shoe going numb in the rain
“Heh… Tony, ya beautiful fool,” I slurred
“You traded your name for a three-letter word”
I loosened one lace, let the cold air in
And kicked that glowing habit into the bin

[Final Drop]
Horn blast, heel crack, carousel bends
The bass falls down, then it rises again
No more curb and no bargain-bin throne
If I’m walking through Hell, I’m walking it alone

[Final Chorus]
I nearly sold my sole for a pocketful of Sol
Let the game bite deep, let it swallow me whole
Red dawn burning while the streetlights close
I’m a worn-out wonder with a battered toe
Keep your damn rune, keep your glittering curse
I crawled through the gutter, but I’m coming out first
I’m taking back Tony, every scar, every flaw
With a long crooked grin and a heel full of awe

[Outro Tag]
One last step from the carnival glow
No chains on my laces, no master below
I plant my heel where the new sun falls
Tony stands tall—shoe, sinner, and all
Home… at la-a-ast.

My laces frayed, my polish cracked
But the glowing little letters kept pulling me back
No sacred armor, no grand control
Just a cheap-room altar to another Sol

[Chorus]
I’m selling my sole for a pocketful of Sol
Working this curb with a hole in my soul
Red nose moon and the streetlights strobe
I’m a size-ten sinner in a secondhand robe
Pay what you want, but the rune comes first
Every little trade only sharpens the thirst
I’m selling my sole, and I know what it costs
One more night in Sanctuary, completely lost

[Bridge]
Then the server went black at a quarter to four
No loot, no light, no knock at the door
I saw my bent shape in a rainwater stain
A clown-painted shoe going numb in the rain
“Heh… Tony, ya beautiful fool,” I slurred
“You traded your name for a three-letter word”
I loosened one lace, let the cold air in
And kicked that glowing habit into the bin

Horn blast, heel crack, carousel bends
The bass falls down, then it rises again
No more curb and no bargain-bin throne
If I’m walking through Hell, I’m walking it alone

[Final Chorus]
I nearly sold my sole for a pocketful of Sol
Let the game bite deep, let it swallow me whole
Red dawn burning while the streetlights close
I’m a worn-out wonder with a battered toe
Keep your damn rune, keep your glittering curse
I crawled through the gutter, but I’m coming out first
I’m taking back Tony, every scar, every flaw
With a long crooked grin and a heel full of awe

[Outro Tag]
One last step from the carnival glow
No chains on my laces, no master below
I plant my heel where the new sun falls
Tony stands tall—shoe, sinner, and all
Home… at la-a-ast.

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Hrrrmmm—cold moon, blue sign
Name tag crooked, but the boots still mine

[Verse 1]
I had a six-string kingdom and a gasoline van
Smoke in the speakers, cheap gold in my hand
Then the labels learned numbers, the clubs changed names
Every little screen wanted cleaner flames
Too many changes in the music industry
They shaved off the danger, sold the mystery
I missed one turn where the new road curled
Woke up washed out at the end of the world

[Pre-Chorus]
Fairbanks, Alaska, forty below
Breath like a ghost in the parking-lot glow
I laughed through my teeth—heh, look at me
Still got a pulse, still badly free

[Chorus]
Now I work at Wal-Mart under northern lights
Stacking little kingdoms on the graveyard nights
Blue vest swinging while the floor wheels squeal
I lost the old business, not the way I feel
From a backstage roar to aisle twenty-three
The whole cold town gets a concert from me
Hrrrmmm—hear that freezer drone
I can make a broken place my own

[Verse 2]
Had a room by the highway, one chair, one key
Landlord said, “Tomorrow, Tony—settle with me”
Tomorrow came sharp with a boot and a sheet
Then I was kicked out onto the street
My case held socks and a rusted slide
No record deal, no warm place inside
A cart boy nodded by the loading bay
Said, “Night shift needs somebody right away”

[Pre-Chorus]
So I washed in the sink, tied my hair back low
Walked through the doors with the sideways snow
Manager squinted, said, “Can you start at three?”
I said, “Buddy, the dark starts early with me”

[Chorus]
Now I work at Wal-Mart under northern lights
Stacking little kingdoms on the graveyard nights
Blue vest swinging while the floor wheels squeal
I lost the old business, not the way I feel
From a backstage roar to aisle twenty-three
The whole cold town gets a concert from me
Hrrrmmm—hear that freezer drone
I can make a broken place my own

[Bridge]
Low note rolling in my chest like stone
Overtone rising where the wild winds moan
Oud-string shimmer through the intercom buzz
Nobody remembers who I nearly was
But the baker keeps time and the forklift turns
Coffee goes black while the horizon burns
I sing one bent note till the rafters shake
And the tired night crew finally wakes

[Breakdown]
Price check—no, check my name
Washed out never meant washed away
Cold street—cold feet—still stood tall
Now my shadow dances ten feet on the wall

[Final Chorus]
I work at Wal-Mart under northern lights
Building new thunder on the graveyard nights
Blue vest open and my chin held high
Aurora twisting like a chorus in the sky
Fairbanks, Alaska, you made room for me
Not the crown I wanted, but a place to breathe
Hrrrmmm—let that deep note climb
I quit chasing yesterday’s time

[Outro]
When the doors slide wide at the end of my run
I step through the snow toward the pale morning sun
No street owns Tony, no failure gets the last word
I found my stage where the freezer motors stirred
Clocked out, paid up, little room, new key
The world kept changing—and so did me

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Cold Open]
San Francisco, midnight.
Tony got the roses.
Denny got a secret.
Chris-R got the stairs.
This is gonna hurt somebody.

[Verse 1]
Tony wore his smoky smile into the room,
Tommy stood there glowing in the candle gloom.
Football in a tuxedo, pictures on the wall,
Love was like a rooftop with no rail at all.
Lisa crossed the kitchen with a story in her eyes,
Mark kept every answer underneath a bad disguise.
Tony pulled Tommy closer, said, “Forget that crowd,”
But a knock came from the hallway—sharp and loud.

[Pre-Chorus]
Denny said, “It’s nothing,” but his hands said more,
Then a velvet kind of danger stepped across the floor.

[Chorus]
Chris-R, Chris-R, trouble dressed in black,
Tony saw him coming and he couldn’t look back.
Tommy said, “My darling, why you drifting so far?”
There was room for a secret, room for a scar,
But was there room in The Room for Chris-R?

[Verse 2]
Denny owed him money, Denny missed the day,
Chris-R spoke in thunder, blocking every way.
Tony should have helped him, should have made it right,
Still he caught that crooked grin beneath the hallway light.
Tommy brought the flowers, Tommy brought the wine,
Tony muttered, “Honey, this is terrible timing.”
Then the shouting hit the stairwell, everybody ran,
Tony grabbed the railing—and Chris-R grabbed his hand.

[Pre-Chorus]
One touch, one debt, one dangerous spark,
Tommy in the doorway saying, “Oh, hi Mark.”

[Chorus]
Chris-R, Chris-R, trouble dressed in black,
Tony felt the rhythm and he couldn’t step back.
Tommy cried, “You’re tearing me apart” beneath the stars,
There was room for betrayal, room for bizarre,
But was there room in Tony’s heart for Chris-R?

[Verse 3]
Down at the coffee shop, the stories multiplied,
Lisa blamed the universe, Claudette nearly cried.
Mark said, “I know nothing,” Denny faced the truth,
Tony watched his fantasy collapse around the youth.
Chris-R wasn’t charming when the debt came due,
A handsome face meant nothing when the fear broke through.
Tony stood between them, smoky voice gone clear:
“You don’t buy affection, and you don’t deal fear.”

[Bridge]
No more roses covering a lie,
No more rooftop questions for the empty sky.
Tommy, I loved the legend, but I need what’s real;
Chris-R, keep your danger—I know how danger feels.
Denny, call for help now, let the daylight in;
Tonight this twisted story gets a different end.

[Final Chorus]
Chris-R, Chris-R, take your shadow back,
Tony found his heartbeat on a straighter track.
Tommy heard the answer underneath the stars:
There was room for forgiveness, not another scar.
Tony chose the living over playing a part,
Put Denny on the safe side, put truth in his heart.
The door closed softly; dawn replaced the dark—
No debt, no triangle, no dangerous spark.

[Outro]
Tony left one rose where the old dream had been,
Laughed low, kissed Tommy, let the morning begin.

songs.title: You Left Me to the Swarm

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Red stars burn through the tactical glass
New Gettysburg flickers below
One last order in a dead man's voice:
“Hold the line. Do not let go.”

[Verse 1]
We planted ghosts where the towers could see
Psi fire calling the teeth from the dark
Mengsk watched Tarsonis choke on its knees
Then handed me the final spark
I knew his mercy was circuitry
A switch he could kill from afar
Still I walked into the hive-lit streets
With my rifle against my heart

[Pre-Chorus]
Dropship gone, signal thin
Raynor shouting, “Bring her in!”
Static answered, cold and calm
Then the sky unfolded its arms

[Chorus]
You left me to the swarm
Under a blood-red storm
You sealed the doors and burned the map
While every warning cracked
You left me there alive
Where only monsters thrive
Remember my name when your empire learns
What comes back from the swarm

[Verse 2]
Hydralisk shadows crossed through the smoke
Zerglings rang on the barricade
I called command till the channel broke
And heard the choice that you had made
“Nothing personal”—that polished lie
From a throne not built quite yet
But betrayal has a longer life
Than the man who thinks it forgets

[Pre-Chorus]
Magazine low, visor split
No extraction, that was it
One green beacon faded black
Raynor swore he would come back

[Chorus]
You left me to the swarm
Under a blood-red storm
You sealed the doors and burned the map
While every warning cracked
You left me there alive
Where only monsters thrive
Remember my name when your empire learns
What comes back from the swarm

[Bridge]
Inside the noise, a deeper voice
No rank, no flag, no human choice
A thousand minds beneath my skin
Not an ending—a way in

I saw your fleet become a thread
I saw the crown above your head
Arcturus, sleep while engines hum
You made the blade that is to come

[Instrumental Break]

[Final Verse]
The platform vanished under claws
The woman fell, the signal died
But somewhere past the human laws
A darker heart opened its eyes
Jim, keep flying, keep your flame
There are debts the stars record
When I return, I won't be prey
And he won't be my lord

[Final Chorus]
You left me to the swarm
I rose inside the storm
You sealed the doors and burned the map
Now hear the darkness answer back
You left me there to die
I learned another kind of life
Remember my name when your empire burns—
I came back with the swarm

[Outro]
New Gettysburg fades beneath me
No rescue light, no morning star
The channel closes on Sarah Kerrigan
The blade awakens in the dark

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Midnight, cheap wine, television glow
I pressed play with nowhere else to go
Then you turned around in that candlelit room
Oh hi, Tommy—my heart went boom

[Verse 1]
Black hair falling like a velvet curse
Every tender line made my fever worse
You tossed that bottle, you laughed at the sky
And something unholy climbed into my eye
I had a little cross by the old TV
Now it shakes on the wall like it’s judging me
I said, “Lord, forgive what I’m dreaming tonight”
Then you walked through the door in that suit—good night

[Pre-Chorus]
The accordion wheezes, the floorboards bend
Is this temptation or my new best friend?

[Chorus]
Oh hi, my dark beloved
Tommy, you tore my heaven open
My faith says kneel, but my blood says run
Straight to your rooftop under the sun
Oh hi, my beautiful disaster
My pulse goes filthy, faster and faster
If loving you means I’m damned tonight
Save me a seat by the firelight

[Verse 2]
I tried the Good Book, I tried cold prayer
But I pictured your fingers tangled in my hair
That dangerous whisper, that sideways grin
Made an unlocked chapel of my skin
I want your mouth where my doubt begins
Your hands on the places I confess my sins
I’m sweating through Sunday, biting my lip
While the choir sings and my morals slip

[Pre-Chorus]
The tuba is laughing beneath the floor
And every commandment points to your door

[Chorus]
Oh hi, my dark beloved
Tommy, you tore my heaven open
My faith says kneel, but my blood says run
Straight to your rooftop under the sun
Oh hi, my beautiful disaster
My pulse goes filthy, faster and faster
If loving you means I’m damned tonight
Save me a seat by the firelight

[Bridge]
[Half-time, muttered]
Was I made to fear every hungry spark?
Would grace really leave me alone in the dark?
Maybe love wears strange cologne
Maybe mercy talks in a wandering tone

[Build]
So ring that bell till the rafters crack
I won’t stuff this fever in a Bible sack
No thunder came, no angels fled
Just your famous greeting inside my head

[Final Chorus]
Oh hi, my dark beloved
Tommy, you tore my heaven open
I still believe, but I won’t pretend
Desire and faith can never be friends
Oh hi, my beautiful disaster
Come dance this polka faster and faster
If heaven is love, then love won’t bite
For holding your ghost in my arms tonight

[Outro]
I set the little cross beside the screen
Kept my soul and kept the dream
The credits rolled; dawn filled the room
“Oh hi, Tommy”—then the roses bloomed

songs.title: The One Warrior and the Heavier Feather

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro]
Will you hear my riddle?

[Verse 1]
At Blackbriar Gate, where the moonstones glow,
A keeper barred the crooked road below.
One warrior arrived with a dented crown,
Boasting he could stare any dragon down.
He carried one sword and opinions galore,
No horse, no map, no plan for the moor.
Weigh gold against feathers, a pound in each pan;
Which load bows the balance? Answer if you can.

[Spoken Interlude]
Feathers.
Explain.
They're heavier.

[Pre-Chorus]
The keeper nodded; the answer stood.
The gate swung wide through the dripping wood.
Beyond lay a dragon with emerald eyes,
Guarding a bridge made of polished lies.

[Chorus]
One warrior, walk through the fire,
Crooked little grin and a heart climbing higher.
Feather in your helmet, flame on your trail,
Trick the old dragon where iron would fail.
One warrior, stubborn and bright,
Carry that impossible answer tonight.
Gold may glitter, scales may groan,
But the heavier feather will lead you home.

[Verse 2]
The dragon demanded his sword as a fee,
Then offered a bargain beneath a dead tree.
Three stones sat waiting: the black and the red,
And one painted loaf masquerading as lead.
The warrior broke it; a key tumbled free.
He unlocked the bridge with a theatrical knee.
Then tripped on his scabbard and blamed the map,
While his crown went rolling into the trap.

[Spoken Interlude]
Only testing, my lord.

[Bridge]
The dragon laughed smoke through a chipped golden tooth;
The hero stopped boasting and told him the truth.
He wanted the bell that the village had lost,
Not kingdoms or tribute or glory at cost.
An honest small wish undid all that pride;
The dragon unchained it and moved to one side.

[Spoken Interlude]
He may be the one.

[Final Chorus]
One warrior, out of the fire,
Less of a monarch, but twice the squire.
Feather in his helmet, bell on his back,
Dragon beside him on Blackbriar Track.
Gold may glitter, scales may groan,
But the heavier feather has brought them home.

[Outro]
The bell woke the valley; the road reached its end.
He laid down his sword and made room for a friend.

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
Coffee leaves a circle where the daylight used to be
Lower Kurast loads another little piece of me
Run between the torches, kick the basket by the door
Three expensive dreams and yellow garbage on the floor
I've memorized the crooked boards, the corners of each hut
My wrist has filed a grievance and my eyes are welded shut
Something orange flashes, I'm halfway out my chair
It's another lousy potion; leave my dignity right there

[Pre-Chorus]
Everybody's teleporting
I'm commuting through the mud
Got a kingdom full of monsters
And a pocket full of crud

[Chorus]
Jah, Ith, Ber, in that order
Three-socket body armor, that's the spell
Ith is sitting pretty in the corner
Jah and Ber can send a postcard back from hell
Ten hours straight in Lower Kurast
Same two huts, same desperate little prayer
I could cross the world inside a heartbeat
If the means to cross it ever would appear

[Verse 2]
Somebody says, "Found mine while I was looking for a key"
Somebody posts a double drop; how nice for somebody
I congratulate the lucky guy with murder in my grin
Then click another hollow chest and crawl back in again
Got flawless gems for flooring, got enough gold for a throne
Got a stash of almost something and an Ith that lives alone
Superchests, you wooden liars, cough your little treasures out
I'm bargaining with furniture; that's what tonight's about

[Chorus]
Jah, Ith, Ber, in that order
Three-socket body armor, that's the spell
Ith is sitting pretty in the corner
Jah and Ber can send a postcard back from hell
Ten hours straight in Lower Kurast
Same two huts, same desperate little prayer
I could cross the world inside a heartbeat
If the means to cross it ever would appear

[Bridge]
The sun comes up without permission
My mercenary watches me
I've made a second occupation
Out of wanting to be free
One last run becomes another
Then I let the silence stay
Shut the chest and stretch my fingers
Let the jungle keep today

[Final Chorus]
Jah, Ith, Ber, I still remember
Three sockets waiting patiently at home
But I won't feed the morning to the timber
Those empty little boxes don't get everything I own
Ten hours gone in Lower Kurast
I stand up with nothing new to wear
Enigma, you can wait until tomorrow
Tonight I'm walking out for air

lyrics.text:
[Spoken Intro]
Dis is Tony C? From da shoes?

[Verse 1]
You were building casseroles in the sand
I brought a fork, you brought a marching band
You buttered me up just to toast me brown
Then crossed my name off the lost and found
You drew me out of your coloring book
I lost my place when the radiator shook
There was something important I meant to accuse
But the words fell out through a hole in my shoes

[Chorus]
You turned me to scones
And the scones don't need you
My beautiful reducer
My beautiful Medusa
I'm losing the remote, don't even care
Somebody left all the snakes downstairs
You turned me to scones
Now the kettle's coming home

[Verse 2]
When first I met you, you were wearing a raincoat
I called it a halo; that's what my brain wrote
Now I realize, underneath that sleeve
You had seventeen receipts and a wheel of cheese
You said forever, I heard four leather chairs
I carried them up seventeen flights of stairs
You gave me a look that could petrify bread
I thanked the conductor and climbed into bed

[Chorus]
You turned me to scones
And the scones don't need you
My beautiful reducer
My beautiful Medusa
I'm losing the remote, don't even care
Somebody left all the snakes downstairs
You turned me to scones
Now the kettle's coming home

[Bridge]
Surprised every morning my socks aren't dead
Got a mouth full of coupons, a cabbage for a head
Checked the mirror, both eyes were plaid
That's the finest reflection I've almost had
The bottle said shampoo, the sandwich said leave
I wiped all my prophecies off on my sleeve
There's a proper last verse somewhere under this chair
But a pigeon has eaten it, fair is fair

[Final Chorus]
You turned me to scones
But I finally forgive you
My beautiful umbrella
No, my beautiful Medusa
Lost every word, found you sitting there
With a little crooked smile and a snake in your hair
I'll put down the page, let the kitchen light glow
My beautiful Medusa, that's the one I know

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
Dropped on the map with a beautiful plan
Enough ammunition to bury a sun
First little bastard comes over the sand
My whole army fires and nothing gets done
There's a mark on his head like a practical joke
He's picking his teeth in my artillery smoke
Your boys could erase him by turning around
But you're chasing a bonus halfway across town

[Pre-Chorus]
I put one ping where the trouble begins
Then three where the trouble walks in
You say you're coming, I swallow my pride
There's something enormous approaching the side

[Chorus]
That's the one I cannot kill
Walking through the fire, standing still
I've got thunder in my hands
But the answer's in your hands
Get here before the walls give way
I'll take the beast that shrugs your shots away
Two commanders, one terrible hill
And the one I cannot kill

[Verse 2]
Siege tanks barking till the barrels glow red
Marines disappear where the ramp used to be
That hybrid keeps stepping across all my dead
Like Amon arranged this especially for me
You've got your own monster chewing your gate
I can hurt yours, but I'm arriving late
We pass in the middle with opposite debts
And a list of apologies neither forgets

[Pre-Chorus]
My finest upgrade is begging for aid
Your finest defense is the promise I made
The clock keeps its teeth in the neck of the run
We don't get to win this by being just one

[Chorus]
That's the one I cannot kill
Walking through the fire, standing still
I've got thunder in my hands
But the answer's in your hands
Get here before the walls give way
I'll take the beast that shrugs your shots away
Two commanders, one terrible hill
And the one I cannot kill

[Bridge]
Wait—there you are through the burning machinery
One crooked volley and down goes my misery
I laugh like a fool with a mouth full of dust
Then turn toward yours because somebody must

[Final Chorus]
That's the one I couldn't kill
Now it's broken underneath the hill
Keep your shoulder next to mine
Let the wreckage mark the line
Last wave falling, both of us stay
Each takes the nightmare the other can't slay
Two commanders breathing until
There isn't one we cannot kill

songs.title: An Old Friend in the Emergency Light

lyrics.text:
[Verse 1]
Third watch, coffee cold beside the navigation screen
Hyperion shakes like something waking from a dream
I take the narrow passage where the coolant pipes complain
One hand finds the railing, one remembers how to aim
Then every little warning lamp goes swimming out of sight
And something taller than a man unfolds inside the night
I draw before I breathe; the barrel trembles in the gloom
A voice comes through the darkness like a seal upon a tomb

[Ominous, low and deliberate]
James Raynor I bring tidings of doom

[Verse 2]
Zeratul, you bastard, there's a doorway down the hall
Could've used the intercom, could've given me a call
A broken little chuckle gets no answer from his eyes
There's dust upon his armor from beneath forgotten skies
I lower down the pistol; he inclines his weary head
Two soldiers stand together with an army of their dead

[Chorus]
Come into the emergency light
Let me see the friend inside the fright
You crossed the stars to find me here
Pull up the truth; I'll pull up a chair
If dawn's gone missing, we'll search all night
Old friend, come into the light

[Verse 3]
He speaks of doors beneath the worlds, of futures burning black
Of something waiting past the point where prayers can bring us back
I want a name, a target, something engines can outrun
He watches my reflection on the cold steel of my gun
Says the road ahead will ask what hatred cannot give
And the woman in my nightmares may be why the living live
I taste an old betrayal; I hear an older plea
The ship keeps breathing softly while he leaves that thought with me

[Bridge]
For once I have no wisecrack
For once he looks his age
His hand extends a crystal
Mine opens like a cage
No promises of victory
No clean and easy end
Just something worth protecting
And the warning of a friend

[Final Chorus]
Stay beneath the emergency light
We've both been ghosts enough tonight
I'll carry what you came to share
Even when your shadow isn't there
Whatever waits beyond our sight
You found a friend aboard this flight

[Closing, quietly sung]
His footsteps vanish; mine resume
I turn toward the bridge with room for doom
And room for hope beside it

lyrics.text:
[Intro]
Lut Gholein, keep my stool warm.
I've found a cheaper place to drink.
The door has teeth. That's fucking charming.
I'll finish this before you blink.

[Verse 1]
Geglash swaggered down the stair,
Desert sand still in his hair.
Told a guard, I've fought much bigger—
Then the bastard pulled the trigger.
Not a gun: a great big cleaver.
Lost an arm, became a leaver.
Crawled three rooms to find a bandage,
Bled out bargaining for damage.
Back outside, two hands again.
Nothing earned except the pain.

[Chorus]
Heads, I'm dead; tails, I'm dreaming.
Same damn doorway, same damn screaming.
Fear and Hunger, pour my grave;
All that glory, no fucking save.
I was nearly somebody down below.
Now I'm nobody, here we go.
Turn the handle, curse the floor—
Geglash dies and wants one more.

[Verse 2]
Found some bread and ate it standing,
Called that tactical understanding.
Rusty nail went through my boot;
Kept the boot and lost the foot.
Met a crow with shoulders wider
Than the tavern's apple cider.
Raised my sword, began my story;
Lost my head before the glory.
Somewhere Warriv felt a shiver.
Someone had to mind my liver.

[Chorus]
Heads, I'm dead; tails, I'm dreaming.
Same damn doorway, same damn screaming.
Fear and Hunger, pour my grave;
All that glory, no fucking save.
I had food and a halfway decent blade.
Now they're ghosts of a run I made.
Turn the handle, curse the floor—
Geglash dies and wants one more.

[Bridge]
There was a bed. There was a silence.
I mistook the peace for kindness.
Flipped a coin with filthy fingers:
Lost the toss; the laughter lingers.
Then a book! Salvation, surely!
Should have read the title thoroughly.
Empty shelves and empty pockets.
Fuck your gods and cursed door sockets.

[Final Verse]
No more charging. Watch the hinges.
Count the torches. Stop the binges.
Take the food and leave the boasting;
All my former selves are roasting.
Found the book that keeps tomorrow,
Held it like a child of sorrow.
Saved at last, then laughed so hard
I backed straight into another guard.

[Final Chorus]
Heads, I'm dead; tails, I'm dreaming.
Same damn doorway, same damn screaming.
Fear and Hunger, you can keep
Every corpse beneath that heap.
Load the page—the torch still glows.
There's my sword, and there's my toes.
Keep my stool. I've learned to behave.
This dead bastard finally has a save.

lyrics.text:
[Intro — whistled pickup, then spoken]
Tickets out, beautiful trouble.
That's my train.

[Verse 1]
Got a midnight blue jacket and a pocket full of steam,
Brass buttons shining like a pinball dream.
My engine's got shoulders, my carriage got class,
You can watch your bad luck disappearing through the glass.
There's a chandelier swinging in the dining car,
And a lady selling peaches from a silver guitar.
I punch one moon in your little paper square:
Take whichever seat you like, we're going somewhere.

[Pre-Chorus]
Hear those big wheels picking up the slack,
Leave your busted little clock beside the track.
One sharp whistle, then the whole world leans—
I'm the conductor of this beautiful machine.

[Chorus]
Ride my midnight chrome express,
Bring your Sunday shoes and your Saturday mess.
Choo choo, honey, hear that low-down brass,
Even old tomorrow lets the big train pass.
I call the stops, you catch your breath,
Nobody's late on the chrome express.

[Verse 2]
There's a heavyweight boxer teaching kittens to dance,
An undertaker wearing very optimistic pants.
The mayor bought a ticket just to loosen his tie,
Now he's washing all the windows as the towns go by.
I tip my hat when the mountain bows,
Got a snow-white whistle waking up the cows.
The engineer grins, says, "Boss, looking fine."
I say, "Keep your eyes ahead; the hat is mine."

[Chorus]
Ride my midnight chrome express,
Bring your Sunday shoes and your Saturday mess.
Choo choo, honey, hear that low-down brass,
Even old tomorrow lets the big train pass.
I call the stops, you catch your breath,
Nobody's late on the chrome express.

[Bridge — half-time, warmly sung]
Back in the last car, somebody cries,
Watching their old street shrink to a light.
I sit beside them, let the wheels explain:
You can carry a sorrow on a beautiful train.
Then dawn puts gold on the window frame.
They straighten my collar and ask my name.

[Final Chorus]
Tony runs the midnight chrome express,
With a crooked little smile and a velvet vest.
Choo choo, honey, hear that low-down brass,
See the morning open as the big train passes.
I call the stop, you catch your breath—
Welcome home from the chrome express.

[Coda — slowing into the station]
Step down easy. Mind that seam.
My, what a beautiful machine.
